## Textarea (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/forms/textarea)

Accessible multiline text input supporting field-sizing auto-resize, rows configuration, and automatic Field wiring.

`Textarea` provides multiline text input for customer remarks, delivery instructions, procurement notes, and descriptions. Built on standard HTML5 textarea ergonomics, it supports automatic vertical resizing via CSS `field-sizing: content` while integrating directly with `<Field>` for validation and error reporting.

<ComponentPreview name="forms/textarea/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Textarea } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

- **Use Textarea** for multiline text entries such as shipping instructions, invoice notes, or bug reports.
- **Use Input** for single-line values such as customer names, email addresses, or phone numbers.
- **Use RichTextEditor** when formatted text (bold, lists, links, headers) or document authoring is required.

## Examples

### Basic usage

Specify the initial visible height using the `rows` prop:

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Dispatch instructions</FieldLabel>
  <Textarea rows={4} placeholder="Gate delivery instructions, bay access codes..." />
  <FieldDescription>Max 500 characters.</FieldDescription>
</Field>
```

### Auto-resize

Enable `autoResize` to allow the textarea to grow vertically as the operator types:

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Internal procurement note</FieldLabel>
  <Textarea
    autoResize
    rows={2}
    placeholder="Describe vendor negotiation terms..."
  />
  <FieldDescription>Grows smoothly with content using CSS field-sizing.</FieldDescription>
</Field>
```

Browsers without native `field-sizing: content` support gracefully fall back to standard vertical drag-resizing.

### Validation state

When used inside `<Field>`, validation errors trigger error rings and ARIA live announcements:

```tsx
<Field name="justification" required>
  <FieldLabel required>Order cancellation reason</FieldLabel>
  <Textarea required minLength={10} />
  <FieldError match="valueMissing">Please state a reason for cancelling this order.</FieldError>
  <FieldError match="tooShort">Please provide at least 10 characters of explanation.</FieldError>
</Field>
```

## Accessibility

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  rows={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus to the textarea or away to the subsequent interactive control.' },
    { key: 'Enter', action: 'Inserts a new line character within the text content.' },
  ]}
/>

### Screen readers and ARIA

- **Automatic labelling**: When wrapped inside `<Field>`, the `<FieldLabel>` is programmatically coupled via `htmlFor`/`id`.
- **Validation binding**: Error and helper descriptions connect via `aria-describedby` and set `aria-invalid="true"` when invalid.

## Guidelines

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Provide an initial `rows` value (typically 3 to 5) that accommodates expected content without overwhelming the screen.
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never use a `Textarea` for single-line values like titles, email addresses, or tax numbers; use `Input` instead.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Use `autoResize` for compact comment forms to keep the initial footprint minimal.
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never hide the scrollbar or restrict manual resizing when `autoResize` is disabled.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Textarea']} />

## Related

- [Input](/ui/docs/components/forms/input) — Single-line text input field.
- [Field and Form](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) — Accessible form layout and error handling container.
- [RichTextEditor](/ui/docs/components/forms/rich-text-editor) — Formatted document and markup editor.

## App Rail (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/layout/app-rail)

Compact module navigation rail with active states, accessible tooltips, and badges for enterprise multi-app suites.

<ComponentPreview name="layout/app-rail/basic" align="start" className="p-4 sm:p-4" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  AppRail,
  AppRailItem,
  AppRailHeader,
  AppRailFooter,
  AppRailSeparator,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `AppRail` when building two-tier enterprise navigation suites:

- **Multi-module ERP platforms**: Fast switching between Procurement, Inventory, Finance, and HRMS.
- **Persistent workspace switcher**: Keeping global shortcuts reachable regardless of current deep view.
- **High-density desktop apps**: Minimising horizontal space loss while retaining full-screen module switching.

**Do not use AppRail for:**
- Single-purpose applications with fewer than 5 total pages — use a standard [Sidebar](/ui/docs/components/layout/sidebar).
- Page-level content tabs — use [Tabs](/ui/docs/components/navigation/tabs).
- Mobile screens — `AppRail` hides automatically below the `md` breakpoint, where `Sidebar` assumes mobile navigation duties.

## Examples

### Two-tier navigation shell

Composing `AppRail` alongside `Sidebar` inside `SidebarProvider`:

```tsx
import Link from 'next/link';
import {
  SidebarProvider,
  AppRail,
  AppRailHeader,
  AppRailItem,
  AppRailFooter,
  Sidebar,
  SidebarInset,
} from '@innostes/ui';
import { Package, ShoppingCart, Landmark, Users } from 'lucide-react';

export function ErpShell({ children }) {
  return (
    <SidebarProvider>
      <AppRail label="ERP modules">
        <AppRailHeader>
          <div className="size-8 rounded bg-primary font-bold text-primary-foreground flex items-center justify-center">
            N
          </div>
        </AppRailHeader>

        <AppRailItem
          icon={<ShoppingCart />}
          label="Procurement"
          isActive
          render={<Link href="/procurement" />}
        />
        <AppRailItem
          icon={<Package />}
          label="Inventory"
          badge={12}
          render={<Link href="/inventory" />}
        />
        <AppRailItem
          icon={<Landmark />}
          label="Finance & GST"
          render={<Link href="/finance" />}
        />

        <AppRailFooter>
          <AppRailItem
            icon={<Users />}
            label="Employees"
            render={<Link href="/hrms" />}
          />
        </AppRailFooter>
      </AppRail>

      <Sidebar>
        {/* Secondary navigation for Procurement */}
      </Sidebar>

      <SidebarInset>
        {children}
      </SidebarInset>
    </SidebarProvider>
  );
}
```

### With badges and tooltips

Each `AppRailItem` automatically renders an accessible tooltip when hovered or focused, displaying the item's label and notification badge count:

```tsx
<AppRailItem
  icon={<Bell />}
  label="Approvals"
  badge={3}
  render={<Link href="/approvals" />}
/>
```

## Accessibility

`AppRail` renders semantic HTML5 navigation landmarks.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus sequentially between interactive module items.' },
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Activates the focused module link or trigger.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The container renders as `<nav aria-label="Apps">` (customisable via the `label` prop).
- Active items receive `aria-current="page"`.
- If an item includes a numerical badge, the count is included in accessible label computations for screen readers.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Always supply a clear text label for each AppRailItem so tooltips and screen reader names are complete.',
    code: `<AppRailItem icon={<Box />} label="Inventory" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not omit the label prop on icon-only rail items.',
    code: `<AppRailItem icon={<Box />} />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use the render prop with your framework router Link (e.g. Next.js Link) for fast client-side transitions.',
    code: `<AppRailItem render={<Link href="/finance" />} label="Finance" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not nest native anchor tags inside interactive button triggers.',
    code: `<AppRailItem><a href="/finance">Finance</a></AppRailItem>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable
  components={[
    'AppRail',
    'AppRailItem',
    'AppRailHeader',
    'AppRailFooter',
    'AppRailSeparator',
  ]}
/>

## Related

- [Sidebar](/ui/docs/components/layout/sidebar) — Application sidebar supporting hierarchical trees, groups, and mobile drawers.
- [TopBar](/ui/docs/components/layout/top-bar) — Top application navigation bar.
- [Tooltip](/ui/docs/components/overlays/tooltip) — Floating hint used internally by AppRailItem.

## Form Layout (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/layout/form-layout)

Container-query powered grids (FormGrid), titled sections (FormSection), and persistent action bars (FormActions).

<ComponentPreview name="layout/form-layout/basic" align="start" />

## Import

```tsx
import { FormGrid, FormSection, FormActions } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `FormLayout` primitives to establish clean, predictable field spacing across diverse layout environments:

- **Full-page forms**: Vendor onboarding, purchase order creation, or product catalogue entries.
- **Side drawer forms**: Edit forms inside [Sheet](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet).
- **Modal forms**: Quick entry dialogues inside [Dialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dialog).

Because `FormGrid` uses CSS **container queries** rather than viewport media queries, the grid automatically adapts to the actual width of its container (page, drawer, or modal) without needing custom responsive breakpoint classes.

## Examples

### Responsive FormGrid with column spans

Organise form fields into 1, 2, 3, or 4 adaptive columns:

```tsx
<FormGrid columns={2}>
  <Field name="vendorName">
    <FieldLabel>Vendor legal name</FieldLabel>
    <Input defaultValue="Bengaluru Spices Pvt Ltd" />
  </Field>
  <Field name="gstin">
    <FieldLabel>GSTIN</FieldLabel>
    <Input defaultValue="29ABCDE1234F1Z5" />
  </Field>
  <Field name="address" className="col-span-full">
    <FieldLabel>Registered warehouse address</FieldLabel>
    <Textarea defaultValue="Plot 42, Electronic City Phase 1, Hosur Road, Bengaluru 560100" />
  </Field>
</FormGrid>
```

### FormSection: stacked versus aside

Use `layout="stacked"` (default) for dialogs and standard pages, or `layout="aside"` for settings screens where section titles sit on the left:

```tsx
<FormSection
  title="Statutory tax profiles"
  description="Manage registered GSTIN identifiers and TDS rates."
  layout="aside"
>
  <FormGrid columns={2}>
    <Field name="pan">
      <FieldLabel>Company PAN</FieldLabel>
      <Input defaultValue="ABCDE1234F" />
    </Field>
    <Field name="tan">
      <FieldLabel>Tax deduction account number (TAN)</FieldLabel>
      <Input defaultValue="BLRA01234E" />
    </Field>
  </FormGrid>
</FormSection>
```

### FormActions with sticky positioning

`FormActions` aligns save and cancel buttons. Use `align="between"` to place the back/cancel button on the left and the primary submit button on the right:

```tsx
<FormActions align="between" sticky>
  <Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
  <div className="flex gap-2">
    <Button variant="secondary">Save as draft</Button>
    <Button type="submit">Submit for approval</Button>
  </div>
</FormActions>
```

## Accessibility

`FormLayout` primitives enforce structured visual hierarchy and standard DOM order.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Navigates sequentially through all input controls according to DOM order.' },
    { key: 'Enter', action: 'Submits the form when focused inside a standard text input field.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- `FormSection` wraps fields in semantic `<section>` landmarks labelled by the section title.
- `FormGrid` preserves natural reading and focus order, avoiding confusing CSS grid reordering.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use className="col-span-full" on textareas or long addresses that require full container width.',
    code: `<Field className="col-span-full"><Textarea name="notes" /></Field>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not squeeze multi-line notes or long street addresses into narrow half-width columns.',
    code: `<Field><Textarea name="notes" /></Field>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use sticky on FormActions when forms exceed the single screen viewport height.',
    code: `<FormActions sticky><Button type="submit">Save</Button></FormActions>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not leave primary submit buttons hidden far below scroll boundaries without indication.',
    code: `<div className="mt-80"><Button>Submit</Button></div>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['FormGrid', 'FormSection', 'FormActions']} />

## Related

- [Field](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) — Accessible form field container with label, description, and error message.
- [Input](/ui/docs/components/forms/input) — Basic text input primitive.
- [PageHeader](/ui/docs/components/layout/page-header) — Page header for high-level action buttons.

## Layout (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/layout/index)

Scaffolding primitives for responsive ERP application shells, navigation bars, and data panes.

import { CategoryGrid } from '@/components/docs/category-grid';

# Layout

Layout components define the structural scaffold for Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd's ERP applications. They orchestrate viewports, responsive sidebars, persistent headers, and split-pane inspection canvases to support complex enterprise workflows.

## Components

<CategoryGrid category="components/layout" />

## App shell composition

The application shell unites five core primitives: `SkipLink`, `AppRail`, `Sidebar`, `TopBar`, and `PageHeader`. Together, they provide a reliable, keyboard-navigable enterprise structure with fluid mobile adaptations.

### Full layout example

Here is how the components assemble into a complete Next.js root layout:

```tsx
// app/(erp)/layout.tsx
import Link from 'next/link';
import {
  SidebarProvider,
  Sidebar,
  SidebarHeader,
  SidebarContent,
  SidebarGroup,
  SidebarGroupLabel,
  SidebarMenu,
  SidebarMenuItem,
  SidebarMenuButton,
  SidebarTrigger,
  SidebarInset,
  AppRail,
  AppRailHeader,
  AppRailItem,
  TopBar,
  TopBarStart,
  TopBarCenter,
  TopBarEnd,
  SkipLink,
} from '@innostes/ui';
import { ShoppingCart, Package, Users, Search } from 'lucide-react';

export default function ErpAppLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <>
      <SkipLink targetId="main-content">Skip to main content</SkipLink>
      <SidebarProvider>
        {/* Tier 1: Global module switcher (hidden on small viewports) */}
        <AppRail label="ERP modules">
          <AppRailHeader>
            <div className="size-8 rounded bg-primary font-bold text-primary-foreground flex items-center justify-center">
              N
            </div>
          </AppRailHeader>
          <AppRailItem
            icon={<ShoppingCart />}
            label="Purchases"
            isActive
            render={<Link href="/purchases" />}
          />
          <AppRailItem
            icon={<Package />}
            label="Inventory"
            render={<Link href="/inventory" />}
          />
        </AppRail>

        {/* Tier 2: Module-specific navigation tree */}
        <Sidebar>
          <SidebarHeader>
            <div className="font-semibold text-sm px-2 py-3">Procurement Hub</div>
          </SidebarHeader>
          <SidebarContent>
            <SidebarGroup>
              <SidebarGroupLabel>Purchasing</SidebarGroupLabel>
              <SidebarMenu>
                <SidebarMenuItem>
                  <SidebarMenuButton render={<Link href="/purchases/orders" />}>
                    Purchase orders
                  </SidebarMenuButton>
                </SidebarMenuItem>
                <SidebarMenuItem>
                  <SidebarMenuButton render={<Link href="/purchases/vendors" />}>
                    Vendor directory
                  </SidebarMenuButton>
                </SidebarMenuItem>
              </SidebarMenu>
            </SidebarGroup>
          </SidebarContent>
        </Sidebar>

        {/* Content canvas */}
        <SidebarInset>
          <TopBar sticky blur>
            <TopBarStart>
              <SidebarTrigger />
            </TopBarStart>
            <TopBarCenter>
              <div className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground">
                <Search className="size-4" />
                <span>Search records... (⌘K)</span>
              </div>
            </TopBarCenter>
            <TopBarEnd>
              <div className="text-sm font-medium">Priya Sharma</div>
            </TopBarEnd>
          </TopBar>

          <main id="main-content" className="flex-1 p-6">
            {children}
          </main>
        </SidebarInset>
      </SidebarProvider>
    </>
  );
}
```

### CSS variables and sizing tokens

The app shell exposes CSS custom properties to govern structural widths and heights. You can override them globally in your Tailwind CSS theme or inline on `SidebarProvider`:

| Token | Default | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `--sidebar-width` | `16rem` (`256px`) | Width of the desktop sidebar when expanded. |
| `--sidebar-width-icon` | `3.5rem` (`56px`) | Width of the desktop sidebar when collapsed to icon rail. |
| `--sidebar-width-mobile` | `18rem` (`288px`) | Width of the slide-over drawer on mobile devices. |
| `--app-rail-width` | `4.5rem` (`72px`) | Width of the optional primary module rail. |
| `--top-bar-height` | `4rem` (`64px`) | Height of the persistent top application header. |

### Mobile behaviour and responsive transitions

1. **Breakpoints**: Below `768px` (`md`), `AppRail` hides automatically, and `Sidebar` transforms from a fixed column into an off-canvas slide-over drawer.
2. **Backdrop overlay**: When opened via `SidebarTrigger`, a backdrop prevents background interaction and dims page content.
3. **Automatic dismissal**: Navigating to any route by clicking a `SidebarMenuButton` closes the mobile drawer immediately, keeping user flows uninterrupted.
4. **Escape key & inert**: While the mobile drawer is open, background DOM elements are marked `inert`, and pressing `Escape` dismisses the drawer, returning keyboard focus to the trigger.

### Skip link implementation

Accessibility standards require that keyboard and screen reader operators can bypass repetitive top navigation bars and jump straight to the primary work area:

- Place `<SkipLink targetId="main-content">Skip to main content</SkipLink>` at the very top of your root layout.
- Ensure the primary `<main>` element has matching `id="main-content"`.
- When focused via `Tab`, the skip link transitions smoothly into view from off-screen and receives focus.

### Router integration via render prop

All navigation links (`SidebarMenuButton`, `SidebarMenuSubButton`, `AppRailItem`, `BreadcrumbLink`) provide a `render` prop. Pass your framework's router link component (e.g. Next.js `Link`) directly:

```tsx
<SidebarMenuButton
  render={<Link href="/invoices" />}
  isActive={pathname.startsWith('/invoices')}
>
  Invoices
</SidebarMenuButton>
```

This prevents hard browser page refreshes, guarantees fast client-side transitions, and preserves accessibility attributes without invalid HTML DOM nesting.

---

## Page Header (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/layout/page-header)

Standardized page header bringing together breadcrumb, h1 title, status badges, and primary actions.

<ComponentPreview name="layout/page-header/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { PageHeader } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `PageHeader` at the top of every internal administrative view:

- **Record detail pages**: Purchase order `PO-2026-081`, Customer account `Acme Corp`, or Tax invoice `INV-2026-081`.
- **List and catalogue dashboards**: Warehouses, inventory catalogues, or statutory reports.
- **Settings subpages**: Security preferences, GST profiles, or team roles.

**Do not use PageHeader for:**
- Global application-level headers (with tenant switcher, global search, and user avatar) — use [TopBar](/ui/docs/components/layout/top-bar).
- In-page card section titles — use [Card](/ui/docs/components/data-display/card) or standard heading elements.
- Dialog and modal window titles — use `DialogHeader` and `DialogTitle`.

## Examples

### Basic usage with breadcrumb and actions

Render breadcrumbs, page title, description, and primary action buttons:

```tsx
<PageHeader
  breadcrumb={
    <Breadcrumb>
      <BreadcrumbList>
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink href="/purchases">Purchases</BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbPage>PO-2026-081</BreadcrumbPage>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
      </BreadcrumbList>
    </Breadcrumb>
  }
  title="Purchase order PO-2026-081"
  description="Bengaluru Spices Pvt Ltd · Created on 24 Oct 2026 by Priya Sharma"
  actions={
    <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
      <Button variant="outline">Download PDF</Button>
      <Button>Approve order</Button>
    </div>
  }
/>
```

### With status badge in title

Pass React nodes to `title` to pair headings with live status chips:

```tsx
<PageHeader
  title={
    <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
      <span>Tax invoice INV-2026-081</span>
      <Badge variant="success">E-Way Bill Generated</Badge>
    </div>
  }
  description="GST Tax Invoice · Total value ₹89,400"
  actions={<Button variant="destructive">Void invoice</Button>}
/>
```

## Accessibility

`PageHeader` provides unambiguous document heading landmarks.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus sequentially between breadcrumb links and header action buttons.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The container renders as a semantic `<header>` landmark.
- The `title` prop renders the unique primary `<h1>` heading for the page.
- Action buttons remain in logical DOM order so screen reader users encounter contextual breadcrumbs, title, description, and actions in sequence.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Place the primary affirmative call-to-action last in the actions container.',
    code: `<PageHeader actions={<><Button variant="outline">Export</Button><Button>New order</Button></>} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not render multiple PageHeader components on the same view.',
    code: `<><PageHeader title="One" /><PageHeader title="Two" /></>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Keep the description prop concise, focusing on key entity context or status metadata.',
    code: `<PageHeader description="Karnataka division · Validated GSTIN" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not dump multi-paragraph instructional documentation into the description slot.',
    code: `<PageHeader description="Here is a very long paragraph that explains the complete 40-step statutory history..." />`,
  }}
/>

- [Button](/ui/docs/components/actions/button) — Action button component used for page actions.

## Scroll Area (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/layout/scroll-area)

Native momentum scrolling, keyboard accessibility, and styled auto-hiding scrollbars across all operating systems.

<ComponentPreview name="layout/scroll-area/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { ScrollArea } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `ScrollArea` when a region must scroll independently without relying on divergent OS-native scrollbar styling:

- **Audit trails and activity logs**: Displaying long chronological timelines in sidebars or cards.
- **Data drawers and sheets**: Ensuring vertical scrolling inside `SheetBody` or dialog viewports.
- **Wide horizontal tables or code blocks**: Providing clean horizontal scroll tracking without bulky browser bars.

**Do not use ScrollArea for:**
- The primary window body scroll — allow the browser window to scroll naturally.
- Small fixed-size cards where content easily fits without truncation.
- Infinite lists requiring virtual DOM rendering — use a virtualised data grid.

## Examples

### Vertical scrollable audit feed

Giving the container a bounded height or max-height:

```tsx
<ScrollArea className="h-72 rounded-md border p-4">
  <div className="space-y-4">
    <h4 className="text-sm font-semibold">ERP audit log (PO-2026-081)</h4>
    {auditLogs.map((log) => (
      <div key={log.id} className="text-sm border-b pb-2">
        <p className="font-medium text-foreground">{log.action}</p>
        <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">{log.actor} · {log.timestamp}</p>
      </div>
    ))}
  </div>
</ScrollArea>
```

### Horizontal scrolling for wide datasets

Set `scrollbars="horizontal"` or `scrollbars="both"` when hosting wide data grids or timeline bars:

```tsx
<ScrollArea scrollbars="horizontal" className="w-full rounded-md border">
  <div className="flex w-max gap-4 p-4">
    {warehouses.map((wh) => (
      <Card key={wh.id} className="w-64 shrink-0">
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle>{wh.name}</CardTitle>
          <CardDescription>{wh.location}</CardDescription>
        </CardHeader>
      </Card>
    ))}
  </div>
</ScrollArea>
```

## Accessibility

`ScrollArea` is built on Base UI ScrollArea primitives (`@base-ui/react/scroll-area`).

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'PageDown / DownArrow', action: 'Scrolls the viewport content downwards when the scroll area is focused.' },
    { key: 'PageUp / UpArrow', action: 'Scrolls the viewport content upwards when the scroll area is focused.' },
    { key: 'Home / End', action: 'Jumps directly to the very start or end of the scrollable region.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The scroll area maintains standard native scrolling mechanics, ensuring assistive technologies can navigate child nodes sequentially.
- Scrollbar thumbs hide visually when inactive but expand upon pointer hover to offer a clear drag target.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Provide an explicit height or maxHeight class on ScrollArea so the scroll boundaries are established.',
    code: `<ScrollArea className="h-64">{items}</ScrollArea>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not render ScrollArea without height constraints, allowing it to expand infinitely without scrolling.',
    code: `<ScrollArea>{infiniteItems}</ScrollArea>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use viewportClassName when inner padding is needed, keeping scrollbars pinned to the outer edges.',
    code: `<ScrollArea viewportClassName="p-4">{content}</ScrollArea>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not place large padding directly on the outer container if it offsets the scrollbar track awkwardly.',
    code: `<ScrollArea className="p-8">{content}</ScrollArea>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['ScrollArea']} baseUi="scroll-area" />

## Related

- [Sheet](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet) — Slide-over drawer component utilising scrollable body areas.
- [DataTable](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table) — Interactive table component with horizontal overflow handling.
- [Card](/ui/docs/components/data-display/card) — Card container frequently hosting scrollable lists.

## Separator (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/layout/separator)

Horizontal or vertical divider with semantic separator semantics and RTL logical layout support.

<ComponentPreview name="layout/separator/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Separator } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Separator` to establish clear visual boundaries between distinct functional areas:

- **Form and section dividers**: Breaking up long configuration panels into readable chunks.
- **Toolbar dividers**: Separating button groups (e.g. text formatting vs clipboard actions).
- **Detail card segments**: Separating customer metadata from order financial totals.

**Do not use Separator for:**
- Purely decorative lines with no semantic division — use CSS borders.
- Spacing between consecutive table rows — use table row borders.
- Top-level page borders — rely on layout containers like `PageHeader` and `TopBar`.

## Examples

### Horizontal card divider

Separating enterprise entity headers from summary line items:

```tsx
<div className="rounded-lg border p-6">
  <div className="space-y-1">
    <h4 className="text-sm font-semibold">Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd</h4>
    <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Bengaluru Central Hub · GSTIN 29ABCDE1234F1Z5</p>
  </div>
  <Separator className="my-4" />
  <div className="flex justify-between text-sm">
    <span>Active purchase orders</span>
    <span className="font-semibold">₹4,28,900</span>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Vertical divider inside button toolbars

Set `orientation="vertical"` to separate interactive clusters:

```tsx
<div className="flex h-9 items-center gap-2 rounded-md border p-1">
  <Button size="sm" variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="Bold"><BoldIcon /></Button>
  <Button size="sm" variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="Italic"><ItalicIcon /></Button>
  <Separator orientation="vertical" className="h-4" />
  <Button size="sm" variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="Align left"><AlignLeftIcon /></Button>
  <Button size="sm" variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="Align center"><AlignCenterIcon /></Button>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

`Separator` is built on Base UI Separator primitives (`@base-ui/react/separator`).

### Keyboard navigation

Separators are non-focusable elements skipped by keyboard tab loops.

### ARIA attributes

- Renders with `role="separator"`.
- Sets `aria-orientation="horizontal"` (default) or `aria-orientation="vertical"`.
- When used purely for cosmetic decoration without structural meaning, pass `decorative={true}` to render `role="none"` and hide it from screen readers.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use Separator to delineate distinct semantic clusters of actions or form sections.',
    code: `<Separator className="my-6" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not insert dozens of separators where whitespace alone provides sufficient visual breathing room.',
    code: `<><Field /><Separator /><Field /><Separator /><Field /></>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Set orientation="vertical" when placing separators between inline items in a horizontal row.',
    code: `<div className="flex items-center"><Item /><Separator orientation="vertical" className="h-4" /><Item /></div>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not rely on standard unstyled horizontal separators inside flex row layouts.',
    code: `<div className="flex"><Item /><Separator /><Item /></div>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Separator']} baseUi="separator" />

## Related

- [FormLayout](/ui/docs/components/layout/form-layout) — Structured form container using section separators.
- [Card](/ui/docs/components/data-display/card) — Card container frequently segmented by separators.
- [TopBar](/ui/docs/components/layout/top-bar) — Header bar featuring inline separators.

## Sidebar (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/layout/sidebar)

Collapses to icons on desktop, slides in on mobile, with groups, badges, tooltips, nested submenus, and keyboard shortcut (⌘B).

<ComponentPreview name="layout/sidebar/basic" align="start" className="p-4 sm:p-4" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  SidebarProvider,
  Sidebar,
  SidebarHeader,
  SidebarContent,
  SidebarFooter,
  SidebarSeparator,
  SidebarGroup,
  SidebarGroupLabel,
  SidebarGroupAction,
  SidebarMenu,
  SidebarMenuItem,
  SidebarMenuButton,
  SidebarMenuAction,
  SidebarMenuBadge,
  SidebarMenuSub,
  SidebarMenuSubItem,
  SidebarMenuSubButton,
  SidebarTrigger,
  SidebarRail,
  SidebarInset,
  useSidebar,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Sidebar` as the primary navigation backbone of administrative and enterprise applications:

- **ERP application shell**: Multi-level navigation across Procurement, Warehousing, Invoicing, and Master Data.
- **Hierarchical menu structures**: Submenus grouping purchase orders, vendor master, and goods received notes.
- **Responsive administrative layouts**: Desktop sidebars that cleanly switch to mobile slide-over drawers below 768px.

**Do not use Sidebar for:**
- Isolated page-level filters — use [Sheet](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet) or inline filter cards.
- Horizontal category tabs — use [Tabs](/ui/docs/components/navigation/tabs).
- Single-page marketing websites — use standard top headers.

## Examples

### Basic application shell composition

Compose `SidebarProvider`, `Sidebar`, `TopBar`, and `SidebarInset` into an accessible layout with router integration:

```tsx
import Link from 'next/link';
import { usePathname } from 'next/navigation';
import {
  SidebarProvider,
  Sidebar,
  SidebarHeader,
  SidebarContent,
  SidebarFooter,
  SidebarGroup,
  SidebarGroupLabel,
  SidebarMenu,
  SidebarMenuItem,
  SidebarMenuButton,
  SidebarTrigger,
  SidebarInset,
  TopBar,
} from '@innostes/ui';
import { ShoppingCart, Package, FileText } from 'lucide-react';

export function AdminLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const pathname = usePathname();

  return (
    <SidebarProvider>
      <Sidebar>
        <SidebarHeader>
          <div className="flex items-center gap-2 px-2 py-3 font-semibold text-sm">
            <span className="size-6 rounded bg-primary text-primary-foreground flex items-center justify-center font-bold text-xs">
              N
            </span>
            Northwind Traders
          </div>
        </SidebarHeader>

        <SidebarContent>
          <SidebarGroup>
            <SidebarGroupLabel>Procurement</SidebarGroupLabel>
            <SidebarMenu>
              <SidebarMenuItem>
                <SidebarMenuButton
                  icon={<ShoppingCart className="size-4" />}
                  isActive={pathname.startsWith('/purchases')}
                  render={<Link href="/purchases" />}
                >
                  Purchase orders
                </SidebarMenuButton>
              </SidebarMenuItem>
              <SidebarMenuItem>
                <SidebarMenuButton
                  icon={<Package className="size-4" />}
                  isActive={pathname.startsWith('/inventory')}
                  render={<Link href="/inventory" />}
                >
                  Inventory stock
                </SidebarMenuButton>
              </SidebarMenuItem>
            </SidebarMenu>
          </SidebarGroup>
        </SidebarContent>

        <SidebarFooter>
          {/* User profile and sign-out */}
        </SidebarFooter>
      </Sidebar>

      <SidebarInset>
        <TopBar>
          <SidebarTrigger />
        </TopBar>
        <main className="p-6">
          {children}
        </main>
      </SidebarInset>
    </SidebarProvider>
  );
}
```

### Collapsible behavior and keyboard shortcuts

- **Desktop state**: Expands to standard width (default `256px`) or collapses into an icon rail (default `56px`). In icon mode, hovering or focusing any menu item displays its title via an accessible tooltip.
- **Mobile drawer**: Below `768px` (customisable via `mobileQuery`), the sidebar automatically switches to a slide-in modal drawer. Selecting any item automatically closes the drawer.
- **Global hotkey**: Pressing `Ctrl + B` or `⌘ + B` toggles the sidebar open or closed. Disable by setting `keyboardShortcut={null}`.
- **State hook**: `useSidebar()` gives any descendant component access to `{ open, setOpen, toggle, isMobile, openMobile, setOpenMobile }`.

### Custom sizing and CSS variables

Adjust sizing variables on `SidebarProvider` or via standard CSS properties:

<ComponentPreview name="layout/sidebar/width" align="start" className="p-4 sm:p-4" />

```tsx
<SidebarProvider
  style={
    {
      '--sidebar-width': '18rem',
      '--sidebar-width-icon': '4rem',
      '--sidebar-width-mobile': '20rem',
    } as React.CSSProperties
  }
>
  <Sidebar>...</Sidebar>
</SidebarProvider>
```

### Visual variants

The sidebar supports `sidebar` (classic full-height navigation), `floating` (a floating surface inset from edges), and `inset` (a sidebar wrapping the inner content with a rounded border):

<ComponentPreview name="layout/sidebar/variants" align="start" className="p-4 sm:p-4" />

### Hierarchical submenus

Use `SidebarMenuSub` for nested multi-level trees:

<ComponentPreview name="layout/sidebar/nav-submenu" align="start" className="p-4 sm:p-4" />

```tsx
<SidebarMenuItem>
  <SidebarMenuButton icon={<FileText />}>
    Invoicing & GST
  </SidebarMenuButton>
  <SidebarMenuSub>
    <SidebarMenuSubItem>
      <SidebarMenuSubButton render={<Link href="/invoices/tax" />}>
        Tax invoices
      </SidebarMenuSubButton>
    </SidebarMenuSubItem>
    <SidebarMenuSubItem>
      <SidebarMenuSubButton render={<Link href="/invoices/e-way" />}>
        E-Way bills
      </SidebarMenuSubButton>
    </SidebarMenuSubItem>
  </SidebarMenuSub>
</SidebarMenuItem>
```

### Theming the sidebar

The sidebar consumes dedicated CSS colour tokens, allowing a distinct brand surface (e.g. dark navy sidebar inside a light neutral application) without conflicting with page background tokens:

```css
@theme {
  --color-sidebar: var(--color-slate-900);
  --color-sidebar-foreground: var(--color-slate-50);
  --color-sidebar-primary: var(--color-blue-500);
  --color-sidebar-primary-foreground: var(--color-white);
  --color-sidebar-accent: var(--color-slate-800);
  --color-sidebar-accent-foreground: var(--color-slate-50);
  --color-sidebar-border: var(--color-slate-800);
  --color-sidebar-ring: var(--color-blue-500);
}
```

## Accessibility

`Sidebar` implements WAI-ARIA Landmark and Disclosure specifications.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: '⌘ + B / Ctrl + B', action: 'Toggles sidebar expansion on desktop or drawer visibility on mobile.' },
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Cycles sequentially through interactive sidebar menu links and triggers.' },
    { key: 'Escape', action: 'Dismisses the open mobile drawer panel and restores focus to the trigger button.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The sidebar root renders as `<nav aria-label="Sidebar">` (or custom `label`).
- Active items receive `aria-current="page"`.
- `SidebarTrigger` provides `aria-expanded="true | false"` and `aria-label="Toggle sidebar"`.
- When in icon-collapsed mode, items render accessible tooltips to prevent icon ambiguity.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use the render prop with framework Link components (like Next.js Link) for fast client routing.',
    code: `<SidebarMenuButton render={<Link href="/inventory" />}>Inventory</SidebarMenuButton>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not nest interactive <a> tags inside <button> elements.',
    code: `<SidebarMenuButton><a href="/inventory">Inventory</a></SidebarMenuButton>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Persist the sidebar open state in browser cookies so Server Components render the correct initial state without layout shift.',
    code: `<SidebarProvider defaultOpen={cookieOpen}>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not allow the sidebar to flash or jump width after hydration.',
    code: `<SidebarProvider defaultOpen={false}>{/* jumps after mount */}</SidebarProvider>`,
  }}
/>

## Related

- [AppRail](/ui/docs/components/layout/app-rail) — Ultra-narrow module navigation rail placed alongside Sidebar.
- [TopBar](/ui/docs/components/layout/top-bar) — Global application top navigation bar.
- [PageHeader](/ui/docs/components/layout/page-header) — Page title and action header within the main content canvas.

---

## Split Pane (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/layout/split-pane)

Draggable, keyboard-accessible split canvas with percentage-based bounds, collapse thresholds, and double-click reset.

<ComponentPreview name="layout/split-pane/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { SplitPane, type SplitPaneProps } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `SplitPane` for desktop master-detail views where operators need continuous access to both a list and its details:

- **Purchase order inspection**: Orders list on the left, line-item inspector on the right.
- **Logistics consignment tracking**: Consignment manifest beside live map tracking or warehouse logs.
- **Code or payload comparison**: Side-by-side JSON comparison of ERP webhook payloads.

**Do not use SplitPane for:**
- Mobile screens — viewports below `768px` lack sufficient width; render the detail view inside a [Sheet](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet) instead.
- Simple multi-column forms — use [FormGrid](/ui/docs/components/layout/form-layout).
- Tabbed perspectives of the same entity — use [Tabs](/ui/docs/components/navigation/tabs).

## Examples

### Basic usage with default sizing and constraints

Pass exactly two child elements and give the container a defined height:

```tsx
<SplitPane
  defaultSize={35}
  minSize={20}
  maxSize={60}
  className="h-[calc(100dvh-8rem)] rounded-lg border"
>
  <div className="overflow-y-auto p-4 border-r">
    {/* Master list of purchase orders */}
  </div>
  <div className="overflow-y-auto p-6">
    {/* Detail inspection view */}
  </div>
</SplitPane>
```

### Responsive pattern: SplitPane on desktop, Sheet on mobile

A canonical ERP master-detail pattern that switches gracefully between split panes and slide-over drawers:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { SplitPane, Sheet, SheetContent, SheetHeader, SheetTitle, SheetBody, useMediaQuery } from '@innostes/ui';

export function MasterDetailOrders({ orders }) {
  const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const isDesktop = useMediaQuery('(min-width: 768px)');
  const activeOrder = orders.find((o) => o.id === selectedId);

  if (isDesktop) {
    return (
      <SplitPane defaultSize={40} minSize={25} maxSize={65} className="h-full">
        <OrderList orders={orders} onSelect={setSelectedId} selectedId={selectedId} />
        <OrderDetail order={activeOrder} />
      </SplitPane>
    );
  }

  return (
    <>
      <OrderList orders={orders} onSelect={setSelectedId} selectedId={selectedId} />
      <Sheet open={Boolean(activeOrder)} onOpenChange={(open) => !open && setSelectedId(null)}>
        <SheetContent side="end">
          <SheetHeader>
            <SheetTitle>Order #{activeOrder?.id}</SheetTitle>
          </SheetHeader>
          <SheetBody>
            <OrderDetail order={activeOrder} />
          </SheetBody>
        </SheetContent>
      </Sheet>
    </>
  );
}
```

### Vertical orientation

Stack panes vertically by specifying `orientation="vertical"`:

```tsx
<SplitPane orientation="vertical" defaultSize={60} className="h-96">
  <div className="p-4">{/* Top pane: Query editor */}</div>
  <div className="p-4">{/* Bottom pane: Execution results */}</div>
</SplitPane>
```

## Accessibility

`SplitPane` implements the WAI-ARIA Window Splitter pattern.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'LeftArrow / RightArrow', action: 'Resizes horizontal panes by the step increment (2% by default).' },
    { key: 'UpArrow / DownArrow', action: 'Resizes vertical panes by the step increment.' },
    { key: 'Shift + Arrow keys', action: 'Resizes panes at 4× standard speed (8% per press).' },
    { key: 'Home', action: 'Jumps directly to the minimum allowed pane size (minSize).' },
    { key: 'End', action: 'Jumps directly to the maximum allowed pane size (maxSize).' },
    { key: 'Enter / Double Click', action: 'Resets the pane divider to its initial defaultSize position.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The divider handle renders with `role="separator"` and `tabIndex={0}`.
- It supplies `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, and `aria-valuemax` representing the percentage width of the primary pane.
- `aria-controls` explicitly references the identifier of the primary resizing pane.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Enforce reasonable minSize and maxSize constraints so neither pane collapses into an illegible sliver.',
    code: `<SplitPane minSize={20} maxSize={70} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not allow panes to resize freely from 0% to 100% without bounds.',
    code: `<SplitPane minSize={0} maxSize={100} />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Switch to a Sheet overlay drawer on mobile viewports below 768px.',
    code: `{isDesktop ? <SplitPane /> : <Sheet />}`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not render two-column split panes on narrow mobile smartphones.',
    code: `<div className="w-[320px]"><SplitPane /></div>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['SplitPane']} />

## Related

- [Master-detail screens pattern](/ui/docs/patterns/master-detail) — Responsive split-screen guide with SplitPane on desktop and Sheet on mobile.
- [Sheet](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet) — Slide-over drawer used for responsive mobile master-detail views.
- [DataTable](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table) — Interactive table component frequently placed in the primary pane.
- [ScrollArea](/ui/docs/components/layout/scroll-area) — Independent scrolling container for individual pane contents.

## Top Bar (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/layout/top-bar)

Responsive application header with semantic slots (TopBarStart, TopBarCenter, TopBarEnd) and translucent blur support.

<ComponentPreview name="layout/top-bar/basic" align="start" className="p-4 sm:p-4" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  TopBar,
  TopBarStart,
  TopBarCenter,
  TopBarEnd,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `TopBar` as the persistent header across administrative and enterprise applications:

- **Application header**: Housing the organization logo, workspace switcher, and mobile sidebar trigger.
- **Global search integration**: Providing a prominent trigger for [CommandPalette](/ui/docs/components/overlays/command-palette).
- **Tenant and user profile tools**: Housing branch switchers (e.g. Bengaluru vs Mumbai), alert notifications, and user avatars.

**Do not use TopBar for:**
- In-page sub-headers with breadcrumbs and primary entity actions — use [PageHeader](/ui/docs/components/layout/page-header).
- Local card headers — use [Card](/ui/docs/components/data-display/card).
- Pure marketing navigation headers with multi-level megamenus.

## Examples

### Three-slot header composition

Using `TopBarStart`, `TopBarCenter`, and `TopBarEnd`:

```tsx
<TopBar sticky blur>
  <TopBarStart>
    <SidebarTrigger />
    <div className="flex items-center gap-2 font-semibold text-sm">
      <span className="size-6 rounded bg-primary text-primary-foreground flex items-center justify-center font-bold text-xs">
        N
      </span>
      <span>Northwind Traders</span>
    </div>
  </TopBarStart>

  <TopBarCenter>
    <Button
      variant="outline"
      size="sm"
      className="w-full max-w-sm justify-between text-muted-foreground"
      onClick={openSearch}
    >
      <span>Search invoices, POs, vendors...</span>
      <kbd className="text-xs bg-muted border px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded">⌘K</kbd>
    </Button>
  </TopBarCenter>

  <TopBarEnd>
    <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" iconOnly aria-label="Notifications">
      <BellIcon className="size-4" />
    </Button>
    <UserMenu name="Priya Sharma" email="priya.sharma@northwind.in" />
  </TopBarEnd>
</TopBar>
```

### Sticky positioning and backdrop blur

`TopBar` sticks to the top of the viewport by default. Enable `blur` for a translucent frosted glass effect over scrolling content:

```tsx
<TopBar sticky blur className="border-b">
  {/* Content blurred under header while scrolling */}
</TopBar>
```

## Accessibility

`TopBar` implements semantic landmark navigation.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus sequentially across interactive controls inside Start, Center, and End slots.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The container renders as a `<header>` element with `data-slot="top-bar"`.
- Buttons and search triggers inside `TopBar` maintain clear `aria-label` text for assistive devices.
- Focus order flows naturally from left to right in LTR (and right to left in RTL).

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Place global command search in TopBarCenter, configured to shrink gracefully on smaller viewports.',
    code: `<TopBarCenter><SearchTrigger /></TopBarCenter>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not overload TopBar with dozens of primary form buttons (use PageHeader or FormActions instead).',
    code: `<TopBarEnd><Button>Save</Button><Button>Export</Button><Button>Audit</Button></TopBarEnd>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Include an accessible SidebarTrigger in TopBarStart so mobile users can easily open navigation.',
    code: `<TopBarStart><SidebarTrigger /></TopBarStart>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not omit the mobile trigger, leaving mobile drawer navigation unreachable.',
    code: `<TopBarStart>{/* No SidebarTrigger */}</TopBarStart>`,
  }}
/>

<ApiTable
  components={[
    'TopBar',
    'TopBarStart',
    'TopBarCenter',
    'TopBarEnd',
  ]}

## Accordion (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/navigation/accordion)

Single or multi-expanded collapsible sections with animated height transitions and keyboard support.

<ComponentPreview name="navigation/accordion/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Accordion,
  AccordionItem,
  AccordionTrigger,
  AccordionPanel,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Accordion` to organize progressive disclosure content in vertically constrained spaces:

- **Frequently asked questions (FAQs)**: Compliance and GST tax invoice questions.
- **Grouped settings**: Collapsible sections for billing preferences, notifications, and permissions.
- **Detailed record audit logs**: Expanding historical revisions on vendor profiles.

**Do not use Accordion for:**
- Primary application navigation across distinct URLs — use [Tabs](/ui/docs/components/navigation/tabs) or [Sidebar](/ui/docs/components/layout/sidebar).
- A single isolated disclosure box like "Advanced options" — use [Collapsible](/ui/docs/components/navigation/collapsible).
- Sequential multi-stage onboarding flows — use [Stepper](/ui/docs/components/navigation/stepper).

## Examples

### Basic usage with default open item

An accordion for enterprise procurement terms:

```tsx
<Accordion defaultValue={['gst-compliance']}>
  <AccordionItem value="gst-compliance">
    <AccordionTrigger>GST compliance and invoicing</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionPanel>
      Northwind Traders generates digital e-invoices with valid IRN numbers and dynamic QR codes for B2B transactions under Indian GST laws.
    </AccordionPanel>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem value="delivery-terms">
    <AccordionTrigger>Delivery schedule and transit insurance</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionPanel>
      Consignments dispatched from our Bengaluru hub include full transit insurance under All Risks Marine clauses.
    </AccordionPanel>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

### Multiple expanded sections

Set `multiple` to allow users to inspect multiple sections simultaneously:

```tsx
<Accordion multiple defaultValue={['summary', 'tax']}>
  <AccordionItem value="summary">
    <AccordionTrigger>Order summary</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionPanel>PO-2026-081 created for ₹89,400 with 18% integrated GST.</AccordionPanel>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem value="tax">
    <AccordionTrigger>Tax breakdown</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionPanel>CGST (9%): ₹6,818.64 | SGST (9%): ₹6,818.64</AccordionPanel>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

## Accessibility

`Accordion` is built on Base UI Accordion primitives (`@base-ui/react/accordion`).

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Expands or collapses the focused accordion trigger.' },
    { key: 'DownArrow', action: 'Moves focus to the next accordion header trigger.' },
    { key: 'UpArrow', action: 'Moves focus to the previous accordion header trigger.' },
    { key: 'Home', action: 'Moves focus to the first accordion header trigger.' },
    { key: 'End', action: 'Moves focus to the last accordion header trigger.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- Each `AccordionTrigger` is rendered as an accessible button with `aria-expanded="true | false"` and `aria-controls` pointing to its panel id.
- Each `AccordionPanel` receives `role="region"` and `aria-labelledby` referencing its trigger.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use clear, descriptive trigger headers that indicate the contents hidden inside.',
    code: `<AccordionTrigger>Statutory GST information</AccordionTrigger>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not use vague trigger text that leaves users guessing what each panel contains.',
    code: `<AccordionTrigger>More info</AccordionTrigger>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use multiple when users need to cross-reference details across multiple panels at once.',
    code: `<Accordion multiple defaultValue={['items', 'taxes']} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not force single expansion when users must frequently compare data across sections.',
    code: `<Accordion defaultValue={['items']} />`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable
  components={[
    'Accordion',
    'AccordionItem',
    'AccordionTrigger',
    'AccordionPanel',
  ]}
  baseUi="accordion"
/>

## Related

- [Collapsible](/ui/docs/components/navigation/collapsible) — Standalone disclosure container for a single section.
- [Tabs](/ui/docs/components/navigation/tabs) — Switch between distinct views without stacking them vertically.
- [Stepper](/ui/docs/components/navigation/stepper) — Multi-step sequential progression indicator.

## Breadcrumb (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/navigation/breadcrumb)

Linear ancestral navigation with router integration, current-page indication, and ellipsis support for deep paths.

<ComponentPreview name="navigation/breadcrumb/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Breadcrumb,
  BreadcrumbList,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbLink,
  BreadcrumbPage,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
  BreadcrumbEllipsis,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Breadcrumb` to establish hierarchical context within deep enterprise applications:

- **Multi-tiered resource views**: `Purchasing > Vendors > Bengaluru Spices > Orders > PO-2026-081`.
- **Complex nested configuration**: `Settings > Enterprise > Billing & Tax > GSTIN Profiles`.
- **Catalogue and warehousing**: `Inventory > Raw Materials > Spices & Seasonings > Cardamom Grade A`.

**Do not use Breadcrumb for:**
- Flat top-level navigation — use [TopBar](/ui/docs/components/layout/top-bar) or [AppRail](/ui/docs/components/layout/app-rail).
- Linear multi-step sequential tasks or wizards — use [Stepper](/ui/docs/components/navigation/stepper).
- History-based browser back/forward pagination.

## Examples

### Integration with Next.js router

`BreadcrumbLink` renders a semantic anchor tag (`<a>`). Use the `render` prop to pass Next.js `Link` for client-side transitions:

```tsx
import Link from 'next/link';

<Breadcrumb>
  <BreadcrumbList>
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbLink render={<Link href="/" />}>Dashboard</BreadcrumbLink>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbLink render={<Link href="/purchases" />}>Purchases</BreadcrumbLink>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbPage>PO-2026-081</BreadcrumbPage>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
  </BreadcrumbList>
</Breadcrumb>
```

### Deep hierarchies with ellipsis

When path depths exceed four levels, collapse middle steps using `BreadcrumbEllipsis`:

```tsx
<Breadcrumb>
  <BreadcrumbList>
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbLink href="/inventory">Inventory</BreadcrumbLink>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbEllipsis />
    </BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbLink href="/inventory/warehouses/blr-01">Bengaluru Central Hub</BreadcrumbLink>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbPage>Aisle 4 Bay 12</BreadcrumbPage>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
  </BreadcrumbList>
</Breadcrumb>
```

## Accessibility

`Breadcrumb` renders semantic HTML5 navigation landmarks.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus sequentially along each breadcrumb link in ancestral order.' },
    { key: 'Enter', action: 'Navigates to the focused breadcrumb link.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The container element is a `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">`.
- The list uses `<ol>` and `<li>` elements, giving screen readers an accurate count of total path levels.
- The current page indicator uses `<BreadcrumbPage>` which marks the element with `aria-current="page"`.
- Separators render with `aria-hidden="true"` so assistive technologies ignore decorative divider symbols.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Mark the final item with BreadcrumbPage, rendering text rather than a redundant self-link.',
    code: `<BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbPage>PO-2026-081</BreadcrumbPage></BreadcrumbItem>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not render the current active page as a clickable hyperlink that links to itself.',
    code: `<BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="/current">PO-2026-081</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Keep breadcrumb labels short and consistent with page titles.',
    code: `<BreadcrumbLink href="/purchases">Purchases</BreadcrumbLink>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not include entire verbose descriptions in breadcrumb links.',
    code: `<BreadcrumbLink href="/purchases">Northwind Traders Purchase Order Management System</BreadcrumbLink>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable
  components={[
    'Breadcrumb',
    'BreadcrumbList',
    'BreadcrumbItem',
    'BreadcrumbLink',
    'BreadcrumbPage',
    'BreadcrumbSeparator',
    'BreadcrumbEllipsis',
  ]}
/>

- [PageHeader](/ui/docs/components/layout/page-header) — Standard layout header containing breadcrumb, title, and actions.
- [Pagination](/ui/docs/components/navigation/pagination) — Paginating through records within a single level.
- [Stepper](/ui/docs/components/navigation/stepper) — Multi-step sequential progression flow.

## Collapsible (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/navigation/collapsible)

A flexible disclosure primitive for secondary form options, filter expansions, and collapsible detail cards.

<ComponentPreview name="navigation/collapsible/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Collapsible,
  CollapsibleTrigger,
  CollapsiblePanel,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Collapsible` for isolated disclosures where a user might optionally need extra settings or secondary details:

- **Advanced form fields**: E-way bill vehicle numbers, GST exemption certificates, or dispatch notes.
- **Filter drawers and panels**: Expanding extra facet filters on inventory search.
- **Code snippet disclosures**: Showing generated JSON payloads or webhook logs.

**Do not use Collapsible for:**
- Stacked groups of mutually exclusive sections — use [Accordion](/ui/docs/components/navigation/accordion).
- Top-level page tab switches — use [Tabs](/ui/docs/components/navigation/tabs).
- Complex overlay modals — use [Dialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dialog).

## Examples

### Secondary form options

Hiding advanced tax and compliance fields until requested by the procurement agent:

```tsx
<Collapsible>
  <div className="flex items-center justify-between border-b pb-2">
    <h4 className="text-sm font-semibold">Consignment details</h4>
    <CollapsibleTrigger
      render={
        <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" className="group">
          Advanced options
          <ChevronDownIcon className="size-4 transition-transform duration-200 group-data-panel-open:rotate-180" />
        </Button>
      }
    />
  </div>
  <CollapsiblePanel className="space-y-4 pt-4">
    <Field name="vehicleNo">
      <FieldLabel>E-Way bill vehicle number</FieldLabel>
      <Input placeholder="KA-01-AB-1234" />
    </Field>
    <Field name="transporterId">
      <FieldLabel>Transporter GSTIN / ID</FieldLabel>
      <Input placeholder="29AAAAA0000A1Z5" />
    </Field>
  </CollapsiblePanel>
</Collapsible>
```

### Controlled open state

Manage the disclosure programmatically from external component state:

```tsx
const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);

<Collapsible open={isOpen} onOpenChange={setIsOpen}>
  <div className="flex gap-2">
    <Button onClick={() => setIsOpen((prev) => !prev)}>
      {isOpen ? 'Hide raw audit logs' : 'View raw audit logs'}
    </Button>
  </div>
  <CollapsiblePanel className="mt-4 rounded bg-muted p-4 font-mono text-xs">
    {JSON.stringify(auditRecord, null, 2)}
  </CollapsiblePanel>
</Collapsible>
```

## Accessibility

`Collapsible` is built on Base UI Collapsible primitives (`@base-ui/react/collapsible`).

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Toggles the collapsible panel open or closed when the trigger is focused.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The `CollapsibleTrigger` receives `aria-expanded="true | false"` and `aria-controls` referencing the panel id.
- The trigger button receives `data-panel-open` when the panel is visible, enabling Tailwind group-hover or sibling animations.
- The `CollapsiblePanel` receives `hidden` when closed, ensuring screen readers do not read collapsed content.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use CollapsibleTrigger with a clear label describing what is being toggled.',
    code: `<CollapsibleTrigger render={<Button>Show GST details</Button>} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not hide required primary form fields behind a collapsed panel.',
    code: `<CollapsiblePanel><Field required><Input name="totalAmount" /></Field></CollapsiblePanel>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Animate indicator chevrons with transition-transform and group-data-panel-open:rotate-180.',
    code: `<ChevronDown className="transition-transform group-data-panel-open:rotate-180" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not change the text label completely if it disorients screen readers without aria-live.',
    code: `<CollapsibleTrigger>{open ? 'Close' : 'Open'}</CollapsibleTrigger>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable
  components={[
    'Collapsible',
    'CollapsibleTrigger',
    'CollapsiblePanel',
  ]}
  baseUi="collapsible"
/>

- [Accordion](/ui/docs/components/navigation/accordion) — Vertically stacked series of collapsible disclosure panels.
- [FormLayout](/ui/docs/components/layout/form-layout) — Structured layout for complex forms with optional sections.
- [Card](/ui/docs/components/data-display/card) — Card container often hosting collapsible details.

## Navigation (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/navigation/index)

Structures and controls that guide operators through multi-step journeys and hierarchical data.

import { CategoryGrid } from '@/components/docs/category-grid';

# Navigation

Navigation components establish information architecture and wayfinding across Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd's ERP modules. They provide predictable, keyboard-accessible paths through complex inventory hierarchies, multi-stage procurement flows, and paginated records.

## Components

<CategoryGrid category="components/navigation" />

## Usage guidelines

- **Wayfinding hierarchy**: Combine `Breadcrumb` for relational hierarchy, `Tabs` for alternate views of an entity, and `Stepper` for sequential multi-step wizards.
- **Keyboard navigation**: Tab strips support Left/Right arrow keys for roving focus. Accordions support Up/Down arrow navigation.
- **RTL awareness**: All navigation elements honour document directionality (`dir="rtl"`) with logical margin and icon rotation.

---

## Pagination (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/navigation/pagination)

Controlled page navigation with stable button widths, boundary offsets, and server-side range calculation.

<ComponentPreview name="navigation/pagination/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Pagination, getPaginationRange, type PaginationProps } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Pagination` when dividing large datasets into discrete pages:

- **Enterprise data tables**: Navigating through thousands of purchase orders, stock items, or ledger entries.
- **Search result listings**: Paginated inventory queries or customer catalogues.
- **Audit logs**: Stepping through historical system logs.

**Do not use Pagination for:**
- Infinite feed streams or chat conversations.
- Multi-step wizards or checkout funnels — use [Stepper](/ui/docs/components/navigation/stepper).
- Switching between distinct functional sections on a single screen — use [Tabs](/ui/docs/components/navigation/tabs).

## Examples

### Basic controlled pagination

Managing the current page in component state:

```tsx
const [page, setPage] = useState(1);
const totalRecords = 480;
const pageSize = 20;
const pageCount = Math.ceil(totalRecords / pageSize);

<Pagination
  page={page}
  pageCount={pageCount}
  onPageChange={(nextPage) => {
    setPage(nextPage);
    fetchOrders({ page: nextPage, pageSize });
  }}
/>
```

### Boundary and sibling counts

Adjust `boundaryCount` (pages anchored at the start and end) and `siblingCount` (pages surrounding the current page):

```tsx
<Pagination
  page={page}
  pageCount={50}
  siblingCount={2}
  boundaryCount={2}
  onPageChange={setPage}
/>
```

### Server-side range helper (`getPaginationRange`)

`getPaginationRange` calculates the page numbers and ellipsis positions without importing React, making it ideal for Server Components or custom pagination renderers:

```ts
import { getPaginationRange } from '@innostes/ui';

const range = getPaginationRange({
  page: 6,
  pageCount: 20,
  siblingCount: 1,
  boundaryCount: 1,
});
// Output: [1, 'ellipsis-start', 5, 6, 7, 'ellipsis-end', 20]
```

## Accessibility

`Pagination` implements the WAI-ARIA Navigation pattern.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus sequentially between Previous, page number buttons, and Next.' },
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Activates the focused page number or directional button.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The container is rendered as `<nav aria-label="Pagination">`.
- The active page button has `aria-current="page"`.
- Previous and Next buttons receive descriptive `aria-label` text via `labels.previous` and `labels.next`.
- Ellipsis spans receive `aria-hidden="true"`.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Keep the number of visible buttons stable across page transitions to prevent layout shifts.',
    code: `<Pagination page={page} pageCount={pageCount} onPageChange={setPage} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not re-render dynamic layouts that shift the Next button position as the user clicks.',
    code: `<div style={{ width: page * 20 }}>{buttons}</div>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Disable the Previous button on page 1 and the Next button on the final page.',
    code: `<Pagination page={1} pageCount={10} onPageChange={setPage} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not allow navigation past the first or last available page.',
    code: `<button onClick={() => setPage(page - 1)}>Prev</button>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Pagination']} />

## Related

- [DataTable](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table) — Interactive table component frequently combined with pagination.
- [Stepper](/ui/docs/components/navigation/stepper) — Multi-step sequential progression flow.
- [Tabs](/ui/docs/components/navigation/tabs) — Category switching without numerical paging.

## Stepper (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/navigation/stepper)

Horizontal or vertical multi-step indicator with validation status, step descriptions, and clickable navigation.

<ComponentPreview name="navigation/stepper/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Stepper, type StepperStep, type StepStatus } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Stepper` when guiding users through a sequential multi-stage process where order matters:

- **Purchase order creation**: 1. Supplier details → 2. Line items & GST → 3. Shipping & delivery → 4. Review & confirmation.
- **Vendor onboarding wizard**: Company profile, GSTIN & PAN verification, bank mandate, document upload.
- **Physical goods consignment**: Order booked → Picked & packed → In transit → Delivered.

**Do not use Stepper for:**
- Unordered or freely navigable content sections — use [Tabs](/ui/docs/components/navigation/tabs).
- Simple progress percentages (e.g. 64% complete) without discrete steps — use [Progress](/ui/docs/components/feedback/progress).
- Page-by-page table navigation — use [Pagination](/ui/docs/components/navigation/pagination).

## Examples

### Horizontal stepper with interactive step clicking

Allowing users to return to completed steps to revise information:

```tsx
const steps: StepperStep[] = [
  { title: 'Vendor details', description: 'Bengaluru Spices' },
  { title: 'Items & tax', description: 'HSN 0908 cardamom lines' },
  { title: 'Logistics', description: 'Transport & E-Way' },
  { title: 'Review', description: 'Final verification' },
];

const [currentStep, setCurrentStep] = useState(1);

<Stepper
  steps={steps}
  currentStep={currentStep}
  onStepClick={(index) => {
    // Only allow navigating back to completed steps
    if (index < currentStep) setCurrentStep(index);
  }}
/>
```

### Vertical stepper for consignment tracking

Vertical layout suits long audit histories and mobile screen sizes:

<ComponentPreview name="navigation/stepper/vertical" />

```tsx
const dispatchSteps: StepperStep[] = [
  { title: 'Order placed', description: 'PO-2026-081 approved by Priya Sharma' },
  { title: 'Quality check passed', description: 'Inspected at Bengaluru Hub' },
  { title: 'Dispatched via Blue Dart', description: 'AWB 4910291481' },
  { title: 'Delivered', description: 'Pending destination sign-off' },
];

<Stepper
  orientation="vertical"
  steps={dispatchSteps}
  currentStep={2}
/>
```

### Error states in steps

Flag steps that require user remediation:

```tsx
const stepsWithErrors: StepperStep[] = [
  { title: 'Company profile', status: 'complete' },
  { title: 'GSTIN verification', status: 'error', description: 'Invalid GSTIN checksum' },
  { title: 'Bank account', status: 'upcoming' },
];

<Stepper steps={stepsWithErrors} currentStep={1} />
```

## Accessibility

`Stepper` implements semantic ordered navigation for multi-step procedures.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus to clickable completed step markers.' },
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Navigates back to the selected step.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The container element is a `<nav aria-label="Progress">` enclosing an `<ol>`.
- The current step has `aria-current="step"`.
- Completed and errored steps have accessible announcements via hidden helper labels (e.g. `(completed)`, `(has errors)`), ensuring screen reader users do not miss step statuses that rely on colour.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Allow users to click previously completed steps to review or edit earlier entries.',
    code: `<Stepper steps={steps} currentStep={2} onStepClick={setCurrentStep} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not allow users to skip ahead to incomplete upcoming steps before validation passes.',
    code: `<Stepper steps={steps} currentStep={0} onStepClick={(i) => setCurrentStep(i)} />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use the vertical orientation for mobile responsive layouts and long activity logs.',
    code: `<Stepper orientation="vertical" steps={steps} currentStep={step} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not cram 6+ horizontal steps onto narrow mobile viewports.',
    code: `<div className="w-[320px]"><Stepper steps={sixSteps} /></div>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Stepper']} />

## Related

- [Tabs](/ui/docs/components/navigation/tabs) — Switch between parallel sections without enforced order.
- [Progress](/ui/docs/components/feedback/progress) — Continuous completion bar for deterministic tasks.
- [FormLayout](/ui/docs/components/layout/form-layout) — Layout container for enterprise multi-step form steps.

## Tabs (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/navigation/tabs)

Underline and pill variants with animated active indicator, keyboard navigation, and vertical orientation support.

<ComponentPreview name="navigation/tabs/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTab, TabsPanel } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Tabs` to present parallel views or alternate perspectives of the same core entity:

- **Entity detail views**: Overview, Line Items, Documents, Audit Trail, and Invoices.
- **Settings panels**: Account, Security, Billing, and Team Members.
- **Reporting ranges**: Compact pill switches for Day, Week, Month, Quarter.

**Do not use Tabs for:**
- Sequential step-by-step wizards where order is strictly enforced — use [Stepper](/ui/docs/components/navigation/stepper).
- Deep ancestral tree hierarchies — use [Breadcrumb](/ui/docs/components/navigation/breadcrumb).
- Primary multi-page top-level navigation — use [AppRail](/ui/docs/components/layout/app-rail) or [Sidebar](/ui/docs/components/layout/sidebar).

## Examples

### Underline variant for page sections

The standard underline tab strip with an animated active highlight bar:

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="overview" variant="underline">
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTab value="overview">Order overview</TabsTab>
    <TabsTab value="items">Line items (14)</TabsTab>
    <TabsTab value="shipping">Logistics & E-Way</TabsTab>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsPanel value="overview">
    <div className="py-4">Purchase order details for Bengaluru Spices.</div>
  </TabsPanel>
  <TabsPanel value="items">
    <div className="py-4">Items table with HSN breakdown.</div>
  </TabsPanel>
  <TabsPanel value="shipping">
    <div className="py-4">Tracking consignment via Blue Dart Express.</div>
  </TabsPanel>
</Tabs>
```

### Pills variant for compact metric cards

Use `variant="pills"` inside toolbars or card headers:

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="quarterly" variant="pills">
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTab value="monthly">Monthly</TabsTab>
    <TabsTab value="quarterly">Quarterly</TabsTab>
    <TabsTab value="annual">FY 2025-26</TabsTab>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsPanel value="monthly">{/* Monthly revenue chart */}</TabsPanel>
  <TabsPanel value="quarterly">{/* Quarterly tax review */}</TabsPanel>
  <TabsPanel value="annual">{/* Annual compliance statement */}</TabsPanel>
</Tabs>
```

### Vertical orientation for settings sidebars

Stack tabs vertically for wide screen settings dialogs or configuration layouts:

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="gst" orientation="vertical" className="w-full">
  <TabsList className="w-64 border-r pr-4">
    <TabsTab value="profile">Company profile</TabsTab>
    <TabsTab value="gst">GSTIN & Taxes</TabsTab>
    <TabsTab value="bank">Bank accounts</TabsTab>
  </TabsList>
  <div className="flex-1 pl-6">
    <TabsPanel value="profile">Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd</TabsPanel>
    <TabsPanel value="gst">State: Karnataka (29), GSTIN: 29ABCDE1234F1Z5</TabsPanel>
    <TabsPanel value="bank">HDFC Bank, Bengaluru Koramangala Branch</TabsPanel>
  </div>
</Tabs>
```

## Accessibility

`Tabs` is built on Base UI Tabs primitives (`@base-ui/react/tabs`).

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'ArrowRight / ArrowDown', action: 'Moves focus and selection to the next tab.' },
    { key: 'ArrowLeft / ArrowUp', action: 'Moves focus and selection to the previous tab.' },
    { key: 'Home', action: 'Moves focus and selection to the first tab in the list.' },
    { key: 'End', action: 'Moves focus and selection to the last tab in the list.' },
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus into the currently active tab panel.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The tab strip has `role="tablist"`.
- Each tab trigger has `role="tab"` with `aria-selected="true | false"` and `aria-controls` pointing to its corresponding panel.
- Each content panel has `role="tabpanel"` and `aria-labelledby` referencing its tab trigger.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Keep tab labels concise (1–3 words) so tab strips remain legible and avoid awkward wraps.',
    code: `<TabsTab value="audit">Audit trail</TabsTab>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not use long sentences or paragraphs as tab labels.',
    code: `<TabsTab value="audit">Click here to inspect full transaction history</TabsTab>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use the pills variant for compact segmented controls inside toolbars and card headers.',
    code: `<Tabs variant="pills"><TabsList><TabsTab value="day">Day</TabsTab></TabsList></Tabs>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not mix underline and pills styles arbitrarily on the same page.',
    code: `<Tabs variant="underline"><Tabs variant="pills" /></Tabs>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable
  components={[
    'Tabs',
    'TabsList',
    'TabsTab',
    'TabsPanel',
  ]}
  baseUi="tabs"
/>

## Related

- [Accordion](/ui/docs/components/navigation/accordion) — Stacked vertical disclosure panels.
- [AppRail](/ui/docs/components/layout/app-rail) — Vertical navigation rail for primary application modules.
- [Stepper](/ui/docs/components/navigation/stepper) — Multi-step sequential progression flow.
