## Alert Dialog (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/overlays/alert-dialog)

Strict modal confirmation dialog that disables backdrop light-dismiss, focuses the safe cancel action by default, and communicates consequences clearly.

<ComponentPreview name="overlays/alert-dialog/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogClose,
  type AlertDialogProps,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `AlertDialog` when an operator initiates an irreversible, high-consequence action that permanently deletes records or alters financial transactions:

- Voiding verified tax invoices or reversing finalized journal entries.
- Deleting customer profiles, vendor contracts, or warehouse location definitions.
- Terminating active team credentials or revoking tenant API keys.

When choosing overlay confirmation components:
- Use `AlertDialog` (`role="alertdialog"`) for critical confirmations where an accidental click would result in data loss. Backdrop clicking is intentionally disabled.
- Use [Dialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dialog) (`role="dialog"`) for standard multi-field data entry forms, where users can dismiss by clicking outside.
- Use [DropdownMenu](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu) for reversible low-impact choices.
- Refer to the [Overlay decision guide](/ui/docs/components/overlays#overlay-decision-guide) for detailed guidance.

## Examples

### Destructive confirmation

Compose `AlertDialog` with `AlertDialogHeader`, `AlertDialogTitle`, `AlertDialogDescription`, and `AlertDialogFooter`. Use `AlertDialogClose` with `Button variant="destructive"` to handle confirmation:

```tsx
'use client';

import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogClose,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
  Button,
  toast,
} from '@innostes/ui';

export function DeleteVendorConfirmation({ vendorId, vendorName }) {
  const handleDelete = () => {
    // API deletion call
    toast.success(`Vendor ${vendorName} removed.`);
  };

  return (
    <AlertDialog>
      <AlertDialogTrigger render={<Button variant="destructive" />}>
        Delete vendor
      </AlertDialogTrigger>
      <AlertDialogContent>
        <AlertDialogHeader>
          <AlertDialogTitle>Delete {vendorName}?</AlertDialogTitle>
          <AlertDialogDescription>
            This action cannot be undone. Removing this vendor will archive 48 purchase order line items and deactivate all linked procurement catalogs.
          </AlertDialogDescription>
        </AlertDialogHeader>
        <AlertDialogFooter>
          <AlertDialogClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>
            Cancel
          </AlertDialogClose>
          <AlertDialogClose
            render={<Button variant="destructive" />}
            onClick={handleDelete}
          >
            Delete vendor
          </AlertDialogClose>
        </AlertDialogFooter>
      </AlertDialogContent>
    </AlertDialog>
  );
}
```

### Strict modality without light-dismiss

Unlike standard dialogs, clicking the dimmed background backdrop does **not** close an `AlertDialog`. Operators must explicitly press the "Cancel" action or Escape key to dismiss:

```tsx
<AlertDialog>
  <AlertDialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Revoke license</AlertDialogTrigger>
  <AlertDialogContent>
    <AlertDialogHeader>
      <AlertDialogTitle>Revoke enterprise license?</AlertDialogTitle>
      <AlertDialogDescription>
        Active depot operators will immediately lose access to the dispatch terminal.
      </AlertDialogDescription>
    </AlertDialogHeader>
    <AlertDialogFooter>
      <AlertDialogClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Cancel</AlertDialogClose>
      <AlertDialogClose render={<Button variant="destructive" />}>Revoke license</AlertDialogClose>
    </AlertDialogFooter>
  </AlertDialogContent>
</AlertDialog>
```

### Asynchronous deletion with progress feedback

Combine `AlertDialog` with controlled open state and loading feedback during asynchronous API requests:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogClose,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
  Button,
  toast,
} from '@innostes/ui';

export function AsyncVoidInvoice({ invoiceId }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [isVoiding, setIsVoiding] = useState(false);

  const handleVoid = async () => {
    setIsVoiding(true);
    try {
      await fetch(`/api/v1/invoices/${invoiceId}/void`, { method: 'POST' });
      setOpen(false);
      toast.success(`Invoice ${invoiceId} voided`);
    } catch {
      toast.error('Failed to void invoice. Check e-invoicing gateway status.');
    } finally {
      setIsVoiding(false);
    }
  };

  return (
    <AlertDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
      <AlertDialogTrigger render={<Button variant="destructive" />}>
        Void invoice
      </AlertDialogTrigger>
      <AlertDialogContent>
        <AlertDialogHeader>
          <AlertDialogTitle>Void invoice {invoiceId}?</AlertDialogTitle>
          <AlertDialogDescription>
            This action will reverse accounts receivable ledger entries and submit a credit memo to the GSTN portal.
          </AlertDialogDescription>
        </AlertDialogHeader>
        <AlertDialogFooter>
          <AlertDialogClose render={<Button variant="outline" disabled={isVoiding} />}>
            Cancel
          </AlertDialogClose>
          <Button variant="destructive" loading={isVoiding} onClick={handleVoid}>
            Confirm void
          </Button>
        </AlertDialogFooter>
      </AlertDialogContent>
    </AlertDialog>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

`AlertDialog` implements the W3C WAI-ARIA Alert Dialog design pattern via Base UI (`@base-ui/react/alert-dialog`).

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Escape', action: 'Dismisses the alert dialog and restores focus to the trigger button.' },
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Cycles focus between the Cancel button and the confirming action button.' },
    { key: 'Enter', action: 'Activates the currently focused button.' },
  ]}
/>

### Initial safe focus

When the alert dialog mounts, focus is automatically placed on the non-destructive **Cancel** action by default. This deliberate safeguard prevents operators who instinctively press Enter from accidentally executing an irreversible operation.

### Screen readers (role="alertdialog")

- `AlertDialogContent` carries `role="alertdialog"`. Assistive technologies announce both the title and the descriptive warning text immediately upon display.
- Background content is marked `inert`, preventing virtual cursors from escaping the modal window.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Clearly describe the irreversible consequences in AlertDialogDescription (e.g., number of affected rows, financial reversals).',
    code: `<AlertDialogDescription>\n  Reverses ₹42,000 in receivables and cancels the e-way bill.\n</AlertDialogDescription>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not use generic, unhelpful questions like "Are you sure?" without explaining the consequences.',
    code: `<AlertDialogDescription>Are you sure you want to proceed?</AlertDialogDescription>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use explicit verbs on confirmation buttons matching the action (e.g. "Void invoice", "Delete customer").',
    code: `<Button variant="destructive">Void invoice</Button>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not use vague "Yes" or "OK" buttons that require reading the title again to know what is happening.',
    code: `<Button variant="destructive">OK</Button>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable
  components={[
    'AlertDialog',
    'AlertDialogTrigger',
    'AlertDialogContent',
    'AlertDialogHeader',
    'AlertDialogTitle',
    'AlertDialogDescription',
    'AlertDialogFooter',
    'AlertDialogClose',
  ]}
  baseUi="alert-dialog"
/>

- [Dialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dialog) — Standard modal dialog for forms and multi-field inputs.
- [Button](/ui/docs/components/actions/button) — Action button with destructive styling.

## Command Palette (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/overlays/command-palette)

A global command overlay triggered by keyboard shortcut (⌘K) to quickly search records, navigate pages, and execute administrative actions.

<ComponentPreview name="overlays/command-palette/basic" align="start" className="p-4 sm:p-4" />

## Import

```tsx
import { CommandPalette, type CommandGroup, type CommandItem } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `CommandPalette` as the central keyboard-driven interface for enterprise applications:

- **Global navigation**: Jumping across ERP modules (Purchase Orders, Tax Invoices, General Ledger, Vendors).
- **Administrative actions**: Creating records, exporting reports, or toggling developer modes.
- **Search and recent items**: Finding recently edited contracts or frequently accessed supplier files.

**Do not use CommandPalette for:**
- Standard dropdown action lists on a single row — use [DropdownMenu](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu).
- Form field selection from a predefined enumeration — use [Select](/ui/docs/components/forms/select).
- Complex workflows requiring multiple user inputs or validation — use [Dialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dialog).

## Examples

### Grouping and shortcuts

Organise commands into logical categories such as Pages, Recent items, and Actions:

```tsx
const groups: CommandGroup[] = [
  {
    heading: 'Recent items',
    items: [
      {
        id: 'po-2026-081',
        label: 'PO-2026-081 · Bengaluru Spices',
        description: 'Updated 10 minutes ago · ₹89,400',
        onSelect: () => router.push('/purchases/PO-2026-081'),
      },
    ],
  },
  {
    heading: 'Quick actions',
    items: [
      {
        id: 'new-po',
        label: 'Create purchase order',
        shortcut: 'C P',
        keywords: ['procurement', 'buy', 'vendor'],
        onSelect: () => router.push('/purchases/new'),
      },
      {
        id: 'export-gst',
        label: 'Generate GST return (GSTR-1)',
        shortcut: 'G R',
        keywords: ['tax', 'finance', 'invoices'],
        onSelect: openGstExportDialog,
      },
    ],
  },
];

<CommandPalette groups={groups} />
```

### Global shortcut configuration

By default, the palette listens for `Ctrl + K` or `⌘ + K`. Customise the shortcut key with `hotkey="j"` or pass `hotkey={null}` to disable the automatic global listener and control visibility manually:

```tsx
// Custom hotkey ⌘J
<CommandPalette hotkey="j" groups={groups} />

// Manual trigger from top navigation bar button
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
  Search commands (⌘K)
</Button>
<CommandPalette
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  hotkey="k"
  groups={groups}
/>
```

### Dynamic search and recent items

Combine static navigation items with dynamically updated recent items stored in local state or browser storage:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
import { CommandPalette, type CommandGroup } from '@innostes/ui';

export function GlobalSearch() {
  const [recentIds, setRecentIds] = useState<string[]>([]);

  useEffect(() => {
    const saved = localStorage.getItem('northwind_recent_records');
    if (saved) setRecentIds(JSON.parse(saved));
  }, []);

  const groups: CommandGroup[] = [
    {
      heading: 'Recent records',
      items: recentIds.map((id) => ({
        id,
        label: `Record ${id}`,
        onSelect: () => navigateToRecord(id),
      })),
    },
    {
      heading: 'Modules',
      items: [
        { id: 'inventory', label: 'Inventory & Warehousing', onSelect: () => router.push('/inventory') },
        { id: 'billing', label: 'Invoices & E-Way Bills', onSelect: () => router.push('/billing') },
      ],
    },
  ];

  return <CommandPalette groups={groups} />;
}
```

## Accessibility

`CommandPalette` implements the WAI-ARIA Combobox pattern anchored within a modal dialog (`@base-ui/react/dialog`).

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: '⌘ + K / Ctrl + K', action: 'Toggles the command palette open or closed from anywhere in the app.' },
    { key: 'DownArrow / UpArrow', action: 'Moves active selection through the filtered list of commands.' },
    { key: 'Enter', action: 'Executes the active command and automatically dismisses the palette.' },
    { key: 'Escape', action: 'Dismisses the command palette and restores focus to the previously focused element.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The search input element uses `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded="true"`, and `aria-autocomplete="list"`.
- `aria-activedescendant` tracks the focused option without removing keyboard focus from the search input, allowing continuous typing while navigating.
- The results list uses `role="listbox"`, with individual entries having `role="option"` and `aria-selected="true | false"`.
- Groups are marked with `role="group"` and reference their group headings via `aria-labelledby`.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Provide relevant keywords in item definitions so users can find commands using alternative search terms.',
    code: `{ id: 'gstr', label: 'GST Returns', keywords: ['tax', 'compliance', 'hsn'] }`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not overload the palette with hundreds of unfiltered records; keep initial lists focused and relevant.',
    code: `{ heading: 'All 50,000 customers', items: allCustomers }`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Include visual shortcut badges (e.g. "C P") to teach users faster navigation combinations over time.',
    code: `{ id: 'new-po', label: 'Create PO', shortcut: 'C P' }`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not invent confusing or non-standard shortcut keys that conflict with native browser commands.',
    code: `{ id: 'print', label: 'Print', shortcut: '⌘ W' }`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['CommandPalette']} />

## Related

- [TopBar](/ui/docs/components/layout/top-bar) — Global application top bar with search trigger button.
- [Dialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dialog) — Modal window for focused multi-step workflows.
- [DropdownMenu](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu) — Trigger-anchored action lists for individual entities.

## Context Menu (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/overlays/context-menu)

Pointer-anchored action menus supporting submenus, keyboard shortcuts, and toggle items.

<ComponentPreview name="overlays/context-menu/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  ContextMenu,
  ContextMenuTrigger,
  ContextMenuContent,
  ContextMenuItem,
  ContextMenuSeparator,
  ContextMenuShortcut,
  ContextMenuCheckboxItem,
  ContextMenuRadioGroup,
  ContextMenuRadioItem,
  ContextMenuSub,
  ContextMenuSubTrigger,
  ContextMenuSubContent,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `ContextMenu` to provide power-user contextual shortcuts directly where the user clicks or taps:

- **Enterprise data grid rows**: Quick access to edit, copy ID, duplicate, or inspect records.
- **Tree view and file directories**: Renaming, moving, downloading, or archiving documents.
- **Canvas or diagram editors**: Context-specific manipulation of nodes and edges.

**Do not use ContextMenu as the only way to perform an action.** Right-click gestures are invisible, undiscoverable for new users, and difficult to trigger on touch screens. Always provide a primary on-screen button or a [DropdownMenu](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu) alongside it.

## Examples

### Table row contextual actions

Allowing users to right-click an ERP table row for immediate options:

```tsx
<ContextMenu>
  <ContextMenuTrigger className="flex items-center justify-between rounded border p-4">
    <div>
      <div className="font-medium">INV-2026-081 (Bengaluru Spices)</div>
      <div className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">₹89,400 · Tax invoice</div>
    </div>
    <span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Right-click for options</span>
  </ContextMenuTrigger>
  <ContextMenuContent>
    <ContextMenuItem onClick={() => router.push('/invoices/INV-2026-081')}>
      View details
      <ContextMenuShortcut>⌘O</ContextMenuShortcut>
    </ContextMenuItem>
    <ContextMenuItem onClick={copyInvoiceNumber}>
      Copy invoice number
      <ContextMenuShortcut>⌘C</ContextMenuShortcut>
    </ContextMenuItem>
    <ContextMenuSeparator />
    <ContextMenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={openVoidDialog}>
      Void invoice
    </ContextMenuItem>
  </ContextMenuContent>
</ContextMenu>
```

### Contextual submenus

Organise deeper secondary actions using nested submenus:

```tsx
<ContextMenu>
  <ContextMenuTrigger className="rounded-lg border border-dashed p-8 text-center text-sm">
    Right-click here to view reporting options
  </ContextMenuTrigger>
  <ContextMenuContent>
    <ContextMenuItem onClick={refreshData}>Refresh data</ContextMenuItem>
    <ContextMenuSub>
      <ContextMenuSubTrigger>Export as</ContextMenuSubTrigger>
      <ContextMenuSubContent>
        <ContextMenuItem onClick={exportXlsx}>Excel spreadsheet (.xlsx)</ContextMenuItem>
        <ContextMenuItem onClick={exportPdf}>PDF summary</ContextMenuItem>
      </ContextMenuSubContent>
    </ContextMenuSub>
  </ContextMenuContent>
</ContextMenu>
```

## Accessibility

`ContextMenu` is built on Base UI Menu primitives (`@base-ui/react/menu`).

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Shift + F10 / Menu', action: 'Opens the context menu anchored to the currently focused trigger element.' },
    { key: 'DownArrow / UpArrow', action: 'Cycles keyboard focus between menu items.' },
    { key: 'RightArrow', action: 'Opens a submenu when focused on a sub-trigger item.' },
    { key: 'LeftArrow / Escape', action: 'Closes a submenu and returns focus to its parent trigger item.' },
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Executes the focused menu item and dismisses the context menu.' },
    { key: 'Escape', action: 'Closes the context menu and restores focus to the trigger element.' },
  ]}
/>

### Discovery and touch interfaces

- Right-click is not discoverable through visual scanning alone. Every action exposed in a context menu must also be accessible via a visible UI element (such as a toolbar button or table row action menu).
- Long-press support allows mobile browsers to trigger the context menu, but primary mobile workflows should rely on explicit touch buttons.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Ensure every action available in a context menu is also accessible via standard on-screen controls.',
    code: `<><ContextMenuTrigger>{row}</ContextMenuTrigger><Button iconOnly><MoreHorizontal /></Button></>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not hide primary actions exclusively behind right-click context menus.',
    code: `<ContextMenuTrigger>{row}</ContextMenuTrigger>{/* No visible button */}`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Provide keyboard shortcut indicators when the corresponding keyboard shortcuts are globally active.',
    code: `<ContextMenuItem>Duplicate<ContextMenuShortcut>⌘D</ContextMenuShortcut></ContextMenuItem>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not list keyboard shortcuts that are not actually bound or functional in the current view.',
    code: `<ContextMenuItem>Export<ContextMenuShortcut>Ctrl+Alt+Shift+E</ContextMenuShortcut></ContextMenuItem>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable
  components={[
    'ContextMenu',
    'ContextMenuTrigger',
    'ContextMenuContent',
  ]}
  baseUi="context-menu"
/>

- [DropdownMenu](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu) — Standard button-triggered action menu.
- [DataTable](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table) — Interactive table component frequently combined with row context menus.
- [Popover](/ui/docs/components/overlays/popover) — Non-modal floating surface for interactive forms.

## Dialog (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/overlays/dialog)

Modal dialog with automatic focus trapping, backdrop blur, Escape and outside-click dismissal, and five content size tiers.

<ComponentPreview name="overlays/dialog/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogTrigger,
  DialogContent,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogClose,
  type DialogProps,
  type DialogContentProps,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Dialog` when an operator needs to complete a critical, self-contained sub-task without losing the context of their underlying workspace:

- Editing entity records (updating vendor contact details, revising purchase order items).
- Creating new ledger accounts, cost centres, or warehouse storage bins.
- Providing focused administrative forms that require explicit submission or cancellation.

When choosing overlay components:
- Use `Dialog` for short, focused modal interactions and multi-field forms.
- Use [Alert Dialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/alert-dialog) when presenting irreversible destructive confirmation prompts ("Delete vendor", "Void transaction").
- Use [Sheet](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet) for long edit forms, complex audit logs, or side inspection panels.
- Refer to the [Overlay decision guide](/ui/docs/components/overlays#overlay-decision-guide) for full details.

## Examples

### Basic dialog with form

Combine `Dialog` with `Form` and `Field`. Use the `render` prop on `DialogTrigger` and `DialogClose` to render `@innostes/ui` `Button` components:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import {
  Button,
  Dialog,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
  Field,
  FieldLabel,
  Form,
  Input,
  toast,
} from '@innostes/ui';

export function EditVendorDialog() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

  return (
    <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
      <DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>
        Edit vendor details
      </DialogTrigger>
      <DialogContent>
        <DialogHeader>
          <DialogTitle>Edit vendor details</DialogTitle>
          <DialogDescription>
            Update registered address and GSTIN for Tata Consumer Products.
          </DialogDescription>
        </DialogHeader>
        <Form
          onFormSubmit={() => {
            setOpen(false);
            toast.success('Vendor details updated successfully');
          }}
        >
          <div className="flex flex-col gap-4 py-2">
            <Field name="vendorName">
              <FieldLabel>Legal entity name</FieldLabel>
              <Input defaultValue="Tata Consumer Products Ltd" required />
            </Field>
          </div>
          <DialogFooter>
            <DialogClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Cancel</DialogClose>
            <Button type="submit">Save changes</Button>
          </DialogFooter>
        </Form>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  );
}
```

### Preventing close during async save

To prevent accidental data loss or partial submissions, block dismissal while an asynchronous operation is saving:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { Button, Dialog, DialogContent, DialogTitle, toast } from '@innostes/ui';

export function AsyncSafeDialog() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [saving, setSaving] = useState(false);

  const handleOpenChange = (nextOpen: boolean) => {
    // Prevent closing via backdrop click or Escape while async save is executing
    if (saving) return;
    setOpen(nextOpen);
  };

  const handleSave = async () => {
    setSaving(true);
    try {
      await saveRecord();
      setOpen(false);
      toast.success('Record persisted.');
    } finally {
      setSaving(false);
    }
  };

  return (
    <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={handleOpenChange}>
      {/* Dialog content with saving state on submit button */}
    </Dialog>
  );
}
```

### Confirming unsaved changes

When a user attempts to dismiss a dirty form, open a nested `AlertDialog` to confirm whether changes should be discarded:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogAction,
  AlertDialogCancel,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  Button,
  Dialog,
  DialogContent,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
} from '@innostes/ui';

export function DirtyCheckDialog() {
  const [dialogOpen, setDialogOpen] = useState(false);
  const [confirmOpen, setConfirmOpen] = useState(false);
  const [isDirty, setIsDirty] = useState(false);

  const handleDismissAttempt = () => {
    if (isDirty) {
      setConfirmOpen(true);
    } else {
      setDialogOpen(false);
    }
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Dialog open={dialogOpen} onOpenChange={(open) => !open ? handleDismissAttempt() : setDialogOpen(true)}>
        <DialogContent>
          <DialogHeader>
            <DialogTitle>Edit consignment notes</DialogTitle>
          </DialogHeader>
          {/* Form fields that set isDirty */}
        </DialogContent>
      </Dialog>

      <AlertDialog open={confirmOpen} onOpenChange={setConfirmOpen}>
        <AlertDialogContent>
          <AlertDialogHeader>
            <AlertDialogTitle>Discard unsaved changes?</AlertDialogTitle>
            <AlertDialogDescription>
              You have unsaved edits. Closing will discard all modifications.
            </AlertDialogDescription>
          </AlertDialogHeader>
          <AlertDialogFooter>
            <AlertDialogCancel>Keep editing</AlertDialogCancel>
            <AlertDialogAction
              variant="destructive"
              onClick={() => {
                setIsDirty(false);
                setConfirmOpen(false);
                setDialogOpen(false);
              }}
            >
              Discard changes
            </AlertDialogAction>
          </AlertDialogFooter>
        </AlertDialogContent>
      </AlertDialog>
    </>
  );
}
```

### Controlled opening from a data table

Trigger a dialog programmatically from a row action inside [DataTable](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table):

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { DataTable, Dialog, DialogContent, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, type DataTableColumn } from '@innostes/ui';

interface OrderRow {
  id: string;
  total: number;
}

export function OrderTableWithModal() {
  const [selectedOrder, setSelectedOrder] = useState<OrderRow | null>(null);

  const columns: DataTableColumn<OrderRow>[] = [
    { id: 'id', header: 'Order', accessor: (r) => r.id },
    {
      id: 'actions',
      header: 'Actions',
      cell: (order) => (
        <button type="button" onClick={() => setSelectedOrder(order)} className="text-primary hover:underline text-sm font-medium">
          Edit order
        </button>
      ),
    },
  ];

  return (
    <>
      <DataTable
        aria-label="Orders"
        data={[{ id: 'PO-8410', total: 42000 }]}
        columns={columns}
        getRowId={(r) => r.id}
      />

      <Dialog open={Boolean(selectedOrder)} onOpenChange={(open) => !open && setSelectedOrder(null)}>
        <DialogContent>
          <DialogHeader>
            <DialogTitle>Edit order {selectedOrder?.id}</DialogTitle>
          </DialogHeader>
          {/* Edit form */}
        </DialogContent>
      </Dialog>
    </>
  );
}
```

### Content sizes

Set `size` on `DialogContent` to adjust maximum width: `sm` (384px), `md` (512px, default), `lg` (672px), `xl` (896px), and `full` (viewport width with 1rem margin):

```tsx
<DialogContent size="lg">
  {/* Wide form layout */}
</DialogContent>
```

## Accessibility

`Dialog` implements the WAI-ARIA Modal Dialog Pattern via Base UI (`@base-ui/react/dialog`).

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Escape', action: 'Dismisses the dialog and restores keyboard focus to the opening trigger button.' },
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Cycles focus forward through interactive elements inside the dialog; focus cannot leave the dialog.' },
    { key: 'Shift + Tab', action: 'Cycles focus backward through interactive elements inside the dialog.' },
  ]}
/>

### Focus trapping and restoration

- When opened, focus moves to the first focusable control inside `DialogContent` (or an element with `autoFocus`).
- Tab navigation is strictly trapped inside the dialog container; background elements are marked `inert` and excluded from the accessibility tree.
- When closed, focus is automatically restored to the `DialogTrigger` element.

### Screen readers

- `DialogTitle` automatically provides the accessible name via `aria-labelledby`.
- `DialogDescription` provides supplementary descriptive text via `aria-describedby`.
- Always include `DialogTitle`; if a title should be visually hidden, use `<DialogTitle className="sr-only">`.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Always include DialogTitle and DialogDescription inside DialogHeader for screen reader context.',
    code: `<DialogHeader>\n  <DialogTitle>Tax settings</DialogTitle>\n  <DialogDescription>Update GST filing rates.</DialogDescription>\n</DialogHeader>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not render a modal dialog without a DialogTitle element.',
    code: `<DialogContent>\n  <form>...</form>\n</DialogContent> // Screen reader will not announce title`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Provide a clear Cancel button next to the primary action in DialogFooter.',
    code: `<DialogFooter>\n  <DialogClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Cancel</DialogClose>\n  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>\n</DialogFooter>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not force operators to rely solely on the small top-right close icon or backdrop click to dismiss.',
    code: `<DialogFooter><Button type="submit">Save</Button></DialogFooter>`,
  }}
/>

    'Dialog',

    'DialogFooter',

  ]}
  baseUi="dialog"

## Dropdown Menu (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu)

Groups, keyboard shortcuts, checkbox and radio items, submenus, and destructive row actions.

<ComponentPreview name="overlays/dropdown-menu/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuLinkItem,
  DropdownMenuCheckboxItem,
  DropdownMenuRadioGroup,
  DropdownMenuRadioItem,
  DropdownMenuGroup,
  DropdownMenuGroupLabel,
  DropdownMenuSeparator,
  DropdownMenuShortcut,
  DropdownMenuSub,
  DropdownMenuSubTrigger,
  DropdownMenuSubContent,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `DropdownMenu` when presenting a compact list of distinct commands, navigations, or configuration toggles from a single trigger:

- **Data table row actions**: Consolidating View, Edit, Duplicate, Export, and Delete under a single action button.
- **Header account menus**: Switching user profiles, navigating to billing, or initiating sign-out.
- **View customisation menus**: Toggling visible columns or grouping dimensions.

**Do not use DropdownMenu for:**
- Selectable form values that update an input field — use [Select](/ui/docs/components/forms/select).
- Arbitrary interactive form fields or multi-step controls — use [Popover](/ui/docs/components/overlays/popover).
- Direct right-click pointer menus — use [ContextMenu](/ui/docs/components/overlays/context-menu).

## Examples

### Row actions in enterprise tables

The standard ERP pattern: a `⋯` action button per purchase order row:

```tsx
<DropdownMenu>
  <DropdownMenuTrigger
    render={
      <Button
        variant="ghost"
        size="sm"
        iconOnly
        aria-label="Actions for PO-2026-081"
      />
    }
  >
    <MoreHorizontalIcon />
  </DropdownMenuTrigger>
  <DropdownMenuContent align="end">
    <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => router.push('/purchases/PO-2026-081')}>
      View order
      <DropdownMenuShortcut>⌘O</DropdownMenuShortcut>
    </DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuItem onClick={duplicateOrder}>
      Duplicate line
    </DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuSeparator />
    <DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={openCancelDialog}>
      Cancel PO
    </DropdownMenuItem>
  </DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>
```

### Submenus for hierarchical actions

Nested submenus allow deep hierarchies without cluttering the top-level menu:

```tsx
<DropdownMenu>
  <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>
    Export options
  </DropdownMenuTrigger>
  <DropdownMenuContent>
    <DropdownMenuItem onClick={exportPdf}>PDF Document</DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuSub>
      <DropdownMenuSubTrigger>Spreadsheet</DropdownMenuSubTrigger>
      <DropdownMenuSubContent>
        <DropdownMenuItem onClick={exportCsv}>CSV (UTF-8)</DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuItem onClick={exportXlsx}>Excel Workbook (.xlsx)</DropdownMenuItem>
      </DropdownMenuSubContent>
    </DropdownMenuSub>
  </DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>
```

### Checkbox and radio items

Selectable items preserve toggle state for filter criteria and view modes:

```tsx
<DropdownMenu>
  <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>
    View settings
  </DropdownMenuTrigger>
  <DropdownMenuContent className="w-56">
    <DropdownMenuGroup>
      <DropdownMenuGroupLabel>Columns</DropdownMenuGroupLabel>
      <DropdownMenuCheckboxItem
        checked={showGst}
        onCheckedChange={setShowGst}
      >
        Show GST breakdown
      </DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>
      <DropdownMenuCheckboxItem
        checked={showHsn}
        onCheckedChange={setShowHsn}
      >
        Show HSN codes
      </DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>
    </DropdownMenuGroup>
    <DropdownMenuSeparator />
    <DropdownMenuGroup>
      <DropdownMenuGroupLabel>Density</DropdownMenuGroupLabel>
      <DropdownMenuRadioGroup value={density} onValueChange={setDensity}>
        <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="compact">Compact</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
        <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="comfortable">Comfortable</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
      </DropdownMenuRadioGroup>
    </DropdownMenuGroup>
  </DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>
```

## Accessibility

`DropdownMenu` is built on Base UI Menu primitives (`@base-ui/react/menu`).

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Enter / Space / DownArrow', action: 'Opens the menu and focuses the first enabled menu item.' },
    { key: 'DownArrow / UpArrow', action: 'Cycles focus between menu items, skipping disabled options.' },
    { key: 'RightArrow', action: 'Opens a submenu when focused on a DropdownMenuSubTrigger.' },
    { key: 'LeftArrow / Escape', action: 'Closes a submenu and restores focus to its parent trigger.' },
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Activates the focused item and dismisses the menu.' },
    { key: 'Escape', action: 'Dismisses the open menu and restores focus to the trigger button.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The trigger element receives `aria-haspopup="menu"` and dynamic `aria-expanded`.
- The menu popup container has `role="menu"`.
- Menu items receive `role="menuitem"`, `role="menuitemcheckbox"`, or `role="menuitemradio"` with `aria-checked` states.
- Disabled items receive `aria-disabled="true"`.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use variant="destructive" for irreversible actions like deleting orders or voiding invoices.',
    code: `<DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive">Delete vendor</DropdownMenuItem>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not hide destructive actions with normal styling in a menu full of safe operations.',
    code: `<DropdownMenuItem>Delete vendor</DropdownMenuItem>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Provide an accessible label on the trigger button, especially when using an icon-only "⋯" trigger.',
    code: `<Button iconOnly aria-label="Order actions"><MoreHorizontal /></Button>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not render trigger buttons with only an icon and no accessible name.',
    code: `<Button iconOnly><MoreHorizontal /></Button>`,
  }}
/>

    'DropdownMenu',

## Overlays (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/overlays/index)

Layered interface elements with detailed decision matrix, focus management guarantees, and mobile responsiveness.

import { CategoryGrid } from '@/components/docs/category-grid';

# Overlays

Overlays present supplementary workflows, context-sensitive details, and decision prompts above the primary page canvas. They enable Northwind Traders operators to complete focused sub-tasks without navigating away from their active workspace.

## Components

<CategoryGrid category="components/overlays" />

## Overlay decision guide

Use this decision matrix to select the appropriate overlay component:

| Component | Modality | Focus behavior | Mobile behavior | Ideal scenario |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **[Dialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dialog)** | Modal (backdrop) | Trapped; restored to trigger on close | Centered modal (or bottom sheet) | Multi-field creation forms, detailed entity edits, complex configuration. |
| **[AlertDialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/alert-dialog)** | Strict modal (no backdrop click) | Trapped; focuses cancel button | Centered alert dialog | Irreversible destructive actions (voiding invoices, deleting vendors). |
| **[Sheet](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet)** | Modal or non-modal | Trapped if modal; side drawer | Full-width slide-over drawer | Audit inspection trails, record side-panels, mobile filter drawers. |
| **[Popover](/ui/docs/components/overlays/popover)** | Non-modal (or light dismiss) | Tab navigation inside popup | Repositioned within viewport bounds | Rich interactive controls (date pickers, filter builders, color swatches). |
| **[DropdownMenu](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu)** | Non-modal menu | Arrow key navigation; roving focus | Touch-friendly menu items | Action lists, table row action menus ("View", "Download", "Refund"). |
| **[ContextMenu](/ui/docs/components/overlays/context-menu)** | Non-modal context menu | Arrow key navigation; roving focus | Replaced by row action button | Right-click shortcuts on table rows or desktop canvas nodes. |
| **[Tooltip](/ui/docs/components/overlays/tooltip)** | Non-modal informational | Never traps focus; hover / focus only | Hidden on touch (use long-press or tap) | Explanations for icon-only buttons, keyboard hotkey reminders. |
| **[CommandPalette](/ui/docs/components/overlays/command-palette)** | Modal search / launcher | Trapped inside search input | Full-screen mobile search modal | Global navigation (`⌘K`), quick entity lookups, workflow shortcuts. |

## Architectural rules for overlays

### 1. Nesting overlays
- **Permitted**: Opening an `AlertDialog` confirmation from within a `Dialog` (e.g. "Discard unsaved changes?"). Base UI and the design system properly manage the stacking context and trap focus in the topmost active modal.
- **Avoid**: Opening a `Dialog` from another `Dialog`. Prefer multi-step [Stepper](/ui/docs/components/navigation/stepper) wizards or full-page routing.
- **Dropdown menus inside dialogs**: Completely supported. Tooltips, popovers, and dropdown menus automatically port outside the dialog container using standard React portals into `document.body`.

### 2. Focus management
- **Trap focus**: All modal overlays (`Dialog`, `AlertDialog`, `Sheet`, `CommandPalette`) lock focus inside their container. Users cannot tab outside into the background document.
- **Restoration**: Closing an overlay via Escape, cancel buttons, or backdrop clicks always restores keyboard focus to the triggering element.
- **Initial focus**: Destructive alert dialogs focus the safe "Cancel" action first to prevent accidental confirmation by hitting Enter.

### 3. Mobile responsiveness
- Viewport width ceilings: On small screens (`< 640px`), full-width `Sheet` drawers or bottom-sliding dialog sheets provide superior ergonomics compared to cramped desktop popups.

---

## Popover (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/overlays/popover)

Small forms, share panels, and pickers that float next to their trigger without blocking background content.

<ComponentPreview name="overlays/popover/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Popover,
  PopoverTrigger,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverTitle,
  PopoverDescription,
  PopoverClose,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Popover` for rich, interactive controls anchored to a specific button or control that need to open in-place without navigating away:

- **Quick configuration panels**: Filter presets, column toggles, or inline item tagging in ERP records.
- **Share links or copyable details**: Sharing purchase orders, consignment links, or invoice tracking URLs.
- **Embedded mini-forms**: Adjusting order line quantities or applying prompt coupon codes.

**Do not use Popover for:**
- Short, non-interactive hover labels — use [Tooltip](/ui/docs/components/overlays/tooltip).
- Linear action menus or commands — use [DropdownMenu](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu).
- Critical workflows that require strict modality or large layout space — use [Dialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dialog) or [Sheet](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet).

## Examples

### Basic usage

A popover anchored to a share button providing an ERP purchase order link:

```tsx
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" startIcon={<Share2 />} />}>
    Share
  </PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent align="start" className="w-80">
    <PopoverTitle>Share order</PopoverTitle>
    <PopoverDescription>
      Anyone with the link can view this purchase order.
    </PopoverDescription>
    <div className="mt-3 flex gap-2">
      <Input size="sm" readOnly value="https://erp.northwind.in/orders/PO-2026-081" />
      <Button size="sm" variant="secondary">Copy</Button>
    </div>
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

### Positioning and alignments

`PopoverContent` accepts `side` (`top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`) and `align` (`start`, `center`, `end`). The popover automatically flips when close to viewport edges:

```tsx
<PopoverContent side="right" align="start" sideOffset={8}>
  <PopoverTitle>Delivery note details</PopoverTitle>
  <PopoverDescription>Dispatched via Blue Dart Express, Bengaluru hub.</PopoverDescription>
</PopoverContent>
```

### Mini-form inside popover

Wrap interactive controls in a popover with an explicit `PopoverClose` button:

```tsx
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" size="sm" />}>
    Adjust allocation
  </PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent className="w-72">
    <PopoverTitle>Stock allocation</PopoverTitle>
    <PopoverDescription>Update reserved inventory units.</PopoverDescription>
    <div className="mt-3 flex flex-col gap-3">
      <Field name="units">
        <FieldLabel>Units reserved</FieldLabel>
        <Input type="number" defaultValue={250} />
      </Field>
      <div className="flex justify-end gap-2">
        <PopoverClose render={<Button size="sm" variant="outline" />}>
          Cancel
        </PopoverClose>
        <Button size="sm">Save</Button>
      </div>
    </div>
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

## Accessibility

`Popover` is built on Base UI Popover primitives (`@base-ui/react/popover`).

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Opens or toggles the popover from the trigger button.' },
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus to the first focusable element inside the popover content.' },
    { key: 'Escape', action: 'Dismisses the popover and restores focus to the trigger element.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The `PopoverTrigger` receives `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded="true | false"`.
- When opened, focus shifts into the popover, and the popover container links to `PopoverTitle` and `PopoverDescription` via `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby`.
- Clicking outside or pressing `Escape` dismisses the popover and returns focus to the trigger.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Provide an explicit dismiss or action button when hosting input fields inside a popover.',
    code: `<PopoverClose render={<Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not place primary destructive actions inside a popover without modal confirmation.',
    code: `<Popover><Button variant="destructive">Delete ERP database</Button></Popover>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use Tooltip instead of Popover when simply providing an accessible label for an icon button.',
    code: `<Tooltip><TooltipTrigger>{icon}</TooltipTrigger><TooltipContent>Download PDF</TooltipContent></Tooltip>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not use Popover to show read-only one-word tooltips on hover.',
    code: `<Popover><PopoverTrigger>{icon}</PopoverTrigger><PopoverContent>Help</PopoverContent></Popover>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable
  components={[
    'Popover',
    'PopoverTrigger',
    'PopoverContent',
    'PopoverTitle',
    'PopoverDescription',
    'PopoverClose',
  ]}
  baseUi="popover"
/>

## Related

- [Tooltip](/ui/docs/components/overlays/tooltip) — Non-interactive short label on hover or keyboard focus.
- [DropdownMenu](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu) — List of actions and menu options anchored to a button.
- [Dialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dialog) — Modal window for complex workflows and forms.

---

## Sheet (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet)

Drawer overlay supporting four directional edges, RTL-aware logical sides, scrollable body containers, and master-detail responsiveness.

<ComponentPreview name="overlays/sheet/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Sheet,
  SheetTrigger,
  SheetContent,
  SheetHeader,
  SheetTitle,
  SheetDescription,
  SheetBody,
  SheetFooter,
  SheetClose,
  type SheetProps,
  type SheetContentProps,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Sheet` when an operator needs to inspect extensive record metadata or adjust complex filters while preserving their visual anchor on the underlying page:

- Filtering dense transactional tables (date ranges, warehouse zones, item statuses).
- Displaying purchase order audit logs, delivery manifests, and approval histories.
- Providing mobile-responsive detail panes when desktop views use a side-by-side [SplitPane](/ui/docs/components/layout/split-pane).

When choosing overlay surfaces:
- Use `Sheet` when content has substantial vertical length or acts as a supplementary inspection panel beside an active list.
- Use [Dialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dialog) for concise, centered creation forms that require the user's undivided attention.
- Use [Popover](/ui/docs/components/overlays/popover) for lightweight interactive menus anchored directly to a button.
- Refer to the [Overlay decision guide](/ui/docs/components/overlays#overlay-decision-guide) for full details.

## Examples

### Basic drawer with filters

Wrap content in `SheetHeader`, `SheetBody` (which scrolls automatically when contents exceed screen height), and `SheetFooter`:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import {
  Button,
  Field,
  FieldLabel,
  Input,
  Sheet,
  SheetBody,
  SheetClose,
  SheetContent,
  SheetDescription,
  SheetFooter,
  SheetHeader,
  SheetTitle,
  SheetTrigger,
} from '@innostes/ui';
import { Filter } from 'lucide-react';

export function OrderFiltersDrawer() {
  return (
    <Sheet>
      <SheetTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" startIcon={<Filter />} />}>
        Filters
      </SheetTrigger>
      <SheetContent side="right">
        <SheetHeader>
          <SheetTitle>Filter purchase orders</SheetTitle>
          <SheetDescription>
            Refine orders by vendor, delivery date, or warehouse depot.
          </SheetDescription>
        </SheetHeader>
        <SheetBody className="flex flex-col gap-4 py-4">
          <Field name="poNumber">
            <FieldLabel>PO identifier</FieldLabel>
            <Input placeholder="e.g. PO-8410" />
          </Field>
        </SheetBody>
        <SheetFooter>
          <SheetClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Reset</SheetClose>
          <Button type="button">Apply filters</Button>
        </SheetFooter>
      </SheetContent>
    </Sheet>
  );
}
```

### Responsive master-detail: Sheet on mobile versus SplitPane on desktop

In enterprise applications, master-detail interfaces should adapt to available viewport real estate. On wide desktop monitors (`>= 1024px`), render a persistent [SplitPane](/ui/docs/components/layout/split-pane) with list and details side-by-side. On mobile devices, render the list full-width and slide the detail inspection view over the screen via a `Sheet`:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { Sheet, SheetContent, SheetHeader, SheetTitle, SheetBody, SplitPane } from '@innostes/ui';

export function ResponsiveMasterDetail({ orders, isDesktop }) {
  const [activeOrder, setActiveOrder] = useState(null);

  if (isDesktop) {
    return (
      <SplitPane defaultSizes={[60, 40]} minSizes={[400, 320]}>
        <div>{/* Orders table */}</div>
        <div>{activeOrder && <OrderInspection order={activeOrder} />}</div>
      </SplitPane>
    );
  }

  return (
    <>
      <div>{/* Mobile orders list */}</div>
      <Sheet open={Boolean(activeOrder)} onOpenChange={(open) => !open && setActiveOrder(null)}>
        <SheetContent side="end">
          <SheetHeader>
            <SheetTitle>Order #{activeOrder?.id}</SheetTitle>
          </SheetHeader>
          <SheetBody>
            {activeOrder && <OrderInspection order={activeOrder} />}
          </SheetBody>
        </SheetContent>
      </Sheet>
    </>
  );
}
```

### Sliding sides and logical orientation

`SheetContent` accepts `side="top"`, `side="bottom"`, `side="left"`, or `side="right"`. For internationalized applications, use logical values `side="start"` and `side="end"` which automatically reverse sliding directions in right-to-left (RTL) locales:

```tsx
<SheetContent side="end">
  {/* Slides from right in LTR; slides from left in RTL */}
</SheetContent>
```

### Long scrollable body content

`SheetBody` is pre-styled with `flex-1 overflow-y-auto`, ensuring long forms or audit trails scroll smoothly while header and footer remain pinned in position:

```tsx
<SheetContent side="right">
  <SheetHeader>
    <SheetTitle>Consignment audit trail</SheetTitle>
  </SheetHeader>
  <SheetBody className="p-6">
    {/* 50+ activity log entries scroll here */}
  </SheetBody>
  <SheetFooter>
    <SheetClose render={<Button />}>Done</SheetClose>
  </SheetFooter>
</SheetContent>
```

## Accessibility

`Sheet` is built on Base UI Dialog primitives (`@base-ui/react/dialog`).

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Escape', action: 'Dismisses the slide-over sheet and returns focus to the triggering element.' },
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Cycles focus through interactive elements within the sheet container without escaping to background content.' },
  ]}
/>

### Focus trapping and restoration

- Upon opening, focus shifts to the first focusable element inside `SheetContent`.
- All background page content is marked `inert`, blocking pointer and keyboard navigation outside the drawer.
- Upon dismissal, focus returns to the `SheetTrigger` button.

### Screen readers

- Screen readers announce the drawer title via `SheetTitle` (`aria-labelledby`).
- The close button includes an accessible label (`closeLabel="Close"` by default).

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use Sheet for deep secondary inspection panels (such as item audit histories or extensive filter sidebars).',
    code: `<SheetContent side="end"><SheetBody>{auditLogs}</SheetBody></SheetContent>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not use Sheet for high-stakes destructive confirmations like "Delete company" (use AlertDialog).',
    code: `<Sheet><SheetTitle>Delete account?</SheetTitle></Sheet>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use logical sides (start / end) to ensure drawers slide from the correct margin in both LTR and RTL reading directions.',
    code: `<SheetContent side="end" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not hardcode physical side="right" when internationalizing for RTL languages (Arabic, Hebrew, Urdu).',
    code: `<SheetContent side="right" />`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable
  components={[
    'Sheet',
    'SheetTrigger',
    'SheetContent',
    'SheetHeader',
    'SheetTitle',
    'SheetDescription',
    'SheetBody',
    'SheetFooter',
    'SheetClose',
  ]}
  baseUi="dialog"
/>

## Related

- [Dialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dialog) — Centered modal window for focused forms.
- [SplitPane](/ui/docs/components/layout/split-pane) — Desktop side-by-side pane container.
- [Popover](/ui/docs/components/overlays/popover) — Non-modal contextual dropdown.

## Tooltip (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/overlays/tooltip)

Names icon buttons and shows shortcut hints with shared warm-up delay across toolbars.

<ComponentPreview name="overlays/tooltip/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Tooltip,
  TooltipTrigger,
  TooltipContent,
  TooltipProvider,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Tooltip` to clarify icon-only buttons or provide supplementary keyboard shortcut cues without cluttering the main user interface:

- **Icon-only toolbar controls**: Editing tools, table row shortcuts, or status indicators.
- **Truncated text hint**: Revealing full text when enterprise table cells truncate customer or vendor names.
- **Keyboard shortcut reminders**: Showing `⌘S` or `⌘K` alongside standard actions.

**Do not use Tooltip for:**
- Interactive content such as links or forms — use [Popover](/ui/docs/components/overlays/popover).
- Essential instructional information that touch-device users must read to complete a task.
- Lengthy multi-paragraph explanations — use an inline helper text or [Alert](/ui/docs/components/feedback/alert).

## Examples

### Basic usage

Providing an accessible name for an icon button:

```tsx
<Tooltip>
  <TooltipTrigger
    render={<Button iconOnly variant="ghost" aria-label="Archive purchase order" />}
  >
    <ArchiveIcon />
  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipContent>Archive purchase order</TooltipContent>
</Tooltip>
```

### Shared delay with TooltipProvider

Wrap your application root or toolbar in `TooltipProvider`. After the initial delay timer fires for the first tooltip, hovering over subsequent triggers displays their tooltips immediately without waiting:

```tsx
<TooltipProvider delay={300}>
  <div className="flex gap-1 rounded-md border p-1">
    <Tooltip>
      <TooltipTrigger render={<Button iconOnly variant="ghost" aria-label="Bold text" />}>
        <BoldIcon />
      </TooltipTrigger>
      <TooltipContent>Bold (⌘B)</TooltipContent>
    </Tooltip>
    <Tooltip>
      <TooltipTrigger render={<Button iconOnly variant="ghost" aria-label="Italic text" />}>
        <ItalicIcon />
      </TooltipTrigger>
      <TooltipContent>Italic (⌘I)</TooltipContent>
    </Tooltip>
  </div>
</TooltipProvider>
```

### Position and alignment

Tooltips can position along `top`, `bottom`, `left`, or `right` margins, and will flip dynamically to stay within the visible screen area:

```tsx
<TooltipContent side="bottom" align="center" sideOffset={6}>
  Export GST report (CSV)
</TooltipContent>
```

## Accessibility

`Tooltip` is built on Base UI Tooltip primitives (`@base-ui/react/tooltip`).

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus to the trigger button, which reveals the tooltip after delay.' },
    { key: 'Escape', action: 'Immediately dismisses the active tooltip without moving keyboard focus away.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- For icon-only buttons, always ensure the trigger element possesses an `aria-label`.
- `Tooltip` automatically associates the tooltip content with the trigger via `aria-describedby` when opened.
- Tooltips are not reachable on pure touch screen devices without focus emulation; essential business instructions must never be sequestered in a tooltip.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Ensure icon-only buttons have an explicit aria-label in addition to the tooltip for screen readers.',
    code: `<TooltipTrigger render={<Button iconOnly aria-label="Delete line" />}>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not rely on the tooltip alone as the only accessible label for an icon button.',
    code: `<TooltipTrigger render={<Button iconOnly />}>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Keep tooltip text concise (1–4 words) describing the action or shortcut.',
    code: `<TooltipContent>Export invoice (⌘E)</TooltipContent>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not place complex forms, links, or interactive elements inside a tooltip.',
    code: `<TooltipContent><a href="/docs">Read more in documentation</a></TooltipContent>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable
  components={[
    'Tooltip',
    'TooltipTrigger',
    'TooltipContent',
    'TooltipProvider',
  ]}
  baseUi="tooltip"
/>

## Related

- [Popover](/ui/docs/components/overlays/popover) — Rich interactive floating panel for forms and mini-dialogs.
- [Button](/ui/docs/components/actions/button) — Interactive button component frequently wrapped by tooltips.
- [DropdownMenu](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu) — Contextual action list opened by clicking.

## Dashboard (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/examples/dashboard)

An enterprise dashboard bringing together AppRail, Sidebar, TopBar, MetricCards, CartesianCharts, and widgets.

<ComponentPreview name="examples/dashboard" align="start" className="p-0 sm:p-0" />

## What's in it

This reference screen combines `@innostes/ui` layout primitives, widgets, and charting engines into a high-density operations dashboard for Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd:

| Section | Components |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Global Navigation** | [`AppRail`](/ui/docs/components/layout/app-rail) with persistent primary module icons |
| **Workspace Navigation** | [`Sidebar`](/ui/docs/components/layout/sidebar), `SidebarProvider`, `SidebarMenu`, `SidebarMenuItem` |
| **Top Header** | [`TopBar`](/ui/docs/components/layout/top-bar) with [`AppSwitcher`](/ui/docs/widgets/app-switcher), [`Notifications`](/ui/docs/widgets/notifications), and [`UserMenu`](/ui/docs/widgets/user-menu) |
| **Welcome Header** | [`WelcomeBanner`](/ui/docs/widgets/welcome-banner) with action shortcuts |
| **KPI Metrics** | [`MetricCard`](/ui/docs/widgets/metric-card) formatted for Indian numbering (`₹` Lakhs/Crores) |
| **Data Visualization** | [`CartesianCharts`](/ui/docs/charts/cartesian) wrapped in [`WidgetCard`](/ui/docs/widgets/widget-card) |
| **Operational Widgets** | [`QuickActions`](/ui/docs/widgets/quick-actions), [`EntityList`](/ui/docs/widgets/entity-list), [`ActivityFeed`](/ui/docs/widgets/activity-feed) |

## Responsive behaviour

- **Desktop (>= 1280px)**: The dual-tier navigation displays the full `AppRail` alongside an expanded 256px `Sidebar`. Widgets arrange across a 12-column analytical grid.
- **Tablet (768px – 1279px)**: The `Sidebar` automatically collapses to an icon rail (`state="collapsed"`). Widget cards adapt to two equal columns.
- **Mobile (< 768px)**: The `AppRail` and `Sidebar` transition to an accessible off-canvas drawer triggered by the `SidebarTrigger` in the header. Metric cards and widgets stack into a single vertical scroll stream.

## Accessibility notes

- **Landmark semantics**: The layout exposes landmark regions (`<nav aria-label="Global application rail">`, `<nav aria-label="Workspace sidebar">`, `<header>`, `<main id="main-content">`) allowing screen reader operators to jump between regions using landmark navigation keys.
- **Skip navigation**: Includes a [`SkipLink`](/ui/docs/components/navigation/breadcrumb) targeting `#main-content` at the top of the tab order.
- **Keyboard focus**: When the mobile drawer opens, keyboard focus moves to the close button and remains trapped within the navigation drawer until dismissed.

## Employee Directory (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/examples/employee-directory)

Enterprise personnel directory with SplitPane desktop layout, mobile Sheet inspector, departmental TreeView, and contact cards.

<ComponentPreview name="examples/employee-directory" align="start" className="p-0 sm:p-0" />

## What's in it

This reference screen demonstrates master-detail navigation for enterprise employee records across Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd regional hubs:

| Section | Components |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Desktop Master-Detail** | [`SplitPane`](/ui/docs/components/layout/split-pane) with fluid percentage splits and resizer separator |
| **Mobile Drawer Inspector** | [`Sheet`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet) sliding out from the right on viewports under 1024px |
| **Department Hierarchy** | [`TreeView`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/tree-view) with collapsible department nodes and headcount badges |
| **Employee Selection List** | Semantic `role="listbox"` with keyboard selection and active state styling |
| **Identity & Avatars** | [`Avatar`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/avatar), [`AvatarFallback`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/avatar) rendering calculated initials |
| **Profile Breakdown** | [`Card`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/card) grouping organizational tenure and direct contact channels |
| **Filter & Search** | [`Input`](/ui/docs/components/forms/input) with search icon prefix |

## Responsive behaviour

- **Desktop (>= 1024px)**: Renders a horizontal [`SplitPane`](/ui/docs/components/layout/split-pane). The left pane contains the search filter, department TreeView, and scrollable personnel list. The right pane displays the active profile details.
- **Tablet & Mobile (< 1024px)**: Transitions cleanly to a full-width list. Tapping any associate row slides out a right-hand [`Sheet`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet) drawer containing their full profile and direct action buttons.

## Accessibility notes

- **Listbox semantics**: The associate list exposes `role="listbox"` with each record rendering as `role="option"` and carrying `aria-selected` reflecting active selection.
- **Roving keyboard focus**: Operators can navigate the employee list using <kbd>Arrow Up</kbd> and <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> keys and activate records via <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd>.
- **Resizer separator**: The [`SplitPane`](/ui/docs/components/layout/split-pane) divider exposes `role="separator"` with keyboard accessibility via arrow keys.

## Hiring Pipeline (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/examples/hiring-pipeline)

Recruitment board with multi-stage Kanban columns, drag-and-drop moves, salary indicators, and slide-out candidate Sheet.

<ComponentPreview name="examples/hiring-pipeline" align="start" className="p-0 sm:p-0" />

## What's in it

This reference screen demonstrates talent recruitment and candidate workflow tracking for supply chain personnel at Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd:

| Section | Components |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Pipeline Scaffolding** | [`KanbanBoard`](/ui/docs/widgets/kanban-board) with 5 recruitment stages (Applied, Screening, Technical, Offer, Hired) |
| **Candidate Cards** | Custom card layout with candidate name, role, expected CTC in INR Lakhs, rating stars, and avatar |
| **Candidate Identity** | [`Avatar`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/avatar), [`AvatarFallback`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/avatar) |
| **Stage Badges & Dots** | Color-coded status dots (`tone`) identifying stage urgency and progression |
| **Candidate Inspector** | [`Sheet`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet) slide-out drawer displaying candidate experience, notice periods, and interviewer notes |
| **Action Triggers** | [`Button`](/ui/docs/components/actions/button) to advance candidates to the subsequent pipeline stage |
| **Move Notifications** | [`toast`](/ui/docs/components/feedback/toast) announcing stage transitions upon card drop |

## Responsive behaviour

- **Desktop (>= 1280px)**: All 5 Kanban columns display side-by-side with full card previews. Drag-and-drop interactions work via mouse or keyboard shortcuts.
- **Tablet & Mobile (< 1280px)**: The board enables smooth horizontal swipe scrolling. Tapping any candidate card slides out the candidate details in the full-height mobile [`Sheet`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet).

## Accessibility notes

- **Keyboard drag-and-drop**: In addition to mouse dragging, [`KanbanBoard`](/ui/docs/widgets/kanban-board) supports complete keyboard reordering: press <kbd>Space</kbd> to pick up a card, use <kbd>Arrow</kbd> keys to move across columns, and press <kbd>Space</kbd> to drop.
- **Live region announcements**: All pickup, move, drop, and cancel events trigger accessible announcements through polite live regions.
- **Sheet drawer focus**: When a candidate card is activated, focus transitions into the candidate details sheet and returns to the triggering card when dismissed.

## Invoice Detail (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/examples/invoice-detail)

Detailed transaction invoice inspector with PageHeader breadcrumbs, fiscal summaries, line items, ChangeLog audit, and AlertDialog.

<ComponentPreview name="examples/invoice-detail" align="start" className="p-0 sm:p-0" />

## What's in it

This reference screen provides a transactional review workspace for single tax invoices, bringing together fiscal summaries, statutory line items, audit logs, and irreversible payment settlement workflows:

| Section | Components |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Page Header** | [`PageHeader`](/ui/docs/components/layout/page-header) with breadcrumbs navigation and download/action triggers |
| **Status Tag** | [`Badge`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/badge) reflecting real-time settlement status |
| **Fiscal Summaries** | [`Card`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/card) grid detailing total invoice value, customer GSTIN, issue date, and place of supply |
| **Line Items** | Semantic [`Table`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/table) with item description, HSN codes, quantity, unit rates, and GST subtotals |
| **Audit Lifecycle** | [`ChangeLog`](/ui/docs/widgets/change-log) documenting author, role, timestamp, and GSTN portal filing history |
| **Settlement Confirmation** | [`AlertDialog`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/alert-dialog) providing a two-phase confirmation modal before ledger posting |
| **Toast Confirmation** | [`toast`](/ui/docs/components/feedback/toast) providing immediate asynchronous mutation feedback |

## Responsive behaviour

- **Desktop (>= 1024px)**: Top metrics render in a 4-column balanced card grid. Line items display all 6 columns (Description, HSN, Qty, Rate, Tax, Total) without truncation.
- **Tablet (640px – 1023px)**: Fiscal metrics re-flow into a 2x2 grid. Table allows horizontal scrolling with sticky headers.
- **Mobile (< 640px)**: Action buttons stack below the title. Metrics cards render full-width vertically.

## Accessibility notes

- **Confirmation semantics**: The settlement dialogue uses `role="alertdialog"` to announce high-consequence fiscal commitments to assistive technologies with immediate priority.
- **Focus entrapment**: While the confirmation dialogue is open, keyboard focus remains trapped within the modal boundary until confirmed or cancelled via <kbd>Escape</kbd>.
- **Table summary semantics**: Line item calculations are grouped into `<tbody>` rows with clear `colSpan` totals, allowing screen reader operators to follow accounting hierarchies.

| Section | Components |

| **Filtering Toolbar** | [`Input`](/ui/docs/components/forms/input) with search icon prefix, [`Select`](/ui/docs/components/forms/select) for status segmentation |
| **Batch Action Bar** | Contextual banner rendered conditionally when rows are selected, with bulk reminder and export triggers |

## Accessibility notes

- **Selection semantics**: The master checkbox in the header reflects `aria-checked="mixed"` when a partial subset of rows is selected. Individual row checkboxes carry descriptive `aria-label` tags including invoice numbers.
- **Search debounce**: Search input updates announce results politely via live regions without interrupting screen reader speech mid-keystroke.
- **Row action menus**: Each row menu button exposes an explicit accessible label (e.g. `aria-label="Actions for INV-2026-0801"`).

## Roles and Permissions (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/examples/roles-and-permissions)

Access control management screen with custom and system role listings, member headcounts, and PermissionMatrix grid.

<ComponentPreview name="examples/roles-and-permissions" align="start" className="p-0 sm:p-0" />

## What's in it

This reference screen demonstrates enterprise Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) policy administration for Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd:

| Section | Components |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Header Bar** | Page title, description, and primary Save permissions [`Button`](/ui/docs/components/actions/button) |
| **Role Navigation** | Interactive [`Card`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/card) list displaying role titles, descriptions, member counts, and badges |
| **System & Custom Tags** | [`Badge`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/badge) distinguishing immutable system roles from tenant custom roles |
| **Access Matrix Grid** | [`PermissionMatrix`](/ui/docs/widgets/permission-matrix) with sticky resource column and bulk toggles |
| **Policy Notifications** | [`toast`](/ui/docs/components/feedback/toast) confirming committed security policies |

## Responsive behaviour

- **Desktop (>= 1024px)**: Dual-column layout with the role selection cards on the left (4 columns) and the interactive `PermissionMatrix` on the right (8 columns).
- **Tablet & Mobile (< 1024px)**: Stacks into a single column. The matrix container enables smooth horizontal scrolling with the resource label column frozen (`stickyColumn={true}`).

## Accessibility notes

- **Matrix semantics**: The [`PermissionMatrix`](/ui/docs/widgets/permission-matrix) renders a semantic `<table>` with associated `scope="row"` and `scope="col"` headers. Checkboxes carry programmatic labels combining action and resource.
- **System role immutability**: For system roles, checkboxes render with `disabled` or `readOnly` attributes, preventing unauthorized mutations while maintaining keyboard focusability.
- **Bulk toggle announcements**: Clicking column or row headers announces the updated bulk permission state politely to screen readers.

Multi-section enterprise configuration screen with FormSection, FormGrid, Switches, Selects, and sticky unsaved-changes save bar.

| Section | Components |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Section Scaffolding** | [`FormSection`](/ui/docs/components/layout/form-layout) grouping related preferences with titles and descriptions |
| **Responsive Grid** | [`FormGrid`](/ui/docs/components/layout/form-layout) providing fluid 2-column input layouts on desktop and single-column on mobile |
| **Accessible Fields** | [`Field`](/ui/docs/components/forms/field), [`FieldLabel`](/ui/docs/components/forms/field), [`FieldDescription`](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) |

- **Desktop (>= 768px)**: Inputs inside `FormGrid` sit in balanced pairs or span full width based on `sm:col-span-2` utility classes. The floating save bar floats centered with a max-width of 576px.

- **Switch labels**: Every [`Switch`](/ui/docs/components/forms/switch) includes an explicit programmatic `aria-label` attribute matching its visible section title.
- **Unsaved change warnings**: When the floating save bar mounts upon field modification, the status text is announced via live region to prevent inadvertent data loss.
- **Keyboard navigation**: Operators can navigate the entire settings form and commit updates without leaving the keyboard via standard <kbd>Tab</kbd> and <kbd>Enter</kbd> controls.
