## Create, edit, and delete flows (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/patterns/crud-flows)

Enterprise CRUD workflows with optimistic state mutations, destructive confirmations, and rollback toasts.

Enterprise ERP platforms handle business records—such as vendor purchase agreements, product inventories, and tax invoices—that require deterministic state transitions. This guide covers how to implement create, edit, and delete (CRUD) workflows using `@innostes/ui` primitives with optimistic updates, accessible confirmation dialogues, inline error recovery, and undo capabilities.

## The problem

CRUD workflows in mission-critical software encounter several recurring UX and operational hazards:
1. **Destructive accidents without recourse**: Deleting a vendor agreement or archival record with a single click leads to immediate data loss and operational interruption.
2. **Sluggish mutation feedback**: Waiting for round-trip network requests before reflecting UI state changes creates a perceived latency penalty for high-volume data clerks.
3. **Disjointed error feedback**: Showing generic modal errors or ephemeral toasts when a specific field fails server-side validation disconnects the operator from the root cause.
4. **Permanent vs soft deletions**: Lack of a short undo window prevents operators from recovering from unintended destructive gestures.

## Recommended approach

- **Two-phase destructive confirmation**: Always guard permanent removals behind an [`AlertDialog`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/alert-dialog) with `variant="destructive"` to force deliberate cognitive confirmation.
- **Optimistic UI with rollback**: Mutate local React state or query cache immediately upon user submission. If the server mutation rejects, revert state and surface an actionable error [`toast`](/ui/docs/components/feedback/toast).
- **Inline errors for validation, toasts for system status**: Use [`FieldError`](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) within the active form for schema validation failures. Reserve toasts for asynchronous background events (e.g. "Vendor deleted", "Invoice draft saved").
- **Transient undo windows**: When executing non-critical deletions, provide a 5-second `action` callback within the confirmation toast that restores the record before the mutation finalises.

## Workflow architecture: List → Detail → Edit

The canonical Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd record flow balances discoverability and focused data editing:

```
[List View (/vendors)]
  │
  ├─ [Create Drawer / Modal] ──(Save)──> Optimistic Insert → Background Sync
  │
  ▼
[Detail View (/vendors/:id)]
  │
  ├─ [Inline / Sheet Edit] ─────(Save)──> Optimistic Patch → Rollback on Failure
  │
  └─ [Delete Button] ──────────(Trigger)
        │
        ▼
     [AlertDialog] ──────────(Confirm)─> Optimistic Removal → Undo Toast
```

## Complete example: Vendor management with optimistic deletion and undo

The following production recipe demonstrates an active vendor registry screen with optimistic deletions and undo toasts:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import {
  Button,
  Card,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
  CardDescription,
  CardContent,
  Badge,
  toast,
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogClose,
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuSeparator,
} from '@innostes/ui';
import { MoreHorizontal, Trash2, Edit2, RotateCcw, Building2 } from 'lucide-react';

interface VendorRecord {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  gstin: string;
  category: string;
  status: 'active' | 'archived';
  outstandingBalance: number;
}

const INITIAL_VENDORS: VendorRecord[] = [
  {
    id: 'VND-2041',
    name: 'Kirloskar Electric Co Ltd',
    gstin: '29AAACK1940P1ZB',
    category: 'Heavy Machinery',
    status: 'active',
    outstandingBalance: 485000,
  },
  {
    id: 'VND-2042',
    name: 'Mysore Sandal Oil Mills',
    gstin: '29AABCM8291Q1ZH',
    category: 'Raw Materials',
    status: 'active',
    outstandingBalance: 124000,
  },
  {
    id: 'VND-2043',
    name: 'Bengaluru Logistics Terminal',
    gstin: '29AACBL3019R1ZM',
    category: 'Freight Services',
    status: 'active',
    outstandingBalance: 67200,
  },
];

export function VendorCrudScreen() {
  const [vendors, setVendors] = useState<VendorRecord[]>(INITIAL_VENDORS);
  const [vendorToDelete, setVendorToDelete] = useState<VendorRecord | null>(null);

  // Optimistic delete with undo toast
  const handleConfirmDelete = async () => {
    if (!vendorToDelete) return;
    const target = vendorToDelete;
    const originalVendors = [...vendors];

    // 1. Optimistic removal
    setVendors((current) => current.filter((v) => v.id !== target.id));
    setVendorToDelete(null);

    // 2. Track undo status
    let undone = false;

    // 3. Trigger notification with undo action
    toast({
      title: 'Vendor archived',
      description: `${target.name} (${target.id}) was moved to archives.`,
      action: {
        label: 'Undo',
        onClick: () => {
          undone = true;
          setVendors(originalVendors);
          toast({
            title: 'Action restored',
            description: `${target.name} has been restored to active records.`,
          });
        },
      },
    });

    // 4. Background server dispatch after undo window elapses
    setTimeout(async () => {
      if (undone) return;
      try {
        // Mock server mutation: await fetch(`/api/vendors/${target.id}`, { method: 'DELETE' });
      } catch (err) {
        // Rollback state if server mutation rejects
        setVendors(originalVendors);
        toast({
          title: 'Mutation failed',
          description: `Unable to archive ${target.name}. Server changes were reverted.`,
          variant: 'destructive',
        });
      }
    }, 5000);
  };

  return (
    <div className="space-y-6">
      <div className="flex items-center justify-between">
        <div>
          <h2 className="text-xl font-semibold text-foreground">Vendor directory</h2>
          <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
            Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd active vendor accounts and procurement contracts.
          </p>
        </div>
        <Button variant="primary">Add vendor</Button>
      </div>

      <div className="grid gap-4 md:grid-cols-3">
        {vendors.map((vendor) => (
          <Card key={vendor.id}>
            <CardHeader className="flex flex-row items-start justify-between pb-2">
              <div className="space-y-1">
                <CardTitle className="text-base font-medium">{vendor.name}</CardTitle>
                <CardDescription>{vendor.gstin}</CardDescription>
              </div>
              <DropdownMenu>
                <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
                  <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" aria-label={`Actions for ${vendor.name}`}>
                    <MoreHorizontal className="h-4 w-4" />
                  </Button>
                </DropdownMenuTrigger>
                <DropdownMenuContent align="end">
                  <DropdownMenuItem>
                    <Edit2 className="mr-2 h-4 w-4" />
                    Edit record
                  </DropdownMenuItem>
                  <DropdownMenuSeparator />
                  <DropdownMenuItem
                    className="text-destructive focus:text-destructive"
                    onClick={() => setVendorToDelete(vendor)}
                  >
                    <Trash2 className="mr-2 h-4 w-4" />
                    Archive vendor
                  </DropdownMenuItem>
                </DropdownMenuContent>
              </DropdownMenu>
            </CardHeader>
            <CardContent>
              <div className="flex items-center justify-between text-sm">
                <span className="text-muted-foreground">Outstanding</span>
                <span className="font-semibold text-foreground">
                  ₹{vendor.outstandingBalance.toLocaleString('en-IN')}
                </span>
              </div>
              <div className="mt-2 flex items-center justify-between text-xs text-muted-foreground">
                <span>{vendor.category}</span>
                <Badge variant="outline">{vendor.status}</Badge>
              </div>
            </CardContent>
          </Card>
        ))}
      </div>

      {/* Accessible destructive confirmation dialogue */}
      <AlertDialog
        open={Boolean(vendorToDelete)}
        onOpenChange={(open) => !open && setVendorToDelete(null)}
      >
        <AlertDialogContent>
          <AlertDialogHeader>
            <AlertDialogTitle>Archive vendor account?</AlertDialogTitle>
            <AlertDialogDescription>
              This will suspend purchase order authorisations for{' '}
              <strong>{vendorToDelete?.name}</strong>. Pending invoices totaling ₹
              {vendorToDelete?.outstandingBalance.toLocaleString('en-IN')} will remain in the settlement ledger.
            </AlertDialogDescription>
          </AlertDialogHeader>
          <AlertDialogFooter>
            <AlertDialogClose asChild>
              <Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
            </AlertDialogClose>
            <Button variant="destructive" onClick={handleConfirmDelete}>
              Confirm archive
            </Button>
          </AlertDialogFooter>
        </AlertDialogContent>
      </AlertDialog>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Feedback matrix: Toasts vs inline messages

Select the appropriate communication channel based on operational impact and urgency:

| Scenario | Component | Placement | Rationale |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Validation failure** | [`FieldError`](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) | Directly beneath invalid input | Maintains visual focus and `aria-describedby` linkage. |
| **Asynchronous success** | [`toast`](/ui/docs/components/feedback/toast) | Screen corner viewport | Unobtrusive notification confirming background completion without blocking screen tasks. |
| **Destructive action** | [`AlertDialog`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/alert-dialog) | Modal overlay with backdrop | Enforces modal focus trap and keyboard confirmation. |
| **Systemic outage** | [`Alert`](/ui/docs/components/feedback/alert) | Page header banner | Persistent visibility for wide service degradation or read-only modes. |

## Accessibility notes

- **Focus restoration after deletion**: When removing an item from a list or grid, move keyboard focus to the next logical sibling item, or to the container header if the list becomes empty. Never drop focus to the root `<body>` element.
- **Dialogue semantics**: Use [`AlertDialog`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/alert-dialog) rather than generic [`Dialog`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dialog) for destructive confirmations so assistive software identifies the role as `alertdialog` and announces the prompt with urgency.
- **Undo notifications**: Ensure toast notifications containing interactive action buttons announce through polite live regions (`aria-live="polite"`), and provide keyboard access via the standard tab order.

## Common mistakes

- **Hiding deletion failures**: Swallowing network rejection errors after an optimistic removal causes the UI to drift out of sync with the database. Always retain the prior snapshot and restore it upon error.
- **Using browser window alerts**: Calling native `window.confirm()` or `window.alert()` freezes script execution, breaks design system theming, and fails automated accessibility audits.
- **Overusing toasts for form validation**: Emitting five separate toasts for five invalid fields clutters the interface and disorients the user. Keep field-level errors inline with inputs.

## Related components

- [`AlertDialog`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/alert-dialog) — Accessible modal dialogues for high-stakes operational confirmations.
- [`Toast`](/ui/docs/components/feedback/toast) — Non-modal notifications with optional action callbacks.
- [`DropdownMenu`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu) — Contextual action menus for record listings.
- [`Card`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/card) — Structured containers for entity summaries.

---

## Dashboards (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/patterns/dashboards)

High-density executive and operational dashboard layouts with MetricCard, WidgetCard, charts, and date filtering.

Operational dashboards in enterprise ERP environments aggregate mission-critical KPIs, real-time inventory levels, and financial transaction telemetry. This guide shows how to compose modular dashboard screens using [`MetricCard`](/ui/docs/widgets/metric-card), [`WidgetCard`](/ui/docs/widgets/widget-card), [`CartesianChart`](/ui/docs/charts/cartesian), and [`DonutChart`](/ui/docs/charts/donut), handling per-widget loading and error states, auto-refresh polling, and global date range controls.

## The problem

Enterprise dashboards frequently present three key implementation problems:
1. **Monolithic data fetching**: Fetching all dashboard data in a single massive API payload stalls the entire page if one peripheral widget query encounters database locks.
2. **Layout instability**: Metrics and charts jump across viewports as asynchronous endpoints resolve at unpredictable intervals.
3. **Inaccessible charts**: Screen readers and keyboard operators cannot inspect graphical data points, violating statutory accessibility mandates.
4. **Stale operational data**: Warehouse dispatchers and procurement leads must manually refresh the browser to detect newly logged purchase orders.

## Recommended approach

- **Isolated widget queries**: Decouple metric and chart fetching. Each widget component loads independently, allowing instant rendering of cached metrics while complex financial aggregations compute in the background.
- **Consistent widget wrapper**: Standardise all panels with [`WidgetCard`](/ui/docs/widgets/widget-card), leveraging its built-in loading skeletons, empty state announcements, and error retry triggers.
- **Global filter synchronization**: Manage dashboard date ranges (`fiscalYear`, `quarter`, or `custom`) at the page container level, cascading updates downward via props or URL search params.
- **Accessible tabular alternatives**: Pair every visualization with an accessible hidden data table (`sr-only` or toggleable) so assistive technology users can parse figures.

## Layout composition blueprint

A standard 12-column responsive grid ensures visual balance across executive KPI strips and operational charts:

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Global Header: Fiscal Date Range Selector | Warehouse Selector | Auto-Refresh │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ [ MetricCard 1 ] │ [ MetricCard 2 ] │ [ MetricCard 3 ] │ [ MetricCard 4 ] │
│ 3 cols (desktop) │ 3 cols (desktop) │ 3 cols (desktop) │ 3 cols (desktop) │
├──────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────┤
│ [ WidgetCard: CartesianChart ]       │ [ WidgetCard: DonutChart ]      │
│ 8 columns (Revenue vs Expenditure)   │ 4 columns (Category Breakdown)  │
├──────────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────┤
│ [ WidgetCard: High-Priority Action List / Recent Purchase Orders ]      │
│ 12 columns                                                             │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Complete example: Northwind Operations Dashboard

Below is a complete implementation of the daily procurement and inventory dashboard for Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import {
  MetricCard,
  WidgetCard,
  CartesianChart,
  DonutChart,
  Button,
  Select,
  Badge,
} from '@innostes/ui';
import { RefreshCw, TrendingUp, AlertTriangle, ArrowUpRight } from 'lucide-react';

// Monthly procurement telemetry (en-IN currency formatting)
const REVENUE_DATA = [
  { month: 'Apr', budget: 4200000, actual: 3950000 },
  { month: 'May', budget: 4500000, actual: 4620000 },
  { month: 'Jun', budget: 4800000, actual: 4410000 },
  { month: 'Jul', budget: 5100000, actual: 5280000 },
  { month: 'Aug', budget: 5300000, actual: 5190000 },
  { month: 'Sep', budget: 5600000, actual: 5780000 },
];

// Inventory allocation by regional warehouse
const WAREHOUSE_DATA = [
  { name: 'Bengaluru Central Hub', value: 14200000, color: 'hsl(var(--primary))' },
  { name: 'Chennai Port Depot', value: 9800000, color: 'hsl(var(--chart-2))' },
  { name: 'Hyderabad Distribution', value: 6400000, color: 'hsl(var(--chart-3))' },
  { name: 'Kochi Terminal', value: 3100000, color: 'hsl(var(--chart-4))' },
];

export function OperationsDashboard() {
  const [fiscalRange, setFiscalRange] = useState('FY26-Q2');
  const [isRefreshing, setIsRefreshing] = useState(false);

  const handleManualRefresh = () => {
    setIsRefreshing(true);
    setTimeout(() => setIsRefreshing(false), 800);
  };

  return (
    <div className="space-y-6">
      {/* 1. Global Controls Bar */}
      <div className="flex flex-col sm:flex-row items-start sm:items-center justify-between gap-4 border-b pb-4">
        <div>
          <h1 className="text-2xl font-bold tracking-tight text-foreground">Procurement telemetry</h1>
          <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
            Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd – Southern Distribution Zone
          </p>
        </div>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
          <Select
            value={fiscalRange}
            onValueChange={setFiscalRange}
            options={[
              { value: 'FY26-Q1', label: 'FY 2026-27 Q1 (Apr-Jun)' },
              { value: 'FY26-Q2', label: 'FY 2026-27 Q2 (Jul-Sep)' },
              { value: 'FY26-Q3', label: 'FY 2026-27 Q3 (Oct-Dec)' },
            ]}
            aria-label="Filter fiscal quarter"
          />
          <Button
            variant="outline"
            size="sm"
            onClick={handleManualRefresh}
            disabled={isRefreshing}
            aria-label="Refresh dashboard data"
          >
            <RefreshCw className={`h-4 w-4 mr-2 ${isRefreshing ? 'animate-spin' : ''}`} />
            Refresh
          </Button>
        </div>
      </div>

      {/* 2. Top-level KPI Strips */}
      <div className="grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4">
        <MetricCard
          title="Active purchase commitments"
          value="₹3,41,80,000"
          change={{ value: '+14.2%', trend: 'up' }}
          description="Compared to prior fiscal quarter"
        />
        <MetricCard
          title="Consignment clearance rate"
          value="96.4%"
          change={{ value: '+2.1%', trend: 'up' }}
          description="Customs Port & Logistics gate"
        />
        <MetricCard
          title="Vendor payment turnaround"
          value="18.2 days"
          change={{ value: '-3.4 days', trend: 'down' }}
          description="Avg settlement duration"
        />
        <MetricCard
          title="Exceptions requiring audit"
          value="7"
          change={{ value: '+2', trend: 'neutral' }}
          description="Three-way match discrepancies"
        />
      </div>

      {/* 3. Deep Analytical Visualizations */}
      <div className="grid gap-6 lg:grid-cols-12">
        {/* Main Spending Trajectory Chart */}
        <div className="lg:col-span-8">
          <WidgetCard
            title="Procurement budget vs actual expenditure"
            description="Monthly expenditure comparison against allocated zone capital (₹ Lakhs)"
            loading={isRefreshing}
          >
            <div className="h-[320px] w-full pt-4">
              <CartesianChart
                data={REVENUE_DATA}
                categories={['budget', 'actual']}
                index="month"
                valueFormatter={(val) => `₹${(val / 100000).toFixed(1)}L`}
                colors={['hsl(var(--muted-foreground))', 'hsl(var(--primary))']}
              />
            </div>
          </WidgetCard>
        </div>

        {/* Warehouse Inventory Breakdown */}
        <div className="lg:col-span-4">
          <WidgetCard
            title="Inventory allocation"
            description="Stock asset value by zonal distribution depot"
            loading={isRefreshing}
          >
            <div className="h-[320px] w-full flex items-center justify-center">
              <DonutChart
                data={WAREHOUSE_DATA}
                category="value"
                index="name"
                valueFormatter={(val) => `₹${(val / 10000000).toFixed(2)} Cr`}
              />
            </div>
          </WidgetCard>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility notes

- **High-contrast chart palettes**: Chart color assignments use CSS custom properties linked to design tokens (`hsl(var(--primary))`, `hsl(var(--chart-2))`). Ensure neighbouring segments maintain a 3:1 minimum contrast ratio.
- **Screen reader data tables**: When rendering visual charts, include a hidden `table` element using CSS `.sr-only` detailing category keys and numeric quantities, or render an accessible summary paragraph.
- **Keyboard focus within widgets**: Provide logical tab stops for widget action menus and maximize controls. Ensure widget cards do not trap focus inside chart SVG containers.

## Common mistakes

- **Unbound polling loops**: Running aggressive `setInterval` requests every 2 seconds without checking browser document visibility (`document.visibilityState === 'visible'`) wastes server bandwidth when operators leave tabs backgrounded.
- **Full dashboard layout shifts**: Unmounting entire widget structures during background data re-fetching causes disruptive layout reflow. Always use inline skeletons or subtle loading overlays.
- **Overcrowding single views**: Squeezing more than 6 primary charts onto a single dashboard degrades cognitive readability. Segment operational views with tabs or dedicated routing.

## Related components

- [`MetricCard`](/ui/docs/widgets/metric-card) — Formatted KPI metric display with percentage trend indicators.
- [`WidgetCard`](/ui/docs/widgets/widget-card) — Standardized dashboard container with title, description, and state slots.
- [`CartesianCharts`](/ui/docs/charts/cartesian) — High-performance SVG bar, line, and area charts.
- [`DonutChart`](/ui/docs/charts/donut) — Radial proportional asset distributions.

## Forms and validation (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/patterns/forms-and-validation)

Client and server form validation patterns with React Hook Form, Zod, and Next.js Server Actions.

Enterprise ERP forms handle sensitive fiscal calculations, statutory compliance (such as GSTIN and PAN verification), and multi-step workflows. This guide demonstrates how to build resilient, accessible forms using `@innostes/ui` form primitives paired with React Hook Form, Zod schema validation, and Next.js Server Actions.

## The problem

Form implementations in enterprise software frequently suffer from three critical flaws:
1. **Disconnected validation state**: Errors caught on the server fail to associate with the corresponding input DOM element, leaving screen reader operators stranded without accessible announcements.
2. **Loss of unsaved progress**: Operators accidentally navigate away from deep 20-field procurement forms, discarding unsubmitted input without warning.
3. **Overly aggressive validation**: Showing validation error messages before the operator has finished typing into an input field (poor input ergonomics).

## Recommended approach

- **Colocate schema definitions**: Define a single Zod schema shared between client validation and server action handlers.
- **Accessible form primitives**: Wrap each control in [`Field`](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) (`FieldLabel`, `FieldDescription`, `FieldError`) to guarantee automated `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, and error ring associations.
- **Graceful validation triggers**: Validate on blur or submit rather than every keystroke (`mode: 'onTouched'`).
- **Confirmation dialogs**: Intercept window unload and router transitions with [`AlertDialog`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/alert-dialog) when forms are dirty.

## Complete example: Purchase order creation with React Hook Form & Zod

Below is a complete implementation of a purchase order form for Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd, including client schema validation and server action dispatch:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { useForm, Controller } from 'react-hook-form';
import { zodResolver } from '@hookform/resolvers/zod';
import { z } from 'zod';
import {
  Field,
  FieldLabel,
  FieldDescription,
  FieldError,
  Input,
  Select,
  Textarea,
  Button,
  FormGrid,
  FormActions,
  toast,
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogClose,
} from '@innostes/ui';

// 1. Unified Zod validation schema
const purchaseOrderSchema = z.object({
  poNumber: z
    .string()
    .min(5, 'PO number must be at least 5 characters')
    .regex(/^PO-\d{4}-\d{3,4}$/, 'Must follow format PO-YYYY-NNN (e.g. PO-2026-081)'),
  vendorGstin: z
    .string()
    .regex(/^[0-9]{2}[A-Z]{5}[0-9]{4}[A-Z]{1}[1-9A-Z]{1}Z[0-9A-Z]{1}$/, 'Invalid 15-character Indian GSTIN format'),
  expectedAmount: z
    .number({ invalid_type_error: 'Amount is required' })
    .positive('Order value must be greater than zero'),
  deliveryNotes: z
    .string()
    .max(500, 'Notes cannot exceed 500 characters')
    .optional(),
});

type PurchaseOrderFormValues = z.infer<typeof purchaseOrderSchema>;

export function PurchaseOrderForm({ onSubmitAction }: { onSubmitAction: (data: PurchaseOrderFormValues) => Promise<{ success: boolean; serverErrors?: Record<string, string> }> }) {
  const [isSubmitting, setIsSubmitting] = useState(false);
  const [discardDialogOpen, setDiscardDialogOpen] = useState(false);

  const {
    register,
    handleSubmit,
    setError,
    reset,
    formState: { errors, isDirty },
  } = useForm<PurchaseOrderFormValues>({
    resolver: zodResolver(purchaseOrderSchema),
    mode: 'onTouched',
    defaultValues: {
      poNumber: 'PO-2026-081',
      vendorGstin: '29ABCDE1234F1Z5',
      expectedAmount: 89400,
      deliveryNotes: '',
    },
  });

  const onFormSubmit = async (values: PurchaseOrderFormValues) => {
    setIsSubmitting(true);
    try {
      const result = await onSubmitAction(values);
      if (!result.success && result.serverErrors) {
        // Map server-side rejection keys to individual form fields
        for (const [field, message] of Object.entries(result.serverErrors)) {
          setError(field as keyof PurchaseOrderFormValues, { type: 'server', message });
        }
        toast.error('Submission failed. Check highlighted fields.');
      } else {
        toast.success(`Purchase order ${values.poNumber} created successfully`);
        reset(values); // clear dirty state
      }
    } catch {
      toast.error('Network failure communicating with procurement API.');
    } finally {
      setIsSubmitting(false);
    }
  };

  return (
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit(onFormSubmit)} className="space-y-6">
      <FormGrid columns={2}>
        <Field invalid={Boolean(errors.poNumber)}>
          <FieldLabel htmlFor="poNumber">PO number</FieldLabel>
          <Input
            id="poNumber"
            {...register('poNumber')}
            disabled={isSubmitting}
            placeholder="PO-2026-081"
          />
          <FieldDescription>Standard Northwind fiscal identifier.</FieldDescription>
          {errors.poNumber && <FieldError>{errors.poNumber.message}</FieldError>}
        </Field>

        <Field invalid={Boolean(errors.vendorGstin)}>
          <FieldLabel htmlFor="vendorGstin">Vendor GSTIN</FieldLabel>
          <Input
            id="vendorGstin"
            {...register('vendorGstin')}
            disabled={isSubmitting}
            placeholder="29ABCDE1234F1Z5"
          />
          <FieldDescription>State code (29 Karnataka) followed by 10-digit PAN.</FieldDescription>
          {errors.vendorGstin && <FieldError>{errors.vendorGstin.message}</FieldError>}
        </Field>

        <Field invalid={Boolean(errors.expectedAmount)}>
          <FieldLabel htmlFor="expectedAmount">Order value (₹)</FieldLabel>
          <Input
            id="expectedAmount"
            type="number"
            {...register('expectedAmount', { valueAsNumber: true })}
            disabled={isSubmitting}
          />
          {errors.expectedAmount && <FieldError>{errors.expectedAmount.message}</FieldError>}
        </Field>

        <Field invalid={Boolean(errors.deliveryNotes)} className="col-span-full">
          <FieldLabel htmlFor="deliveryNotes">Consignment delivery instructions</FieldLabel>
          <Textarea
            id="deliveryNotes"
            {...register('deliveryNotes')}
            disabled={isSubmitting}
            placeholder="Specify unloading bay, forklift requirements, or contact person."
          />
          {errors.deliveryNotes && <FieldError>{errors.deliveryNotes.message}</FieldError>}
        </Field>
      </FormGrid>

      <FormActions align="between" sticky>
        {isDirty ? (
          <AlertDialog open={discardDialogOpen} onOpenChange={setDiscardDialogOpen}>
            <AlertDialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" type="button" />}>
              Cancel
            </AlertDialogTrigger>
            <AlertDialogContent>
              <AlertDialogHeader>
                <AlertDialogTitle>Discard unsaved changes?</AlertDialogTitle>
                <AlertDialogDescription>
                  You have modified procurement details. Leaving now will discard all unsaved edits.
                </AlertDialogDescription>
              </AlertDialogHeader>
              <AlertDialogFooter>
                <AlertDialogClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>
                  Continue editing
                </AlertDialogClose>
                <AlertDialogClose
                  render={<Button variant="destructive" />}
                  onClick={() => reset()}
                >
                  Discard changes
                </AlertDialogClose>
              </AlertDialogFooter>
            </AlertDialogContent>
          </AlertDialog>
        ) : (
          <Button variant="outline" type="button" onClick={() => reset()}>
            Reset
          </Button>
        )}

        <Button type="submit" loading={isSubmitting}>
          Submit purchase order
        </Button>
      </FormActions>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## Next.js Server Action recipe

When dispatching form state directly to Server Actions, parse the payload against your Zod schema and return typed error maps rather than throwing unhandled exceptions:

```ts
// app/actions/procurement.ts
'use server';

import { z } from 'zod';

export async function createPurchaseOrderAction(formData: unknown) {
  const parseResult = purchaseOrderSchema.safeParse(formData);

  if (!parseResult.success) {
    const serverErrors: Record<string, string> = {};
    for (const issue of parseResult.error.issues) {
      const field = issue.path[0];
      if (field) serverErrors[String(field)] = issue.message;
    }
    return { success: false, serverErrors };
  }

  // Database transaction with Northwind ERP database
  const order = await db.orders.create({ data: parseResult.data });
  return { success: true, orderId: order.id };
}
```

## Multi-step forms with Stepper

For lengthy multi-stage funnels (e.g. 1. Supplier details → 2. Item specifications → 3. Tax and delivery → 4. Review):

1. **Maintain step index in local state**: `const [step, setStep] = useState(0)`.
2. **Validate only active step fields before progressing**: Trigger `trigger(['poNumber', 'vendorGstin'])` with React Hook Form to verify the active slice before incrementing `step`.
3. **Reflect progress with [`Stepper`](/ui/docs/components/navigation/stepper)**: Pass `steps` with `currentStep={step}`. Completed steps become clickable to permit backward revisions, while forward jumps remain locked until validation passes.

## Accessibility notes

- **Error association**: `Field` links `FieldError` with the input using `aria-describedby` automatically.
- **Focus first error**: Upon submit failure, immediately shift focus to the first invalid input element using `react-hook-form`'s automatic focus management.
- **Disabled state while saving**: Always mark inputs `disabled={isSubmitting}` to prevent duplicate clicks and double submissions.

## Common mistakes

| Anti-pattern | Recommended solution |
| :--- | :--- |
| Validating on every single keystroke (`mode: 'onChange'`). | Use `mode: 'onTouched'` or `mode: 'onBlur'` to avoid interrupting typing. |
| Using `window.alert()` or unformatted error banners. | Use inline `FieldError` directly under the affected field. |
| Allowing form dismissal while async submission is pending. | Disable close buttons and wrap actions with `loading={isSubmitting}`. |
| Hardcoding non-localized regex for Indian statutory identifiers. | Use verified GSTIN (15-character alphanumeric) and PAN (10-character) regex patterns. |

## Related components

- [Field](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) — Accessible field container with label, description, and error message.
- [FormLayout](/ui/docs/components/layout/form-layout) — Responsive container-query grids (`FormGrid`, `FormActions`).
- [Stepper](/ui/docs/components/navigation/stepper) — Multi-step sequential progression wizard.
- [AlertDialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/alert-dialog) — Confirmation dialog for discarding unsaved form edits.

## Internationalisation and right-to-left (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/patterns/internationalisation)

Multi-locale formatting, Indian fiscal conventions, RTL layout configuration, and component labels overrides.

Global enterprise applications serve distributed teams across linguistic borders and regulatory jurisdictions. `@innostes/ui` is built on top of standard web platform internationalisation APIs (`Intl.DateTimeFormat`, `Intl.NumberFormat`, `Intl.Collator`, `Intl.DisplayNames`) and CSS logical properties. This guide explains how to configure language locales, override built-in strings, apply Indian fiscal formatting conventions, and activate bidirectional Right-to-Left (RTL) rendering.

## The problem

Internationalised enterprise interfaces frequently encounter four fundamental issues:
1. **Hardcoded Western number formatting**: Formatting currency with standard Western thousands grouping (`10,000,000`) instead of the Indian numbering system (`1,00,00,000` / 1 Crore) confuses local accounting and tax audit teams.
2. **Untranslatable UI strings**: Hardcoding English text ("Previous", "Next", "Upload files", "Drop files here") inside compiled UI components prevents local language translation.
3. **Broken bidirectional layout**: Using physical directional CSS properties (`left`, `right`, `margin-left`, `padding-right`) causes layouts to invert incorrectly when switching to RTL scripts such as Arabic, Urdu, or Hebrew.
4. **Calendar start-of-week mismatches**: Forcing Sunday as the first day of the week disregards regional ISO-8601 business standards where Monday starts the work week.

## Recommended approach

- **BCP 47 Locale propagation**: Pass the active BCP 47 locale tag (e.g. `en-IN`, `hi-IN`, `ar-AE`, `en-GB`) to `@innostes/ui` date, number, and selection primitives.
- **Component `labels` overrides**: Customise UI strings across components using their typed `labels` prop, or wire them to your app's i18n dictionary (e.g. `next-intl` or `react-i18next`).
- **CSS logical properties**: Apply `start` and `end` logical dimensions (`ms-`, `me-`, `ps-`, `pe-`, `border-s-`, `border-e-`, `inset-inline-start`) instead of left/right physical styles.
- **Top-level `dir` attribute**: Set `<html dir="rtl">` or `<div dir="rtl">` at the root document container. All `@innostes/ui` overlays, dialogs, sheets, and popovers inherit this directionality.

## Components accepting `locale`

The following primitives accept a `locale?: string` prop and use the browser's native `Intl` engine:

| Component | Target `Intl` API | Formatting Behaviour |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [`Calendar`](/ui/docs/components/forms/calendar) | `Intl.DateTimeFormat` | Localises month names, weekday abbreviations, and determines whether the week begins on Sunday or Monday. |
| [`DatePicker`](/ui/docs/components/forms/date-picker) | `Intl.DateTimeFormat` | Formats selected dates in the trigger input matching regional date conventions (e.g. `DD/MM/YYYY` in `en-IN` vs `MM/DD/YYYY` in `en-US`). |
| [`CountrySelect`](/ui/docs/components/forms/locale-select) | `Intl.DisplayNames`, `Intl.Collator` | Translates country names to the specified language and sorts options alphabetically in that language. |
| [`LanguageSelect`](/ui/docs/components/forms/locale-select) | `Intl.DisplayNames` | Translates languages to target locale or displays native autonyms. |
| [`CurrencySelect`](/ui/docs/components/forms/locale-select) | `Intl.DisplayNames`, `Intl.NumberFormat` | Resolves official currency names and ISO code symbols. |
| [`MetricCard`](/ui/docs/widgets/metric-card) | `Intl.NumberFormat` | Formats metric delta values and percentages using local grouping separators. |
| [`CartesianCharts`](/ui/docs/charts/cartesian) | `Intl.NumberFormat` | Formats numeric axis ticks and hover tooltip readout values. |
| [`DonutChart`](/ui/docs/charts/donut) | `Intl.NumberFormat` | Formats slice values and accessible percentage summaries. |
| [`ActivityFeed`](/ui/docs/widgets/activity-feed) | `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` | Formats relative timestamps (e.g. "2 hours ago", "yesterday", "कल"). |
| [`Notifications`](/ui/docs/widgets/notifications) | `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` | Localises event timestamp indicators. |

## Components accepting `labels` overrides

When integrating with translation systems such as `next-intl` or `react-i18next`, override embedded component strings using the `labels` prop:

| Component | Labels Interface | Customisable Keys |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [`Pagination`](/ui/docs/components/navigation/pagination) | `PaginationLabels` | `previous`, `next`, `first`, `last`, `page`, `of` |
| [`Stepper`](/ui/docs/components/navigation/stepper) | `StepperLabels` | `step`, `completed`, `optional` |
| [`FileDropzone`](/ui/docs/components/forms/file-dropzone) | `FileDropzoneLabels` | `title`, `description`, `browse`, `rejectedFile`, `fileSizeExceeded` |
| [`RichTextEditor`](/ui/docs/components/forms/rich-text-editor) | `RichTextEditorLabels` | `bold`, `italic`, `bulletList`, `orderedList`, `link`, `clear` |
| [`KanbanBoard`](/ui/docs/widgets/kanban-board) | `KanbanLabels` | `columnEmpty`, `addCard`, `moveItem` |
| [`ActivityFeed`](/ui/docs/widgets/activity-feed) | `ActivityFeedLabels` | `today`, `yesterday` |
| [`PermissionMatrix`](/ui/docs/widgets/permission-matrix) | `PermissionMatrixLabels` | `subjectHeader`, `actionsHeader`, `allPermissions` |
| [`Notifications`](/ui/docs/widgets/notifications) | `NotificationsLabels` | `trigger`, `markAllRead`, `viewAll` |

## Indian fiscal conventions (`en-IN`)

Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd operates under Indian statutory accounting standards requiring Lakh (`1,00,000`) and Crore (`1,00,00,000`) grouping and INR (`₹`) currency presentation.

### Formatting utility

Use this standard helper across financial summary screens:

```tsx
export function formatINR(amount: number, options: { compact?: boolean } = {}): string {
  if (options.compact) {
    if (Math.abs(amount) >= 10000000) {
      return `₹${(amount / 10000000).toFixed(2)} Cr`;
    }
    if (Math.abs(amount) >= 100000) {
      return `₹${(amount / 100000).toFixed(2)} L`;
    }
  }

  return new Intl.NumberFormat('en-IN', {
    style: 'currency',
    currency: 'INR',
    maximumFractionDigits: 2,
  }).format(amount);
}

// Example outputs:
// formatINR(1485200)                => "₹14,85,200.00"
// formatINR(35000000, { compact: true }) => "₹3.50 Cr"
```

## Right-to-Left (RTL) configuration

To configure RTL mode for Middle Eastern subsidiaries or Arabic/Urdu speaking users:

```tsx
// Root layout or tenant wrapper:
export default function Layout({ children, locale }: { children: React.ReactNode; locale: string }) {
  const isRtl = locale.startsWith('ar') || locale.startsWith('ur') || locale.startsWith('he');

  return (
    <html lang={locale} dir={isRtl ? 'rtl' : 'ltr'}>
      <body className="min-h-screen bg-background text-foreground">
        {children}
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

### RTL CSS checklist

When writing custom application CSS alongside `@innostes/ui`:
- Use `ms-auto` (margin-inline-start) instead of `ml-auto`.
- Use `me-2` (margin-inline-end) instead of `mr-2`.
- Use `ps-4` (padding-inline-start) instead of `pl-4`.
- Use `text-start` and `text-end` instead of `text-left` and `text-right`.
- Use `border-s` and `border-e` instead of `border-l` and `border-r`.

## Testing RTL layouts

Verify RTL layouts in Vitest with Testing Library:

```tsx
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import { Pagination } from '@innostes/ui';

describe('Pagination RTL', () => {
  it('renders correctly within an RTL container', () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <div dir="rtl">
        <Pagination currentPage={1} totalPages={10} onPageChange={() => {}} />
      </div>
    );

    const prevButton = screen.getByRole('button', { name: /previous/i });
    expect(prevButton).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(container.querySelector('[dir="rtl"]')).toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});
```

## Common mistakes

- **Mixing physical and logical Tailwind classes**: Writing `pl-4 rtl:pr-4` creates redundant CSS. Always use standard Tailwind logical utilities like `ps-4` which automatically swap based on container direction.
- **Client-only locale resolution**: Calling `navigator.language` directly in server components or during initial render causes hydration mismatch warnings. Pass the user's preferred locale from cookie or HTTP header state.
- **Ignoring date order differences**: Assuming all dates are `YYYY-MM-DD` causes data entry errors. Always pair date inputs with localized helper placeholders.

## Related components

- [`Calendar`](/ui/docs/components/forms/calendar) — BCP 47 aware monthly date selector.
- [`CountrySelect`](/ui/docs/components/forms/locale-select) — International country, language, currency, and timezone selectors.
- [`Pagination`](/ui/docs/components/navigation/pagination) — Navigation control supporting full string localisation.
- [`MetricCard`](/ui/docs/widgets/metric-card) — KPI metric with locale-formatted numeric deltas.

## Master-detail screens (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/patterns/master-detail)

Responsive split-screen layouts with SplitPane on desktop, Sheet on mobile, and URL selection synchronisation.

Master-detail screens allow operators to scan high-density record lists while inspecting or modifying full entity details without losing their browsing position. This guide explains how to construct responsive master-detail views combining [`SplitPane`](/ui/docs/components/layout/split-pane) for desktop viewports, [`Sheet`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet) for mobile screens, URL search parameter synchronisation, and roving keyboard navigation.

## The problem

Enterprise master-detail layouts often suffer from three usability degradations:
1. **Lost navigation context**: Clicking an item in a list navigates to a new page, forcing operators to click the browser back button repeatedly when inspecting dozens of line items.
2. **Brittle mobile experiences**: Rigid side-by-side split panes collapse into unreadable narrow columns on smartphone or tablet viewports.
3. **Unshareable state**: Selecting an item only mutates transient React memory, meaning bookmarking or refreshing the page resets the detail view to an empty state.
4. **Broken keyboard navigation**: Moving between list items and detail controls requires tabbing through hundreds of unrelated DOM nodes.

## Recommended approach

- **Responsive presentation**: Render a resizable horizontal [`SplitPane`](/ui/docs/components/layout/split-pane) on viewports wider than 1024px (`lg:` breakpoint). On viewports below 1024px, render a full-width list and present the detail panel inside an overlay [`Sheet`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet) side drawer.
- **Deep-linkable URL parameters**: Store the selected record ID in query parameters (`?id=PO-2026-0811`). On initial page mount, hydrate the selected detail item directly from the URL.
- **Roving keyboard focus**: Allow users to navigate the master list with <kbd>Arrow Up</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> keys, press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to inspect details, and press <kbd>Escape</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd> to shift focus into the detail pane.
- **Persistent split pane dimensions**: Persist desktop pane size percentages in `localStorage` so user workspace preferences survive session restarts.

## Complete example: Purchase requisition master-detail

Below is a complete implementation of a purchase requisition review screen for Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState, useEffect, useTransition } from 'react';
import { useSearchParams, useRouter, usePathname } from 'next/navigation';
import {
  SplitPane,
  Sheet,
  SheetContent,
  SheetHeader,
  SheetTitle,
  SheetDescription,
  Badge,
  Button,
  Card,
  Input,
  Skeleton,
} from '@innostes/ui';
import { Search, ChevronRight, FileText, CheckCircle2, Clock } from 'lucide-react';

interface Requisition {
  id: string;
  department: string;
  requester: string;
  amount: number;
  status: 'pending' | 'approved' | 'rejected';
  date: string;
  itemsCount: number;
  description: string;
}

const REQUISITIONS: Requisition[] = [
  {
    id: 'PR-8901',
    department: 'Bengaluru Logistics Hub',
    requester: 'Aarav Sharma',
    amount: 142500,
    status: 'pending',
    date: '28 Oct 2026',
    itemsCount: 4,
    description: 'Replacement hydraulic seal assemblies and conveyor belt rollers.',
  },
  {
    id: 'PR-8902',
    department: 'Quality Assurance Lab',
    requester: 'Priya Patel',
    amount: 88400,
    status: 'approved',
    date: '27 Oct 2026',
    itemsCount: 2,
    description: 'Precision digital calibration gauges and safety thermal probes.',
  },
  {
    id: 'PR-8903',
    department: 'Procurement & Stores',
    requester: 'Rajesh Kumar',
    amount: 320000,
    status: 'pending',
    date: '26 Oct 2026',
    itemsCount: 12,
    description: 'Industrial corrugated packaging cartons and tamper-evident seals.',
  },
];

export function MasterDetailScreen() {
  const router = useRouter();
  const pathname = usePathname();
  const searchParams = useSearchParams();
  const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition();

  // Read selected requisition from URL search params
  const selectedId = searchParams.get('requisitionId') || REQUISITIONS[0].id;
  const selectedItem = REQUISITIONS.find((r) => r.id === selectedId) || null;

  // Track responsive screen width for mobile sheet presentation
  const [isMobile, setIsMobile] = useState(false);
  const [mobileSheetOpen, setMobileSheetOpen] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    const mediaQuery = window.matchMedia('(max-width: 1024px)');
    setIsMobile(mediaQuery.matches);

    const handler = (e: MediaQueryListEvent) => setIsMobile(e.matches);
    mediaQuery.addEventListener('change', handler);
    return () => mediaQuery.removeEventListener('change', handler);
  }, []);

  const handleSelectRequisition = (id: string) => {
    startTransition(() => {
      const params = new URLSearchParams(searchParams.toString());
      params.set('requisitionId', id);
      router.replace(`${pathname}?${params.toString()}`);
    });

    if (isMobile) {
      setMobileSheetOpen(true);
    }
  };

  // Reusable detail view component
  const DetailContent = ({ item }: { item: Requisition | null }) => {
    if (!item) {
      return (
        <div className="flex h-full items-center justify-center p-8 text-center text-muted-foreground">
          Select a requisition from the list to inspect authorization line items.
        </div>
      );
    }

    return (
      <div className="space-y-6 p-6">
        <div className="flex items-start justify-between border-b pb-4">
          <div>
            <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
              <h2 className="text-xl font-bold text-foreground">{item.id}</h2>
              <Badge variant={item.status === 'approved' ? 'default' : 'secondary'}>
                {item.status}
              </Badge>
            </div>
            <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground mt-1">{item.department}</p>
          </div>
          <div className="text-right">
            <span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground block">Estimated Total</span>
            <span className="text-2xl font-bold text-foreground">
              ₹{item.amount.toLocaleString('en-IN')}
            </span>
          </div>
        </div>

        <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4 text-sm">
          <div>
            <span className="text-muted-foreground block">Requested by</span>
            <span className="font-medium text-foreground">{item.requester}</span>
          </div>
          <div>
            <span className="text-muted-foreground block">Submission date</span>
            <span className="font-medium text-foreground">{item.date}</span>
          </div>
        </div>

        <div>
          <h3 className="text-sm font-semibold text-foreground mb-2">Scope of purchase</h3>
          <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground leading-relaxed bg-muted/30 p-4 rounded-md">
            {item.description}
          </p>
        </div>

        <div className="pt-4 flex gap-3">
          <Button variant="primary">Approve requisition</Button>
          <Button variant="outline">Request revision</Button>
        </div>
      </div>
    );
  };

  return (
    <div className="h-[600px] border rounded-lg overflow-hidden bg-background">
      {isMobile ? (
        // Mobile layout: Full width list + Sheet detail drawer
        <div className="p-4 space-y-4">
          <div className="relative">
            <Search className="absolute left-3 top-2.5 h-4 w-4 text-muted-foreground" />
            <Input placeholder="Search requisitions..." className="pl-9" />
          </div>
          <div className="space-y-2">
            {REQUISITIONS.map((req) => (
              <Card
                key={req.id}
                tabIndex={0}
                role="button"
                onClick={() => handleSelectRequisition(req.id)}
                className={`p-4 cursor-pointer transition-colors ${
                  req.id === selectedId ? 'border-primary bg-primary/5' : 'hover:bg-muted/50'
                }`}
              >
                <div className="flex justify-between items-start">
                  <div>
                    <span className="font-semibold text-foreground">{req.id}</span>
                    <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">{req.requester}</p>
                  </div>
                  <span className="text-sm font-medium">₹{req.amount.toLocaleString('en-IN')}</span>
                </div>
              </Card>
            ))}
          </div>

          <Sheet open={mobileSheetOpen} onOpenChange={setMobileSheetOpen}>
            <SheetContent side="right" className="w-full sm:max-w-lg p-0">
              <SheetHeader className="p-6 border-b">
                <SheetTitle>Requisition details</SheetTitle>
                <SheetDescription>Review specifications and fiscal approvals.</SheetDescription>
              </SheetHeader>
              <DetailContent item={selectedItem} />
            </SheetContent>
          </Sheet>
        </div>
      ) : (
        // Desktop layout: SplitPane side-by-side
        <SplitPane defaultSize={38} minSize={20} maxSize={60} orientation="horizontal" className="h-full">
          <div className="border-r flex flex-col h-full">
            <div className="p-4 border-b">
              <div className="relative">
                <Search className="absolute left-3 top-2.5 h-4 w-4 text-muted-foreground" />
                <Input placeholder="Filter by ID or requester..." className="pl-9" />
              </div>
            </div>
            <div className="overflow-y-auto flex-1 divide-y" role="listbox" aria-label="Purchase requisitions">
              {REQUISITIONS.map((req) => (
                <div
                  key={req.id}
                  role="option"
                  aria-selected={req.id === selectedId}
                  tabIndex={0}
                  onClick={() => handleSelectRequisition(req.id)}
                  onKeyDown={(e) => {
                    if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') {
                      e.preventDefault();
                      handleSelectRequisition(req.id);
                    }
                  }}
                  className={`p-4 cursor-pointer transition-colors ${
                    req.id === selectedId
                      ? 'bg-accent/40 border-l-4 border-l-primary'
                      : 'hover:bg-muted/40'
                  }`}
                >
                  <div className="flex items-center justify-between">
                    <span className="font-semibold text-sm text-foreground">{req.id}</span>
                    <Badge variant="outline">{req.status}</Badge>
                  </div>
                  <div className="text-xs text-muted-foreground mt-1 flex justify-between">
                    <span>{req.requester}</span>
                    <span className="font-medium text-foreground">
                      ₹{req.amount.toLocaleString('en-IN')}
                    </span>
                  </div>
                </div>
              ))}
            </div>
          </div>

          <div className="overflow-y-auto bg-muted/5 h-full">
            <DetailContent item={selectedItem} />
          </div>
        </SplitPane>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility notes

- **Keyboard navigation semantics**: Master items rendered inside the navigation column should expose `role="option"` inside a container with `role="listbox"`. Set `aria-selected="true"` on the currently active item.
- **Focus handoff**: When pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd> to inspect a record on desktop, allow keyboard users to advance focus directly to the detail action buttons using <kbd>Tab</kbd>.
- **Accessible resizers**: The [`SplitPane`](/ui/docs/components/layout/split-pane) divider renders `role="separator"` with keyboard accessibility supporting step resizing via <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> and <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd>.
- **Mobile sheet close focus**: When the mobile [`Sheet`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet) dismisses, return keyboard focus cleanly to the trigger list card.

## Common mistakes

- **Hardcoding fixed pixel widths**: Hardcoding static pixel dimensions on master lists causes horizontal clipping on smaller desktop monitors. Always use fluid percentage splits with defined `minSize` safety boundaries.
- **Neglecting URL state**: Failing to update the browser address bar with the selected identifier prevents users from emailing direct links to colleagues or opening items in background tabs.
- **Duplicate scroll containers**: Avoid nesting independently scrolling viewports inside the master column without explicit height constraints; this causes scroll-wheel traps.

## Related components

- [`SplitPane`](/ui/docs/components/layout/split-pane) — Collapsible, resizable two-column and two-row layouts.
- [`Sheet`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet) — Slide-out modal drawer for mobile navigation and detailed inspectors.
- [`Card`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/card) — Compact container for master listing items.
- [`Badge`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/badge) — Status and category indicators.

## Migrating from another library (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/patterns/migration)

Migration guide and component mapping tables from shadcn/ui and Material UI (MUI) to @innostes/ui.

Migrating an enterprise application from legacy component libraries—such as shadcn/ui (Radix Primitives) or Material UI (MUI)—to `@innostes/ui` improves accessibility compliance, simplifies form wiring, and removes heavy runtime CSS-in-JS engines. This guide provides direct mapping tables for component names, layout structures, and API props to accelerate refactoring.

## Why migrate to `@innostes/ui`?

1. **Zero runtime styling overhead**: Replaces Emotion/MUI CSS-in-JS style injection with zero-runtime Tailwind CSS utility tokens and CSS variables.
2. **Unified accessible forms**: Replaces scattered label and error boilerplates with cohesive [`Field`](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) containers that automatically link IDs, descriptions, and ARIA error states.
3. **Integrated enterprise data primitives**: Native support for [`DataTable`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table), [`SplitPane`](/ui/docs/components/layout/split-pane), [`KanbanBoard`](/ui/docs/widgets/kanban-board), [`PermissionMatrix`](/ui/docs/widgets/permission-matrix), and BCP 47 locale selectors.
4. **Multi-React version support**: First-class compatibility across React 17, React 18, and React 19 without peer dependency conflicts.

## Mapping from shadcn/ui (Radix UI)

shadcn/ui copies individual Radix wrapper components into your repository. `@innostes/ui` provides drop-in components built on Base UI with consistent styling and zero boilerplate.

### Component mapping table

| shadcn/ui Component | `@innostes/ui` Equivalent | Key API Differences |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Button` | [`Button`](/ui/docs/components/actions/button) | `variant="default"` maps to `variant="primary"`. Also supports `variant="secondary"`, `variant="outline"`, `variant="ghost"`, `variant="destructive"`. |
| `Input` | [`Input`](/ui/docs/components/forms/input) | Drop-in compatible. Supports `size="sm" \| "md" \| "lg"`. |
| `FormField` / `FormItem` | [`Field`](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) | Single wrapping component. Automatically generates accessible IDs and connects labels to inputs. |
| `FormLabel` | [`FieldLabel`](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) | Renders semantic `<label>` linked via context. |
| `FormDescription` | [`FieldDescription`](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) | Links automatically to input via `aria-describedby`. |
| `FormMessage` | [`FieldError`](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) | Renders error text with `role="alert"` and automatically adds error rings to the field input. |
| `Dialog` / `DialogContent` | [`Dialog`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dialog) | Identical structure: `Dialog`, `DialogTrigger`, `DialogContent`, `DialogHeader`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `DialogFooter`, `DialogClose`. |
| `AlertDialog` | [`AlertDialog`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/alert-dialog) | Identical structure with enforced alertdialog semantics. |
| `Sheet` | [`Sheet`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet) | Same `side="top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left"` prop. Better focus trap and mobile drawer animations. |
| `DropdownMenu` | [`DropdownMenu`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu) | Uses `@base-ui/react` menu engine. `DropdownMenuItem` supports keyboard shortcuts. |
| `Select` | [`Select`](/ui/docs/components/forms/select) | Offers both a convenient single-prop API (`options={items}`) and a full composable subcomponent API. |
| `Tabs` | [`Tabs`](/ui/docs/components/navigation/tabs) | `TabsTrigger` is supported; also exports semantic `TabsTab` and `TabsPanel`. |
| `Badge` | [`Badge`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/badge) | Similar variants (`primary`, `secondary`, `outline`, `destructive`). |
| `Card` | [`Card`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/card) | Drop-in compatible structure (`CardHeader`, `CardTitle`, `CardDescription`, `CardContent`, `CardFooter`). |
| `Table` | [`Table`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/table) | Drop-in compatible HTML table primitives. For server tables, consider [`DataTable`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table). |
| `Toaster` / `toast` | [`Toaster`](/ui/docs/components/feedback/toast) / `toast` | Direct functional API. Supports `title`, `description`, `action`, `variant`. |

### Before & after: shadcn/ui Form migration

```tsx
// ─── Before: shadcn/ui ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
import { useForm } from 'react-hook-form';
import { Form, FormField, FormItem, FormLabel, FormControl, FormMessage, FormDescription } from '@/components/ui/form';
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';

export function OldVendorForm() {
  const form = useForm();
  return (
    <Form {...form}>
      <form onSubmit={form.handleSubmit(console.log)}>
        <FormField
          control={form.control}
          name="vendorName"
          render={({ field }) => (
            <FormItem>
              <FormLabel>Vendor Name</FormLabel>
              <FormControl>
                <Input placeholder="Acme Ltd" {...field} />
              </FormControl>
              <FormDescription>Official legal trade entity</FormDescription>
              <FormMessage />
            </FormItem>
          )}
        />
        <Button type="submit">Submit</Button>
      </form>
    </Form>
  );
}

// ─── After: @innostes/ui ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
import { useForm } from 'react-hook-form';
import { Field, FieldLabel, FieldDescription, FieldError, Input, Button } from '@innostes/ui';

export function NewVendorForm() {
  const { register, handleSubmit, formState: { errors } } = useForm();
  return (
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit(console.log)} className="space-y-4">
      <Field id="vendorName" error={errors.vendorName?.message as string}>
        <FieldLabel>Vendor Name</FieldLabel>
        <Input placeholder="Acme Ltd" {...register('vendorName', { required: 'Name is required' })} />
        <FieldDescription>Official legal trade entity</FieldDescription>
        <FieldError />
      </Field>
      <Button type="submit" variant="primary">Submit</Button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## Mapping from Material UI (MUI v5)

Material UI relies on Emotion/styled-components for style generation. Migrating to `@innostes/ui` removes runtime styling overhead and provides Tailwind CSS agility.

### Component mapping table

| MUI Component | `@innostes/ui` Equivalent | Key API Differences |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Button` (`variant="contained"`) | [`Button`](/ui/docs/components/actions/button) `variant="primary"` | `variant="contained"` → `variant="primary"`; `variant="outlined"` → `variant="outline"`; `variant="text"` → `variant="ghost"`. |
| `TextField` | [`Field`](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) + [`Input`](/ui/docs/components/forms/input) | MUI packages label, input, and helperText in one monolithic component. In `@innostes/ui`, compose [`FieldLabel`](/ui/docs/components/forms/field), [`Input`](/ui/docs/components/forms/input), and [`FieldError`](/ui/docs/components/forms/field). |
| `Dialog` | [`Dialog`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dialog) | MUI uses `onClose={() => setOpen(false)}`; `@innostes/ui` uses `onOpenChange={(open) => setOpen(open)}`. |
| `Drawer` | [`Sheet`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet) | `anchor="right"` becomes `side="right"`. |
| `Menu` / `MenuItem` | [`DropdownMenu`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu) | MUI requires passing an `anchorEl` DOM ref state. `@innostes/ui` uses a declarative trigger (`<DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>`). |
| `Typography` | Semantic HTML + Tailwind | Replace `<Typography variant="h4">` with `<h2 className="text-xl font-bold">`. |
| `Stack` | Tailwind Flexbox | Replace `<Stack direction="row" spacing={2}>` with `<div className="flex flex-row gap-2">`. |
| `Grid` | Tailwind Grid | Replace `<Grid container spacing={3}>` with `<div className="grid grid-cols-12 gap-6">` or [`FormGrid`](/ui/docs/components/layout/form-layout). |
| `CircularProgress` | [`Spinner`](/ui/docs/components/feedback/spinner) | Direct accessible SVG spinner. |
| `LinearProgress` | [`Progress`](/ui/docs/components/feedback/progress) | Supports `value` (0–100) and `aria-label`. |
| `Chip` | [`Badge`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/badge) | Compact status tag. |
| `Snackbar` / `Alert` | [`toast`](/ui/docs/components/feedback/toast) / [`Alert`](/ui/docs/components/feedback/alert) | Transient alerts use `toast()`; persistent banners use `<Alert>`. |

### Before & after: Material UI Modal migration

```tsx
// ─── Before: Material UI ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
import * as React from 'react';
import Button from '@mui/material/Button';
import Dialog from '@mui/material/Dialog';
import DialogActions from '@mui/material/DialogActions';
import DialogContent from '@mui/material/DialogContent';
import DialogContentText from '@mui/material/DialogContentText';
import DialogTitle from '@mui/material/DialogTitle';

export function OldMuiDialog() {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);

  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="contained" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Open Modal</Button>
      <Dialog open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)}>
        <DialogTitle>Confirm Disbursement</DialogTitle>
        <DialogContent>
          <DialogContentText>Are you sure you wish to release payment?</DialogContentText>
        </DialogContent>
        <DialogActions>
          <Button onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</Button>
          <Button variant="contained" color="error" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Confirm</Button>
        </DialogActions>
      </Dialog>
    </>
  );
}

// ─── After: @innostes/ui ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
import { useState } from 'react';
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogTrigger,
  DialogContent,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogClose,
  Button,
} from '@innostes/ui';

export function NewInnostesDialog() {
  return (
    <Dialog>
      <DialogTrigger asChild>
        <Button variant="primary">Open Modal</Button>
      </DialogTrigger>
      <DialogContent>
        <DialogHeader>
          <DialogTitle>Confirm Disbursement</DialogTitle>
          <DialogDescription>Are you sure you wish to release payment?</DialogDescription>
        </DialogHeader>
        <DialogFooter>
          <DialogClose asChild>
            <Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
          </DialogClose>
          <Button variant="destructive">Confirm</Button>
        </DialogFooter>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  );
}
```

## Migration checklist

1. **Install `@innostes/ui` and peer dependencies**:
   ```bash
   pnpm add @innostes/ui @base-ui/react clsx tailwind-merge class-variance-authority lucide-react
   ```
2. **Configure Tailwind CSS preset**: Import `@innostes/ui/tailwind.css` or the design token CSS variables in your global stylesheet (`globals.css`).
3. **Migrate leaf primitives first**: Start refactoring buttons, badges, inputs, and cards before tackling high-level layout shells and data tables.
4. **Replace complex form controls**: Transition forms to [`Field`](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) containers.
5. **Run accessibility test suites**: Confirm all interactive components pass automated axe-core and Testing Library queries.

- [API Conventions](/ui/docs/resources/conventions) — Architectural principles and state models.
- [Forms and validation](/ui/docs/patterns/forms-and-validation) — Zod and React Hook Form recipes.
- [Data tables backed by an API](/ui/docs/patterns/api-tables) — Server table composition.

## Theming for multiple tenants (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/patterns/multi-tenant-theming)

Dynamic runtime brand token injection, multi-tenant CSS variables, WCAG AA contrast validation, and dark mode.

Multi-tenant software-as-a-service (SaaS) and white-label enterprise platforms allow distinct corporate client tenants to brand their workspaces with custom brand colours, typography accents, and logos. This guide explains how to inject runtime CSS brand tokens safely, compute accessible foreground contrast, and support independent light and dark themes per tenant.

## The problem

Multi-tenant UI theming introduces three dangerous engineering pitfalls:
1. **Accessibility violations via arbitrary branding**: Tenants frequently choose brand colours (such as light yellow or pastel cyan) that produce illegible contrast ratios against white or dark text backgrounds, violating WCAG 2.1 AA mandates.
2. **Build-time theme limitations**: Generating separate CSS bundles per tenant requires re-deploying code whenever an enterprise customer updates their brand hex code in their administrative portal.
3. **Dark mode failures**: A brand colour optimized for a light surface often washes out or vibrates aggressively when rendered in dark mode.
4. **CSS cascade leakage**: Overriding global CSS variables without proper scoping causes tenant brand styles to leak across administrative consoles or portal boundaries.

## Recommended approach

- **Runtime CSS variable injection**: Inject tenant-specific tokens directly into the HTML root style attribute or a tenant wrapper element (`style="--primary: 217 91% 60%"`).
- **Automated contrast safety validation**: Calculate relative luminance from tenant hex values. If the tenant's chosen colour fails the 4.5:1 WCAG AA contrast ratio threshold against the foreground text, automatically calculate and apply the compliant accessible foreground token (`#ffffff` or `#09090b`).
- **Dual-palette storage**: Persist separate light-mode and dark-mode brand values in the tenant profile table, or compute a calibrated dark-mode tone programmatically.
- **Scoped container theming**: Wrap tenant workspaces in a dedicated container carrying tenant CSS custom properties, isolating client styles from system-wide administrative interfaces.

## Contrast validation utility

Use this mathematical contrast checker to validate tenant colours before persisting or injecting them:

```ts
/**
 * Computes the relative luminance of an sRGB color.
 * WCAG 2.1 Formula: https://www.w3.org/WAI/GL/wiki/Relative_luminance
 */
function getLuminance(r: number, g: number, b: number): number {
  const [rs, gs, bs] = [r, g, b].map((c) => {
    const s = c / 255;
    return s <= 0.03928 ? s / 12.92 : Math.pow((s + 0.055) / 1.055, 2.4);
  });
  return 0.2126 * rs + 0.7152 * gs + 0.0722 * bs;
}

/**
 * Parses a hex string to RGB numbers.
 */
function hexToRgb(hex: string): [number, number, number] {
  const clean = hex.replace('#', '');
  const bigint = parseInt(clean, 16);
  return [(bigint >> 16) & 255, (bigint >> 8) & 255, bigint & 255];
}

/**
 * Returns the contrast ratio between two hex colours (1:1 to 21:1).
 */
export function getContrastRatio(hex1: string, hex2: string): number {
  const rgb1 = hexToRgb(hex1);
  const rgb2 = hexToRgb(hex2);
  const lum1 = getLuminance(...rgb1);
  const lum2 = getLuminance(...rgb2);

  const brightest = Math.max(lum1, lum2);
  const darkest = Math.min(lum1, lum2);
  return (brightest + 0.05) / (darkest + 0.05);
}

/**
 * Evaluates tenant primary color and determines the accessible foreground color.
 * Ensures minimum 4.5:1 ratio (WCAG AA).
 */
export function getAccessibleForeground(primaryHex: string): '#ffffff' | '#0f172a' {
  const whiteRatio = getContrastRatio(primaryHex, '#ffffff');
  const darkRatio = getContrastRatio(primaryHex, '#0f172a');

  // Choose the foreground that provides the strongest contrast
  return whiteRatio >= darkRatio ? '#ffffff' : '#0f172a';
}
```

## Complete example: Dynamic tenant brand injector

Below is an implementation of a Next.js tenant layout wrapper that resolves the tenant profile and injects validated CSS custom properties:

```tsx
import { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { getAccessibleForeground, getContrastRatio } from '@/lib/contrast';

interface TenantTheme {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  brandPrimary: string;       // e.g. "#1e40af"
  brandAccent?: string;       // e.g. "#0284c7"
  darkBrandPrimary?: string;  // e.g. "#3b82f6"
}

// Convert Hex to CSS HSL string values (e.g. "217 91% 60%")
function hexToHslValues(hex: string): string {
  const [r, g, b] = [0, 2, 4].map((p) => parseInt(hex.slice(p + 1, p + 3), 16) / 255);
  const max = Math.max(r, g, b);
  const min = Math.min(r, g, b);
  let h = 0;
  let s = 0;
  const l = (max + min) / 2;

  if (max !== min) {
    const d = max - min;
    s = l > 0.5 ? d / (2 - max - min) : d / (max + min);
    switch (max) {
      case r: h = (g - b) / d + (g < b ? 6 : 0); break;
      case g: h = (b - r) / d + 2; break;
      case b: h = (r - g) / d + 4; break;
    }
    h /= 6;
  }

  return `${Math.round(h * 360)} ${Math.round(s * 100)}% ${Math.round(l * 100)}%`;
}

export function TenantProvider({
  tenant,
  children,
}: {
  tenant: TenantTheme;
  children: ReactNode;
}) {
  // Validate contrast safety: must be >= 4.5:1
  const lightForeground = getAccessibleForeground(tenant.brandPrimary);
  const lightHsl = hexToHslValues(tenant.brandPrimary);
  const lightForegroundHsl = hexToHslValues(lightForeground);

  const darkPrimary = tenant.darkBrandPrimary || tenant.brandPrimary;
  const darkForeground = getAccessibleForeground(darkPrimary);
  const darkHsl = hexToHslValues(darkPrimary);
  const darkForegroundHsl = hexToHslValues(darkForeground);

  // Generate CSS style string for scoped tenant container
  const cssVariables = `
    [data-tenant="${tenant.id}"] {
      --primary: ${lightHsl};
      --primary-foreground: ${lightForegroundHsl};
      --ring: ${lightHsl};
    }
    .dark [data-tenant="${tenant.id}"],
    [data-tenant="${tenant.id}"].dark {
      --primary: ${darkHsl};
      --primary-foreground: ${darkForegroundHsl};
      --ring: ${darkHsl};
    }
  `;

  return (
    <>
      <style dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: cssVariables }} />
      <div data-tenant={tenant.id} className="min-h-screen bg-background text-foreground">
        {children}
      </div>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Administrative brand preview and safety audit

In the tenant settings panel, provide real-time contrast auditing to prevent administrators from saving non-compliant color schemes:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardContent, Input, Button, Badge, Alert } from '@innostes/ui';
import { getContrastRatio, getAccessibleForeground } from '@/lib/contrast';
import { AlertCircle, CheckCircle2 } from 'lucide-react';

export function TenantThemeEditor() {
  const [primaryHex, setPrimaryHex] = useState('#0f766e'); // Teal-700
  const foreground = getAccessibleForeground(primaryHex);
  const contrastAgainstWhite = getContrastRatio(primaryHex, '#ffffff');
  const passesAA = contrastAgainstWhite >= 4.5;

  return (
    <Card className="max-w-xl">
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Tenant brand configuration</CardTitle>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent className="space-y-4">
        <div>
          <label className="text-sm font-medium text-foreground block mb-2">
            Primary brand color (HEX)
          </label>
          <div className="flex gap-3">
            <Input
              type="text"
              value={primaryHex}
              onChange={(e) => setPrimaryHex(e.target.value)}
              className="font-mono"
            />
            <div
              className="w-10 h-10 rounded-md border flex-shrink-0"
              style={{ backgroundColor: primaryHex }}
            />
          </div>
        </div>

        <div className="p-4 rounded-lg border bg-muted/20 space-y-2">
          <div className="flex justify-between items-center text-sm">
            <span>Contrast against white</span>
            <span className="font-mono font-bold">{contrastAgainstWhite.toFixed(2)}:1</span>
          </div>
          <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
            <Badge variant={passesAA ? 'default' : 'destructive'}>
              {passesAA ? 'WCAG AA Compliant' : 'Insufficient Contrast (< 4.5:1)'}
            </Badge>
          </div>
        </div>

        {!passesAA && (
          <Alert variant="destructive">
            <AlertCircle className="h-4 w-4" />
            <p className="text-xs">
              This brand colour lacks sufficient luminance contrast. Text rendered on top of this button will be illegible to visually impaired operators.
            </p>
          </Alert>
        )}

        <div className="pt-2">
          <Button
            variant="primary"
            disabled={!passesAA}
            style={{ backgroundColor: primaryHex, color: foreground }}
          >
            Sample tenant button
          </Button>
        </div>
      </CardContent>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility notes

- **Strict WCAG 2.1 compliance**: Enterprise business software requires a minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio for regular body text and buttons, and 3:1 for large typography and essential user interface boundaries.
- **Automated fallback enforcement**: If a tenant saves an invalid color below 4.5:1, adjust the lightness channel automatically in your theme parser to guarantee baseline compliance.
- **Focus ring visibility**: Ensure `--ring` custom properties maintain a 3:1 contrast ratio against the page background so keyboard focus indicators remain distinct.

## Common mistakes

- **Saving unverified hex colors**: Allowing tenant admins to type arbitrary hex codes without validation leads to broken buttons with invisible text.
- **Global `body` style overrides**: Injecting tenant styles onto the top-level `document.body` breaks multi-tenant tab switching or unified super-admin consoles where multiple tenants are inspected simultaneously.
- **Ignoring dark mode inversion**: A dark navy blue works well as primary on white backgrounds, but becomes virtually invisible when rendered against a `#09090b` dark mode background. Always supply a distinct dark mode value.

## Related components

- [`Button`](/ui/docs/components/actions/button) — Uses `--primary` and `--primary-foreground` design tokens.
- [`Badge`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/badge) — Brand-aware status indicator.
- [`Alert`](/ui/docs/components/feedback/alert) — Accessible warning banner for theme safety validation.
- [`Card`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/card) — Tenant branding container.
