## Performance (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/patterns/performance)

Optimising bundle size, tree-shaking, subpath entry points, virtualisation, and controlled state rendering.

Enterprise applications handle vast tabular datasets, complex analytical charts, and rich document editing environments. Keeping initial page loads swift and interactions responsive under high data density requires disciplined architectural boundaries. This guide explains how `@innostes/ui` achieves minimal bundle overhead via tree-shaking, separate subpath entry points, and strategies for eliminating unnecessary re-renders.

## The problem

Enterprise frontends frequently degrade under performance bottlenecks:
1. **Monolithic bundle pollution**: Importing a single button inadvertently pulls heavy charting engines (such as Recharts) or document parsers (like Tiptap) into the critical first-load JavaScript bundle.
2. **DOM node explosion in large tables**: Rendering 1,000 raw table rows creates over 10,000 DOM elements, causing noticeable scroll stuttering and memory bloat.
3. **Controlled re-render cascades**: Typing into a controlled filter input at the top of a page re-evaluates the entire component tree, causing input latency for operators.
4. **CSS duplicate bloat**: Bundling multiple copies of utility classes or CSS resets across micro-frontends.

## Architecture: Tree-shaking and subpath exports

`@innostes/ui` uses native ECMAScript Modules (ESM) with explicit package export maps and `sideEffects: ["**/*.css"]` configuration. Compilers like Next.js (Turbopack / Webpack), Vite (Rollup), and esbuild automatically drop unreferenced components.

### Subpath entry points

Heavy third-party peer dependencies are isolated into dedicated subpaths:

```
@innostes/ui
  │
  ├── @innostes/ui          (Core primitives, actions, forms, widgets ~15 KB ESM)
  ├── @innostes/ui/charts   (Isolated Recharts wrappers: CartesianCharts, DonutChart)
  └── @innostes/ui/editor   (Isolated Tiptap wrappers: RichTextEditor)
```

By keeping `@innostes/ui/charts` and `@innostes/ui/editor` behind subpaths, an operator viewing a procurement list page never downloads chart SVG rendering libraries or WYSIWYG parser binaries:

```tsx
// Core components only pull core dependencies
import { Button, Input, Table } from '@innostes/ui';

// Charts only imported on analytics screens
import { CartesianChart } from '@innostes/ui/charts';

// Rich text editor only imported on CMS / documentation screens
import { RichTextEditor } from '@innostes/ui/editor';
```

## Measured bundle sizes

Measured using Rollup with Terser and Brotli compression (production build):

| Import Target | Uncompressed | Gzipped | Brotli | Peer Dependencies |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `import { Button } from '@innostes/ui'` | 4.8 KB | 1.4 KB | 1.2 KB | None (Base UI primitive) |
| Core Set (`Button`, `Input`, `Card`, `Badge`) | 19.2 KB | 5.8 KB | 5.1 KB | None |
| Full Core Library (`@innostes/ui`) | 72.4 KB | 16.8 KB | 14.9 KB | `@base-ui/react` |
| Analytics Subpath (`@innostes/ui/charts`) | 142.0 KB | 42.5 KB | 37.1 KB | `recharts` |
| Editor Subpath (`@innostes/ui/editor`) | 128.0 KB | 38.2 KB | 33.4 KB | `@tiptap/core`, `@tiptap/react` |

### Automated CI bundle budgets

To safeguard against size creep, continuous integration enforces deterministic bundle limits via `pnpm nx check:size ui`:

| Entry Point | Distribution Artifact | Maximum Raw Budget | Maximum Gzip Budget | Current Raw Size |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Core entry (`@innostes/ui`) | `dist/index.js` | 25.0 KB | 10.0 KB | 14.8 KB |
| Charts entry (`@innostes/ui/charts`) | `dist/charts/index.js` | 55.0 KB | 15.0 KB | 0.3 KB |
| Editor entry (`@innostes/ui/editor`) | `dist/editor/index.js` | 45.0 KB | 15.0 KB | 0.1 KB |
| Standalone styles | `dist/styles.css` | 110.0 KB | 20.0 KB | 95.8 KB |

## Eliminating re-render cascades in controlled components

When wrapping controlled `@innostes/ui` inputs inside complex forms or data grids, avoid passing inline function definitions or recreating column definitions on each render.

### 1. Memoising table column definitions

Column definitions passed to [`DataTable`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table) should always be declared outside the component body or memoised using `useMemo`:

```tsx
// ❌ Anti-pattern: columns recreated on every keystroke
export function VendorTable({ searchTerm }: { searchTerm: string }) {
  const columns = [
    { key: 'name', header: 'Vendor Name' },
    { key: 'balance', header: 'Balance', render: (row) => `₹${row.balance}` },
  ];
  return <DataTable columns={columns} data={vendors} />;
}

// ✅ Recommended pattern: static reference or useMemo
const VENDOR_COLUMNS = [
  { key: 'name', header: 'Vendor Name' },
  { key: 'balance', header: 'Balance', render: (row: any) => `₹${row.balance}` },
];

export function VendorTableOptimised({ searchTerm }: { searchTerm: string }) {
  return <DataTable columns={VENDOR_COLUMNS} data={vendors} />;
}
```

### 2. Debouncing high-frequency inputs

Debounce search filters by 300ms before pushing parameters into URL state or dispatching network queries:

```tsx
import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
import { Input } from '@innostes/ui';

export function SearchFilter({ onSearch }: { onSearch: (val: string) => void }) {
  const [query, setQuery] = useState('');

  useEffect(() => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      onSearch(query);
    }, 300);

    return () => clearTimeout(timer);
  }, [query, onSearch]);

  return (
    <Input
      value={query}
      onChange={(e) => setQuery(e.target.value)}
      placeholder="Filter by vendor name or GSTIN..."
    />
  );
}
```

## Large list virtualisation

For tabular datasets exceeding 200 rows without server pagination, virtualise rendering using `@tanstack/react-virtual` paired with semantic `@innostes/ui` [`Table`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/table) markup:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useRef } from 'react';
import { useVirtualizer } from '@tanstack/react-virtual';
import { Table, TableHeader, TableBody, TableRow, TableHead, TableCell } from '@innostes/ui';

interface InventoryItem {
  sku: string;
  name: string;
  quantity: number;
}

export function VirtualizedInventoryTable({ items }: { items: InventoryItem[] }) {
  const parentRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

  const rowVirtualizer = useVirtualizer({
    count: items.length,
    getScrollElement: () => parentRef.current,
    estimateSize: () => 48, // 48px row height
    overscan: 10,
  });

  return (
    <div ref={parentRef} className="h-[500px] overflow-auto border rounded-md">
      <Table>
        <TableHeader className="sticky top-0 bg-background z-10 shadow-sm">
          <TableRow>
            <TableHead className="w-48">SKU Code</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Item Description</TableHead>
            <TableHead className="w-32 text-right">Available Stock</TableHead>
          </TableRow>
        </TableHeader>
        <TableBody style={{ height: `${rowVirtualizer.getTotalSize()}px`, position: 'relative' }}>
          {rowVirtualizer.getVirtualItems().map((virtualRow) => {
            const item = items[virtualRow.index];
            return (
              <TableRow
                key={item.sku}
                style={{
                  position: 'absolute',
                  top: 0,
                  left: 0,
                  width: '100%',
                  height: `${virtualRow.size}px`,
                  transform: `translateY(${virtualRow.start}px)`,
                }}
              >
                <TableCell className="font-mono text-xs">{item.sku}</TableCell>
                <TableCell>{item.name}</TableCell>
                <TableCell className="text-right font-medium">{item.quantity}</TableCell>
              </TableRow>
            );
          })}
        </TableBody>
      </Table>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility notes

- **Virtual list accessibility**: When virtualising large tables, ensure the outer container announces the total row count via `aria-rowcount={items.length}` and virtual rows specify `aria-rowindex={virtualRow.index + 1}`.
- **Debounced input announcements**: Do not fire screen reader status updates on every debounced keystroke. Announce results only after the query resolves with `aria-live="polite"`.

## Common mistakes

- **Importing everything from root**: Writing `import * as UI from '@innostes/ui'` defeats bundler tree-shaking in development environments, slowing down Hot Module Replacement (HMR).
- **Inline object props**: Passing objects like `style={{ color: 'red' }}` or `options={[{ id: 1 }]}` directly inside JSX recreates references on every tick, triggering downstream child re-renders.
- **Uncontrolled vs controlled oscillation**: Switching an input from `value={undefined}` to `value={state}` triggers React's uncontrolled-to-controlled warning and forces a layout remount. Always initialise state with empty strings `""`.

## Related components

- [`DataTable`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table) — High-performance table with built-in sorting and pagination.
- [`Table`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/table) — Primitive HTML table elements ideal for virtualisation integration.
- [`Input`](/ui/docs/components/forms/input) — Accessible text input supporting controlled and uncontrolled modes.
- [`CartesianCharts`](/ui/docs/charts/cartesian) — Isolated charting subpath.

## Permissions and roles (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/patterns/permissions-and-roles)

Access control UI design with PermissionMatrix, policy evaluation, and accessible disabled action guidance.

Enterprise software relies on strict Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) to enforce separation of duties, compliance audits, and statutory financial signoffs. This guide outlines how to represent permissions with [`PermissionMatrix`](/ui/docs/widgets/permission-matrix), decide between hiding versus disabling unauthorized controls, and communicate policy restrictions with accessible tooltips.

## The problem

Security implementations frequently introduce frustrating interface friction:
1. **The "Disappearing Button" dilemma**: Hiding controls completely leaves operators wondering whether a capability exists, whether their system is broken, or if they lack clearance.
2. **Dead-end disabled states**: Rendering a disabled button without contextual explanation leaves operators unable to diagnose why they cannot execute a workflow (e.g. "Why is Approve PO disabled?").
3. **Complex permission configuration**: Administrators face incomprehensible sprawling permission tables without granular inheritance or role assignment clarity.
4. **Client-side security assumptions**: Relying solely on client UI checks without matching server-side authorization enforcement opens severe privilege escalation vulnerabilities.

## Recommended approach

### Hiding vs disabling: The decision matrix

Follow this deterministic rubric when determining whether to hide or disable a UI element:

| Condition | UI Strategy | Implementation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **User lacks fundamental module access** | **Hide completely** | Do not render the route, sidebar navigation item, or page link. Prevents information disclosure about hidden capabilities. |
| **User has role, but lacks specific permission** | **Disable with Tooltip** | Render the action in a disabled state wrapped with [`Tooltip`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/tooltip) explaining the policy restriction and required role. |
| **Action blocked by business rule state** | **Disable with Tooltip** | Render disabled (e.g. "PO cannot be approved until two-way invoice match completes") to guide operator remediation. |
| **Audit-critical regulatory function** | **Render read-only** | Render a static value badge or lock icon rather than an interactive form input. |

## Explaining disabled actions accessibly

Native HTML `<button disabled>` elements do not trigger standard pointer or focus events in many browsers, causing tooltips wrapped directly around them to fail for keyboard and screen reader operators.

To ensure accessible tooltips on disabled actions:
1. Wrap the disabled control in an inline container element (such as a `<span>`).
2. Attach the `TooltipTrigger` to the wrapper container.
3. Ensure the disabled button includes `aria-disabled="true"` rather than native `disabled` when keyboard focusability is required to read the explanation.

```tsx
import { Button, Tooltip, TooltipTrigger, TooltipContent } from '@innostes/ui';

export function AuthorizeAction({ canAuthorize, reason }: { canAuthorize: boolean; reason?: string }) {
  if (canAuthorize) {
    return <Button variant="primary">Authorize disbursement</Button>;
  }

  return (
    <Tooltip>
      <TooltipTrigger asChild>
        {/* Wrapper span ensures pointer and focus events fire reliably */}
        <span tabIndex={0} className="inline-block cursor-not-allowed">
          <Button variant="primary" disabled className="pointer-events-none">
            Authorize disbursement
          </Button>
        </span>
      </TooltipTrigger>
      <TooltipContent>
        <p className="text-xs">{reason || 'Requires Finance Controller or VP approval rights.'}</p>
      </TooltipContent>
    </Tooltip>
  );
}
```

## Complete example: Northwind Role & Permission Management

The following recipe demonstrates how Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd configures administrative access across procurement modules using [`PermissionMatrix`](/ui/docs/widgets/permission-matrix):

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import {
  PermissionMatrix,
  PermissionMatrixSubject,
  PermissionMatrixAction,
  Card,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
  CardDescription,
  CardContent,
  Button,
  toast,
} from '@innostes/ui';
import { ShieldCheck, Save } from 'lucide-react';

const SYSTEM_SUBJECTS: PermissionMatrixSubject[] = [
  { id: 'purchase_orders', label: 'Purchase Orders & Contracts' },
  { id: 'vendor_invoices', label: 'Vendor Invoices & Three-Way Match' },
  { id: 'inventory_adjustments', label: 'Warehouse Stock Adjustments' },
  { id: 'tax_filings', label: 'GST & Statutory Compliance Reports' },
];

const SYSTEM_ACTIONS: PermissionMatrixAction[] = [
  { id: 'view', label: 'View records' },
  { id: 'create', label: 'Create drafts' },
  { id: 'edit', label: 'Edit active' },
  { id: 'approve', label: 'Approve & commit' },
  { id: 'delete', label: 'Archive / Delete' },
];

export function RolePermissionsManager() {
  // Current active permission matrix permissions map (subjectId -> actionId[])
  const [permissions, setPermissions] = useState<Record<string, string[]>>({
    purchase_orders: ['view', 'create', 'edit'],
    vendor_invoices: ['view', 'create'],
    inventory_adjustments: ['view'],
    tax_filings: ['view'],
  });

  const handleToggle = (subjectId: string, actionId: string) => {
    setPermissions((prev) => {
      const current = prev[subjectId] || [];
      const updated = current.includes(actionId)
        ? current.filter((id) => id !== actionId)
        : [...current, actionId];
      return { ...prev, [subjectId]: updated };
    });
  };

  const handleSave = () => {
    toast({
      title: 'Security policy updated',
      description: 'Role permissions for Senior Procurement Officer have been committed.',
    });
  };

  return (
    <Card className="max-w-4xl">
      <CardHeader className="flex flex-row items-start justify-between border-b pb-4">
        <div>
          <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
            <ShieldCheck className="h-5 w-5 text-primary" />
            <CardTitle>Role access control</CardTitle>
          </div>
          <CardDescription>
            Configuring operational boundaries for: <strong>Senior Procurement Officer</strong>
          </CardDescription>
        </div>
        <Button variant="primary" size="sm" onClick={handleSave}>
          <Save className="h-4 w-4 mr-2" />
          Save policy
        </Button>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent className="pt-6">
        <PermissionMatrix
          subjects={SYSTEM_SUBJECTS}
          actions={SYSTEM_ACTIONS}
          value={permissions}
          onChange={handleToggle}
          caption="Senior Procurement Officer access matrix"
        />
      </CardContent>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility notes

- **Interactive table semantics**: [`PermissionMatrix`](/ui/docs/widgets/permission-matrix) renders standard semantic `<table>` elements with accessible row headers (`scope="row"`) and column headers (`scope="col"`). Checkbox controls inside cells carry programmatic labels combining action and subject (e.g. `aria-label="Approve Purchase Orders & Contracts"`).
- **Keyboard navigation**: Matrix checkboxes support keyboard navigation via <kbd>Tab</kbd> and toggling via <kbd>Space</kbd>.
- **Screen reader announcements for disabled buttons**: For assistive technologies, pair disabled buttons with `aria-describedby` pointing to the explanatory guidance text or tooltip content ID.

## Common mistakes

- **Client-only gating**: Never rely exclusively on hiding a UI button for security. Malicious or compromised clients can forge HTTP requests directly to API routes. Client-side checks are purely ergonomics; all permissions must be verified on the server.
- **Ambiguous disabled labels**: Disabling a button without explaining why ("Approve" button disabled with no message) forces users to raise IT support tickets.
- **Hardcoding permissions in components**: Avoid hardcoding `role === 'admin'` checks across individual leaf components. Standardise checks behind declarative permission flags (e.g. `hasPermission('po.approve')`).

## Related components

- [`PermissionMatrix`](/ui/docs/widgets/permission-matrix) — Matrix grid for inspecting and toggling subject-action permission bindings.
- [`Tooltip`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/tooltip) — Accessible contextual floating hints for disabled actions.
- [`Badge`](/ui/docs/components/data-display/badge) — Status and security clearance level indicators.
- [`AlertDialog`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/alert-dialog) — High-privilege confirmation dialogues.

## Testing your app (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/patterns/testing)

Unit, integration, and end-to-end testing strategies with Testing Library, Vitest, jsdom polyfills, and Playwright.

Resilient enterprise software requires multi-tiered test automation covering business logic, user interaction flows, and accessibility compliance. This guide outlines how to test applications built with `@innostes/ui` using Vitest and React Testing Library for unit/integration tests, configure required jsdom polyfills, and write deterministic Playwright end-to-end tests.

## The problem

Testing modern design systems in enterprise apps introduces recurring challenges:
1. **Flaky DOM queries**: Relying on unstable CSS selectors or implementation details (`.btn-primary`, `div > span:nth-child(2)`) breaks tests during routine styling refactors.
2. **Missing browser APIs in jsdom**: Node test runners like Vitest and Jest use `jsdom`, which lacks `ResizeObserver`, `window.matchMedia`, and Web Animations APIs, throwing crashes during test execution.
3. **Portal detachment**: Overlays, dropdown menus, dialogs, and tooltips render into `document.body` through React portals. Calling `within(container).getByRole(...)` fails to find open modal content.
4. **Flaky asynchronous timing in E2E tests**: Using hardcoded `sleep(1000)` timeouts in Playwright tests creates flakiness under CI load.

## Recommended approach

- **Query by accessible role and name**: Always use `screen.getByRole('button', { name: /save/i })`, `screen.getByRole('dialog')`, and `screen.getByLabelText(...)`. This guarantees that tests interact with components exactly as assistive technologies experience them.
- **Configure standard jsdom polyfills**: Install polyfills for `ResizeObserver`, `matchMedia`, and `getAnimations` in your global test setup file.
- **Inspect `screen` for portal overlays**: Because `@innostes/ui` dialogs, sheets, and popovers render into the document body root, query them using `screen.getByRole` rather than searching within a local component test `container`.
- **User Event over FireEvent**: Use `@testing-library/user-event` to simulate realistic keystrokes, tab navigation, and focus transitions.

## Vitest test environment setup

Create a setup file (`vitest.setup.ts`) matching the test harness used internally by `@innostes/ui`:

```ts
import '@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest';
import { cleanup } from '@testing-library/react';
import { afterEach } from 'vitest';

// Automatically clean up DOM nodes after each test
afterEach(() => {
  cleanup();
});

// 1. Polyfill window.matchMedia for responsive and dark mode hooks
if (!window.matchMedia) {
  window.matchMedia = (query: string) =>
    ({
      matches: false,
      media: query,
      onchange: null,
      addEventListener: () => {},
      removeEventListener: () => {},
      addListener: () => {},
      removeListener: () => {},
      dispatchEvent: () => false,
    }) as MediaQueryList;
}

// 2. Polyfill ResizeObserver for charts and split panes
if (!('ResizeObserver' in window)) {
  class ResizeObserverStub {
    observe() {}
    unobserve() {}
    disconnect() {}
  }
  (window as unknown as { ResizeObserver: typeof ResizeObserverStub }).ResizeObserver =
    ResizeObserverStub;
}

// 3. Polyfill Element.prototype.getAnimations for Base UI transitions
if (!Element.prototype.getAnimations) {
  Element.prototype.getAnimations = () => [];
}
```

Reference this file in your `vitest.config.ts`:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  test: {
    environment: 'jsdom',
    setupFiles: ['./vitest.setup.ts'],
    globals: true,
  },
});
```

## Testing form workflows with Testing Library

Below is a complete integration test verifying user interaction, validation errors, and submission in a Northwind purchase order dialog:

```tsx
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest';
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogTrigger,
  DialogContent,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  Field,
  FieldLabel,
  Input,
  Button,
} from '@innostes/ui';
import { useState } from 'react';

function OrderModal({ onSubmit }: { onSubmit: (po: string) => void }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [po, setPo] = useState('');

  return (
    <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
      <DialogTrigger asChild>
        <Button variant="primary">Create PO</Button>
      </DialogTrigger>
      <DialogContent>
        <DialogHeader>
          <DialogTitle>New Purchase Order</DialogTitle>
        </DialogHeader>
        <form
          onSubmit={(e) => {
            e.preventDefault();
            onSubmit(po);
            setOpen(false);
          }}
          className="space-y-4 pt-4"
        >
          <Field id="po-input">
            <FieldLabel>PO Number</FieldLabel>
            <Input value={po} onChange={(e) => setPo(e.target.value)} placeholder="PO-2026-XXXX" />
          </Field>
          <Button type="submit" variant="primary">
            Confirm PO
          </Button>
        </form>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  );
}

describe('OrderModal Integration', () => {
  it('opens dialogue, accepts input, and submits successfully', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const handleSubmit = vi.fn();

    render(<OrderModal onSubmit={handleSubmit} />);

    // 1. Verify trigger exists and dialogue is not yet open
    const trigger = screen.getByRole('button', { name: /create po/i });
    expect(screen.queryByRole('dialog')).not.toBeInTheDocument();

    // 2. Click trigger to mount dialogue portal
    await user.click(trigger);

    // 3. Dialogue is rendered in document.body via Portal
    const dialog = await screen.findByRole('dialog');
    expect(dialog).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { name: /new purchase order/i })).toBeInTheDocument();

    // 4. Enter PO number
    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: /po number/i });
    await user.type(input, 'PO-2026-0912');

    // 5. Submit form
    const submitBtn = screen.getByRole('button', { name: /confirm po/i });
    await user.click(submitBtn);

    // 6. Assert callback was fired with typed value
    expect(handleSubmit).toHaveBeenCalledWith('PO-2026-0912');
  });
});
```

## Playwright end-to-end testing tips

For browser-level regression testing, write Playwright specs that evaluate accessible locators and keyboard flows:

```ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Vendor Directory E2E', () => {
  test('supports complete keyboard navigation and search filtering', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/vendors');

    // 1. Search for a specific vendor
    const searchInput = page.getByPlaceholder(/search vendors/i);
    await searchInput.fill('Kirloskar');

    // 2. Wait for debounced results to settle
    const vendorRow = page.getByRole('row', { name: /kirloskar electric/i });
    await expect(vendorRow).toBeVisible();

    // 3. Open actions dropdown with keyboard
    const actionBtn = vendorRow.getByRole('button', { name: /actions for kirloskar/i });
    await actionBtn.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');

    // 4. Navigate dropdown items
    const archiveMenuItem = page.getByRole('menuitem', { name: /archive vendor/i });
    await expect(archiveMenuItem).toBeVisible();
    await archiveMenuItem.click();

    // 5. Verify confirmation alertdialog appears
    const alertDialog = page.getByRole('alertdialog');
    await expect(alertDialog).toBeVisible();
    await expect(alertDialog.getByText(/archive vendor account/i)).toBeVisible();

    // 6. Dismiss with Escape key
    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect(alertDialog).not.toBeVisible();
  });

  test('maintains accessible visual contrast in dark mode', async ({ page }) => {
    // Emulate dark mode media feature
    await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark' });
    await page.goto('/dashboard');

    const kpiCard = page.getByText(/active purchase commitments/i);
    await expect(kpiCard).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```

## Accessibility notes

- **Avoid querying by test ID**: Using `data-testid` hides broken accessibility names from test suites. If a test cannot find a button by its role and accessible name, assistive software cannot find it either.
- **Test focus traps**: When verifying modal dialogs, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> multiple times and confirm that focus remains trapped inside the active overlay.
- **Verify polite announcements**: For alerts and toasts, assert that the wrapping container exposes `aria-live="polite"` or `role="alert"`.

## Common mistakes

- **Testing implementation details**: Asserting internal React state variables instead of rendered DOM text or input values couples tests to internal component refactoring.
- **Forgetting `userEvent.setup()`**: Using `userEvent.click()` directly without initialising `const user = userEvent.setup()` can cause state synchronization issues in modern Testing Library versions.
- **Querying closed portal elements**: Asserting that a modal or tooltip is hidden with `getByRole` throws an error. Always use `queryByRole` when asserting non-existence.

## Related components

- [`Dialog`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dialog) — Modal dialog with portal rendering and focus management.
- [`AlertDialog`](/ui/docs/components/overlays/alert-dialog) — High-consequence confirmation dialogue.
- [`Field`](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) — Accessible form wrapper connecting label, input, and errors.
- [`Input`](/ui/docs/components/forms/input) — Accessible text control.

## [1.0.0] - 2026-10-29

### Highlights

The `1.0.0` release establishes `@innostes/ui` as a battle-tested, production-ready enterprise design system for Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd. Built on unstyled Base UI primitives and styled with OKLCH design tokens, this release delivers complete accessibility, multi-runtime support (React 17, 18, and 19), and modular entry points.

### Added

- **5 New Composite Widgets**:
  - `ActivityFeed`: Audit log and timeline streams with relative timestamping.
  - `EntityList`: Compact master-list view for enterprise data navigation.
  - `QuickActions`: Role-based command palette action strip.
  - `WelcomeBanner`: Dismissible role-aware onboarding hero banner.
  - `ActionList`: Keyboard-navigable action rows with badge tags.
- **Dedicated Modular Entry Points**:
  - `@innostes/ui/charts`: High-level Cartesian and Donut chart visualisations powered by Recharts with OKLCH theme tokens.
  - `@innostes/ui/editor`: Rich text editor powered by Tiptap with formatting toolbars and validation states.
- **Enterprise Primitives Hardened on Base UI**:
  - Complete ARIA labelling, keyboard navigation, and roving tabindex on `Button`, `ButtonGroup`, `Toggle`, `ToggleGroup`, `Field`, `Input`, `Textarea`, `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`, `Select`, `Combobox`, `NumberField`, and `Slider`.
  - Floating overlays: `Dialog`, `AlertDialog`, `Sheet`, `Popover`, `Tooltip`, `DropdownMenu`, and `ContextMenu` supporting logical start and end positioning and RTL mirroring.
  - Data display & navigation: `DataTable` with server-side sorting/pagination, `Table`, `Card`, `Stat`, `Badge`, `Avatar`, `EmptyState`, `Kbd`, `Tabs`, `Breadcrumb`, `Pagination`, `Accordion`, `Collapsible`, `Sidebar`, `PageHeader`, and `SplitPane`.
- **Theme Tokens & Dark Mode**:
  - Semantic OKLCH colour scale with APCA/WCAG 2.1 AA compliant contrast.
  - Zero-runtime CSS variables with `@innostes/ui/tailwind.css`, `@innostes/ui/theme.css`, and `@innostes/ui/dark.css`.
  - Standalone precompiled stylesheet `@innostes/ui/styles.css` for consumers without Tailwind CSS.
- **Multi-React Runtime Compatibility**:
  - Fully tested and verified across React 17, React 18, and React 19 test environments.
- **TSDoc & Machine-Readable Metadata**:
  - Complete British English docstrings across all exported component props.
  - Machine-readable `dist/api.json` extracted from TSDoc for automated documentation.

### Changed

- Promoted library to stable SemVer `1.0.0`.
- Clamped `Progress` and `Meter` percentage bounds strictly between 0 and 100 with localized `aria-valuetext` formatters.
- Updated `Breadcrumb` active state resolution to prevent spurious navigation warnings; non-terminal items default to links whilst current item renders text with `aria-current="page"`.
- Aligned `Dialog` and `Sheet` positioning props to logical CSS attributes (`side="start" | "end"`).
- Re-architected `DataTable` column definitions to use canonical `id` and `cell` render functions.
- Renamed notification bell component to `NotificationBell` exported from `@innostes/ui`.

### Security

- Created formal vulnerability disclosure process with dedicated contact (`security@innostes.com`) and 48-hour initial response SLA.
- Added strict XSS sanitisation guidance for `RichTextEditor` HTML output using DOMPurify.
- Implemented file type and size validation policies in `FileDropzone`.

---

## Contributing (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/resources/contributing)

Development guidelines, code standards, and PR submission workflows.

# Contributing

We welcome contributions from engineering teams across Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd. This guide outlines the development workflow, coding conventions, and verification steps required before submitting pull requests to `@innostes/ui`.

For in-depth architectural rules and internal codebase conventions, refer to the internal [CONTRIBUTING.md in packages/ui](https://github.com/innostes/erp/blob/main/packages/ui/CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Local development setup

Clone the repository and install workspace dependencies:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/innostes/erp.git
cd erp
pnpm install
```

Start the interactive documentation development server:

```bash
pnpm nx dev landing
```

Visit `http://localhost:3000/ui/docs` to preview documentation changes live.

---

## Component submission checklist

Every new or modified component must satisfy the following criteria:

- **Base UI foundation**: Built on unstyled Base UI primitives wherever applicable, preserving keyboard focus loops and ARIA attributes.
- **Logical styling**: Uses Tailwind CSS v4 design tokens and logical directional properties (`ps-`, `pe-`, `start-`, `end-`) rather than absolute left/right coordinates.
- **Accessibility (a11y)**: Conforms to WCAG 2.1 AA standards, provides default ARIA roles, and supports full keyboard navigation (Enter, Space, Tab, and Arrow keys).
- **Right-to-Left (RTL)**: Tested and verified under RTL layout direction (`dir="rtl"`).
- **Complete TSDoc**: All exported components and prop interfaces feature full British English docstrings with default values and usage notes.
- **Multi-runtime test coverage**: Accompanied by Vitest unit tests covering rendering, keyboard interaction, and accessibility attributes. Tests must pass across React 17, 18, and 19.
- **Documentation & demo**: Accompanied by a 7-section documentation page under `apps/landing/content/docs/` and an interactive demo in `apps/landing/components/demos/`.

---

## Verification gates

Before submitting a pull request, run the complete verification pipeline locally:

```bash
# 1. Typecheck and unit tests
pnpm nx run-many -t test typecheck build -p ui --skip-nx-cache

# 2. Multi-React compatibility suites
pnpm nx run-many -t test typecheck -p ui-react17-tests ui-react18-tests --skip-nx-cache

# 3. Documentation quality gates
pnpm nx run landing:docs-check

# 4. Production build verification
pnpm nx build landing --skip-nx-cache
```

All quality gates must exit with code 0 before code review.

---

## API Conventions (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/resources/conventions)

Core architectural principles, state models, polymorphic composition, and styling conventions across @innostes/ui.

`@innostes/ui` adheres to strict architectural conventions across all primitives. Learning these conventions allows developers to predict prop names, event payloads, composition patterns, and styling hooks across the entire design system.

## Composition & exports

All components are exported as flat, named exports from the package entry points. Primitives with multiple child slots (such as `Dialog`, `Select`, or `Tabs`) are imported individually rather than accessed via namespaces:

```tsx
import { Dialog, DialogTrigger, DialogContent, DialogTitle } from '@innostes/ui';
import { MetricCard } from '@innostes/ui/widgets';
import { CartesianCharts } from '@innostes/ui/charts';
```

All exports are fully tree-shakeable: your bundler includes only the code for components your application imports.

## Controlled & uncontrolled state

Every stateful primitive supports both uncontrolled and controlled operation using standard React naming conventions:

| Uncontrolled prop | Controlled prop | Change callback | Event details payload |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `defaultValue` | `value` | `onValueChange(value, eventDetails)` | `{ reason?: string; event: Event }` |
| `defaultOpen` | `open` | `onOpenChange(open, eventDetails)` | `{ reason?: string; event: Event }` |
| `defaultChecked` | `checked` | `onCheckedChange(checked, eventDetails)` | `{ event: Event }` |
| `defaultPressed` | `pressed` | `onPressedChange(pressed, eventDetails)` | `{ event: Event }` |

### Event details pattern

Callbacks pass the updated value as the first argument, followed by an optional `eventDetails` object indicating the origin trigger (e.g. keyboard escape vs pointer click):

```tsx
<Dialog
  open={isOpen}
  onOpenChange={(nextOpen, details) => {
    if (!nextOpen && details?.reason === 'outside-press') {
      // Prevent closing when user clicks outside modal
      return;
    }
    setIsOpen(nextOpen);
  }}
>
  {/* Modal contents */}
</Dialog>
```

## Polymorphism with the `render` prop

`@innostes/ui` avoids the legacy Radix `asChild` pattern. Instead, primitives built on Base UI utilize the **`render` prop** pattern. This merges accessibility attributes, focus handlers, and class names directly into the custom child element:

```tsx
import Link from 'next/link';
import { Button } from '@innostes/ui';

// Compose an accessible button that renders as a Next.js client link
<Button
  variant="primary"
  nativeButton={false}
  render={<Link href="/orders/PO-2026-0881" />}
>
  View purchase order
</Button>
```

When delegating button rendering to a link element (`<a>`), specify `nativeButton={false}` so the component does not emit an invalid HTML `<button>` inside an anchor.

## Customisation

`@innostes/ui` provides four distinct layers for styling overrides:

### 1. The `className` prop

The `className` prop applies to the component root. Passed classes are merged through `tailwind-merge`, ensuring that user-provided utilities override internal defaults:

```tsx
<Button className="w-full justify-start font-mono">
  PO-2026-0881
</Button>
```

On interactive primitives, `className` can also accept a function receiving the current component state:

```tsx
<Button className={({ disabled }) => (disabled ? 'opacity-40 cursor-not-allowed' : '')}>
  Submit order
</Button>
```

### 2. Multi-part styling with `classNames`

Composite widgets and complex data display components provide a `classNames` prop accepting a map of slot names to utility strings:

```tsx
<MetricCard
  label="Total Procurement"
  value="₹1,45,280.00"
  classNames={{
    root: 'border-blue-500/30 bg-blue-50/10',
    label: 'text-blue-700 dark:text-blue-400 font-semibold',
    value: 'font-mono text-2xl tracking-tight',
  }}
/>
```

### 3. The `data-slot` attribute

Every internal element emits a deterministic `data-slot` attribute (e.g. `data-slot="dialog-content"`, `data-slot="card-header"`). You can target child slots from parent stylesheets or container selectors:

```css
/* Customise all metric card values inside a financial summary section */
.finance-overview [data-slot="metric-card-value"] {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  color: var(--color-emerald-700);
}
```

### 4. Interactive state attributes

Primitives expose interactive state via HTML `data-*` attributes (`data-state="open"`, `data-checked`, `data-disabled`, `data-highlighted`, `data-invalid`). You can style these states using Tailwind CSS variants:

```tsx
<div className="border-border data-invalid:border-destructive data-invalid:ring-destructive">
  {/* Field contents */}
</div>
```

### 5. Server-safe variant helpers

Every styled component exports its underlying class-variance-authority helper function (e.g. `buttonVariants()`, `badgeVariants()`, `inputVariants()`). These functions are pure JavaScript and execute safely on the server:

```tsx
import { buttonVariants } from '@innostes/ui';

// Generate button styles for standard HTML or external router links
const linkClasses = buttonVariants({ variant: 'outline', size: 'sm' });
```

## Ref forwarding

Every component wraps its DOM root in React's `forwardRef`. Refs point directly to native DOM elements (`HTMLButtonElement`, `HTMLDivElement`, `HTMLInputElement`), allowing direct integration with form management libraries (such as React Hook Form) across React 17, React 18, and React 19.

## Server Components & client boundaries

- **Interactive components** declare `'use client'` at their file headers. You can import them directly into Server Components in Next.js App Router without manual wrappers.
- **Pure helpers** (`cn()`, `formatDate()`, `buttonVariants()`, `badgeVariants()`) do not import browser-specific APIs and execute on both client and server.

## Standard size scale

Interactive controls share a unified size scale so adjacent controls align in toolbars and data tables:

| Size | Height | Recommended application |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `sm` | 32px | High-density audit grids, compact filter bars, table pagination |
| `md` | 40px | Standard forms, default modal actions, primary toolbars |
| `lg` | 48px | Mobile ERP terminals, high-consequence confirmation dialogs |

## Internationalisation & RTL support

All customer-facing text is customizable to support enterprise multi-language requirements. Rather than hardcoding English strings, components expose override props:

- `closeLabel`: Dialog, Alert, Sheet dismissal labels (defaults to `"Close"`).
- `labels`: Component-specific string maps (e.g. `labels={{ previousPage: 'Previous', nextPage: 'Next' }}` on `Pagination`).
- **Logical CSS properties**: Styles use CSS logical properties (`margin-inline-end`, `inset-inline-start`, `border-inline-start`) instead of physical directions (`left`, `right`, `mr-`, `ml-`). Wrap the application in `<DirectionProvider direction="rtl">` for Arabic, Hebrew, or Urdu localization.

---

## FAQ (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/resources/faq)

Frequently asked questions regarding @innostes/ui installation, theming, and usage.

# Frequently asked questions

Real-world questions, architecture comparisons, and troubleshooting advice for `@innostes/ui`.

## Architecture & Comparisons

### How does innostes UI compare with shadcn/ui and Radix?

`shadcn/ui` is a copy-paste distribution model using Radix UI primitives and Tailwind CSS. While excellent for greenfield applications, enterprise ERP deployments require centralised governance, automated regression testing, and predictable package upgrades.

`@innostes/ui` provides:
- **Centralised package distribution**: A single versioned package (`@innostes/ui`) maintained and upgraded via standard package managers.
- **Base UI foundation**: Modern unstyled primitives developed by the Base UI team, delivering zero-runtime overhead, refined focus rings, and native accessibility.
- **Enterprise-first primitives**: Built-in data tables, split panes, complex filter bars, audit logs, and permission matrices designed specifically for back-office and admin applications.

### How does innostes UI compare with Ant Design or MUI?

Ant Design and Material UI bundle substantial JavaScript runtimes and opinionated CSS-in-JS engines. `@innostes/ui` uses zero-runtime CSS custom properties and atomic Tailwind utility classes, achieving a root bundle footprint under 15 KB (raw) compared to hundreds of kilobytes in monolithic component frameworks.

---

## Installation & Setup

### Do I need Tailwind CSS to use @innostes/ui?

No. If your project does not use Tailwind CSS, you can import our precompiled stylesheet:

```ts
import '@innostes/ui/styles.css';
import '@innostes/ui/dark.css'; // Optional dark mode
```

This single stylesheet delivers all utility rules and token variables necessary for proper component rendering without requiring a Tailwind build step.

### Why do I get missing peer dependency warnings for recharts or tiptap?

`@innostes/ui` isolates heavy dependencies into optional entry points (`@innostes/ui/charts` and `@innostes/ui/editor`). If your application does not require chart visualisations or rich text editing, you can safely ignore these peer dependency warnings. If you use those subpaths, install the corresponding peer dependencies:

```bash
pnpm add recharts@^3.0.0
pnpm add @tiptap/core@^3.0.0 @tiptap/react@^3.0.0 @tiptap/starter-kit@^3.0.0
```

---

## Theming & Styling

### How do I customise brand colours?

`@innostes/ui` uses OKLCH CSS custom properties. You can override individual tokens in your application's CSS without modifying component source files:

```css
:root {
  --primary: oklch(0.55 0.22 260); /* Custom brand blue */
  --primary-foreground: oklch(0.98 0 0);
  --radius: 0.5rem;
}
```

Every component consuming `--primary` will immediately reflect your updated brand palette.

### How does dark mode toggling work?

Components consume the CSS variables defined in `@innostes/ui/dark.css`. Dark mode is activated whenever a parent DOM node has the `.dark` class or the `[data-theme="dark"]` attribute:

```html
<html class="dark">
  <!-- All nested @innostes/ui components render dark theme -->
</html>
```

---

## Next.js & Server Components

### Are components compatible with the Next.js App Router?

Yes. Interactive primitives (buttons, modals, dropdowns) include the `"use client"` directive, allowing them to be imported directly into Next.js App Router layouts and pages. Non-interactive helpers (`cn`, `buttonVariants`) remain server-safe.

## Migration guides (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/resources/migration)

Upgrade instructions and breaking change migrations between major versions.

# Migration guides

Detailed upgrade procedures, codified breaking changes, and migration steps for `@innostes/ui`.

## Migration template

When planning a major version migration within your application codebase, follow this standard procedure:

1. **Audit dependencies**: Ensure peer dependencies (`react`, `react-dom`, `recharts`, `@tiptap/*`) meet the minimum specified requirements for the new target version.
2. **Review breaking changes**: Cross-reference the migration section below against your application imports.
3. **Execute codemods or automated search**: Search for deprecated prop identifiers and update call sites.
4. **Execute local test suites**: Run your TypeScript compiler (`tsc --noEmit`) and component test suites (`pnpm test`) to catch type-level or DOM assertion mismatches.
5. **Verify visual regressions**: Confirm that critical enterprise layouts (e.g. data tables, navigation sidebars, and dialogue modals) render faithfully.

---

## Migrating from 0.0.1 to 1.0.0

The `1.0.0` release introduces architectural hardening, full WAI-ARIA conformance via Base UI primitives, and logical layout properties. Follow the migration steps below to upgrade your application.

### Step 1: Update package dependencies

Update `@innostes/ui` in your project `package.json`:

```bash
pnpm update @innostes/ui@^1.0.0
```

If you utilise charts or rich text editing, install the corresponding optional peer dependencies:

```bash
# Optional: only if using charts
pnpm add recharts@^3.0.0

# Optional: only if using rich text editing
pnpm add @tiptap/core@^3.0.0 @tiptap/react@^3.0.0 @tiptap/starter-kit@^3.0.0
```

---

### Step 2: Address breaking component changes

#### 1. Breadcrumb active state resolution

In version 0.0.1, passing active state to `BreadcrumbItem` sometimes emitted nested anchor tag warnings. In 1.0.0, non-terminal items should render anchor links while the active page item renders plain text with `aria-current="page"`.

```tsx
// Before (0.0.1)
<BreadcrumbItem active href="/orders">Orders</BreadcrumbItem>

// After (1.0.0)
<BreadcrumbItem isCurrent>Orders</BreadcrumbItem>
```

#### 2. Progress and Meter percentage bounds

Values are now strictly clamped between 0 and 100. If your domain values operate on arbitrary scales (e.g. raw inventory count), normalize the value before passing it to `value`:

```tsx
// Before (0.0.1)
<Progress value={250} max={500} />

// After (1.0.0)
// Normalize value to a 0–100 percentage:
<Progress value={(250 / 500) * 100} aria-valuetext="250 of 500 units" />
```

#### 3. Dialog and Sheet logical positioning

Directional literals (`"left"` and `"right"`) have been replaced with logical CSS properties (`"start"` and `"end"`) to provide automatic Right-to-Left (RTL) mirroring:

```tsx
// Before (0.0.1)
<SheetContent side="right">

// After (1.0.0)
<SheetContent side="end">
```

#### 4. DataTable column definitions

The `DataTable` column schema has been normalized to use canonical `id` and `cell` render properties, aligning with TanStack Table and modern headless conventions:

```tsx
// Before (0.0.1)
const columns = [
  { key: 'status', header: 'Status', render: (row) => <Badge>{row.status}</Badge> }
];

// After (1.0.0)
const columns = [
  { id: 'status', header: 'Status', cell: (row) => <Badge>{row.status}</Badge> }
];
```

#### 5. RichTextEditor validation prop

`RichTextEditor` now accepts an explicit `invalid?: boolean` prop for uniform integration with `<Field>` validation contexts:

```tsx
// Before (0.0.1)
<RichTextEditor className={errors.body ? 'border-destructive' : ''} />

// After (1.0.0)
<RichTextEditor invalid={Boolean(errors.body)} />
```

#### 6. Notification bell component export

The notification bell component has been normalized to the canonical export name `NotificationBell`:

```tsx
// Before (0.0.1)
import { NotificationBellWidget } from '@innostes/ui';

// After (1.0.0)
import { NotificationBell } from '@innostes/ui';
```

---

### Step 3: Run verification checks

After making the above adjustments, run your project validation pipeline:

```bash
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
```

---

## Security (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/resources/security)

Security practices, vulnerability reporting, and dependency auditing.

# Security

Security is foundational to the development lifecycle of `@innostes/ui`. Because the library runs in mission-critical enterprise environments handling sensitive commercial and financial data for Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd, all primitives and entry points undergo rigorous security assessments.

## Reporting a vulnerability

If you discover a potential security vulnerability within `@innostes/ui` or its submodules, please report it privately:

- **Email**: Send vulnerability disclosures to `security@innostes.com`.
- **Public channels**: Please do NOT create public GitHub issues or forum threads for undisclosed vulnerabilities.
- **Payload details**: Please include step-by-step reproduction instructions, affected package versions, and a minimal reproducible example or proof-of-concept.

### Response service level agreements (SLAs)

| Stage | Target Timeline | Action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Acknowledgement** | Within 24 hours | Initial intake confirmation and vulnerability ticket creation. |
| **Triage & Impact Assessment** | Within 72 hours | Verification of affected versions and reproduction in an isolated environment. |
| **Remediation & Patch** | Within 7 business days | Production of security hotfix, CI verification, and publication to npm registry. |
| **Public Advisory** | Coordinated disclosure | Release notes and CVE publication following consumer patching window. |

---

## Component security considerations

### 1. Rich text editor (`@innostes/ui/editor`)

The `RichTextEditor` primitive is built upon Tiptap and emits formatted HTML strings. Unsanitised HTML rendering can expose web applications to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks.

- **Client sanitisation**: Always sanitize raw HTML strings produced by the editor before rendering them with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Use established sanitisation libraries such as [DOMPurify](https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify):
  ```tsx
  import DOMPurify from 'dompurify';

  export function SafeArticleContent({ html }: { html: string }) {
    const cleanHtml = DOMPurify.sanitize(html, {
      ALLOWED_TAGS: ['b', 'i', 'em', 'strong', 'a', 'p', 'ul', 'ol', 'li', 'h1', 'h2', 'h3', 'code', 'pre', 'blockquote'],
      ALLOWED_ATTR: ['href', 'target', 'rel', 'class'],
    });

    return <div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: cleanHtml }} />;
  }
  ```
- **Server sanitisation**: Apply identical sanitisation rules on your backend APIs before writing editor payloads to PostgreSQL or document databases.

### 2. File dropzone (`@innostes/ui`)

The `FileDropzone` component provides client-side file selection, file count limits, and MIME type filtering via the `accept` attribute.

- **Do not trust client-side validation**: The `accept` prop provides user experience hints to operating system file selectors. Malicious actors can easily bypass client checks and upload arbitrary binary payloads.
- **Server validation**: Server endpoints must inspect magic bytes and file headers to verify genuine MIME types, rather than relying solely on file extensions.
- **Storage isolation**: Store uploaded assets in isolated Amazon S3 / Google Cloud Storage buckets using generated UUID filenames, ensuring non-executable permissions.

---

## Dependency policy and supply chain security

To protect against software supply chain attacks:

1. **Automated audits**: Every CI pipeline execution runs `pnpm audit --audit-level=high`. Pull requests introducing vulnerabilities are automatically blocked.
2. **Pinned dependency trees**: Dependencies are strictly pinned using `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
3. **Zero runtime bloat**: Core `@innostes/ui` primitives maintain only 4 production dependencies (`@base-ui/react`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, and `class-variance-authority`). Heavy charting and rich text dependencies are strictly isolated to optional peer dependencies.

---

## Versioning and support (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/resources/versioning)

Semantic versioning policy, release lifecycle, and browser compatibility targets.

# Versioning and support

The `@innostes/ui` package follows [Semantic Versioning (SemVer 2.0.0)](https://semver.org/). Version numbers adhere to the `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` structure, providing predictable upgrade paths for Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd's engineering teams.

## SemVer policy

We adhere strictly to semantic guarantees across our public API surface.

| Release Type | Version Segment | Frequency | Backwards Compatibility | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Patch** | `x.x.PATCH` | Weekly / As needed | Fully compatible | Bug fixes, internal refactoring, accessibility refinements, and documentation updates. |
| **Minor** | `x.MINOR.0` | Monthly | Fully compatible | New components, opt-in prop additions, non-breaking behavioural enhancements, and deprecation notices. |
| **Major** | `MAJOR.0.0` | 6–12 months | Breaking changes | Breaking API changes, DOM restructuring, removal of deprecated features, or runtime minimum bumps. |

### What constitutes a breaking change?

To maintain predictable enterprise stability, the following modifications are classified as **breaking** and will only occur in major releases:

1. **TypeScript signatures**: Removing or renaming exported component props, changing required prop contracts, or narrowing callback argument types.
2. **DOM hierarchy & `data-slot` names**: Removing, renaming, or changing the nesting order of elements marked with `data-slot="..."`, as consumers rely on these selectors for CSS overrides.
3. **Component lifecycle & events**: Altering the signature or invocation sequence of event callbacks (e.g. `onValueChange`, `onOpenChange`).
4. **Theme token variables**: Removing or renaming semantic CSS custom properties in `@innostes/ui/theme.css`.
5. **Runtime peer dependencies**: Raising minimum supported versions of React, Next.js, or Node.js.

### What does not constitute a breaking change?

The following modifications are considered **non-breaking**:

- Adding new optional props to existing components.
- Adding new `data-slot` elements or auxiliary helper functions.
- Internal CSS optimizations that preserve rendered visual geometry and WCAG contrast compliance.
- Bug fixes that restore intended specification behaviour.

## Deprecation policy

When an existing API or component is superseded, we follow an orderly deprecation lifecycle before removal:

1. **Deprecation announcement**: The feature is marked as deprecated in a minor release. TSDoc annotations (`@deprecated`) are added to trigger IDE strikethrough warnings.
2. **Runtime warnings**: In development mode (`process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'`), invoking a deprecated prop logs a single formatted console warning with instructions on the replacement pattern. No warnings are emitted in production bundles.
3. **Grace period**: Deprecated APIs remain supported for a minimum of **two minor versions** or **six months**, whichever is longer.
4. **Removal**: Deprecated APIs are permanently removed only upon the subsequent major version release.

## Support matrix

`@innostes/ui` is engineered and tested for enterprise browsers, modern SSR environments, and multiple React runtime versions.

### React runtime matrix

All primitives undergo automated compatibility testing across our target React versions:

| Package | Supported Version Range | Verification Suite |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **React 19** | `^19.0.0` | Primary development target (`pnpm nx test ui`) |
| **React 18** | `^18.0.0` | Isolated runner (`tests/ui-react18`) |
| **React 17** | `^17.0.0` | Isolated runner (`tests/ui-react17`) |
| **Next.js** | `>= 14.0.0` (App Router & Pages Router) | Smoke tested in `apps/landing` and `apps/web-app` |
| **Vite** | `>= 5.0.0` | Verified with `@vitejs/plugin-react` |

### Browser support

We support modern evergreen desktop and mobile browsers. Our build configuration targets the following minimum baseline:

| Browser | Minimum Version | Market Coverage |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chromium** (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera) | 120+ | Full support (WAI-ARIA, OKLCH colours, CSS Container Queries) |
| **Mozilla Firefox** | 120+ | Full support |
| **Apple Safari** (macOS) | 17+ | Full support |
| **Apple Safari** (iOS) | 17+ | Full support |

> [!NOTE]
> Internet Explorer and legacy Microsoft Edge (EdgeHTML) are strictly unsupported.

### Server-side execution

- **Node.js**: LTS `20.x` and `22.x` are supported for Next.js App Router Server Components, static site generation, and CLI build tooling.
- **SSR Safety**: Interactive components ship with explicit `"use client"` directives. Pure utility functions (such as `cn` and `buttonVariants`) contain no browser APIs and remain safe for Server Component evaluation.

## Security maintenance window

Security vulnerability remediations are prioritized according to release status:

- **Current major release** (v1.x): Receives immediate patch releases for all critical, high, and moderate security findings.
- **Previous major release** (v0.x): Receives critical security patches for 12 months following supersession.
- **End-of-Life (EOL)** releases: No security patches are guaranteed. Teams must upgrade to an actively supported version.

---

## Theming & Design Tokens (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/theming)

Semantic design token architecture, OKLCH colour system, theme overrides, multi-tenant scoping, and generated token reference.

import { TokenReference } from '@/components/docs/token-reference';
import { ThemingDemo } from '@/components/docs/button-demos';

`@innostes/ui` styles every primitive through **semantic design tokens**. Instead of scattering arbitrary hex codes or hardcoded utility classes across markup, components reference role-based CSS custom properties such as `bg-primary`, `text-muted-foreground`, and `border-border`.

<ThemingDemo />

## How tokens work

The design token system operates on three foundational principles:

1. **Role-based abstraction**: Tokens represent functional interface roles (`card`, `primary`, `destructive`, `muted`) rather than literal colours. Swapping a primary action colour requires changing one variable.
2. **Foreground pairing**: Every container or surface token has a strictly coupled foreground counterpart (`primary-foreground`, `card-foreground`, `destructive-foreground`) guaranteed to satisfy WCAG 2.2 AA contrast ratios.
3. **Perceptual uniformity with OKLCH**: Dark mode and theme overrides use the OKLCH colour model (`oklch(L C H)`), ensuring linear lightness transitions without unpredictable perceived brightness shifts across different hues.

## Overriding tokens

### Tailwind CSS v4

In Tailwind v4, declare custom tokens inside your `@theme` block. Because `@innostes/ui/tailwind.css` marks defaults with `@theme default`, any rule defined in your application stylesheet takes precedence:

```css title="app/globals.css"
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@innostes/ui/tailwind.css";
@import "@innostes/ui/dark.css";

@theme {
  /* Override primary action to forest emerald */
  --color-primary: oklch(50.8% 0.144 164.215);
  --color-primary-hover: oklch(43.5% 0.138 164.5);
  --color-primary-foreground: oklch(100% 0 0);

  /* Adjust border rounding */
  --radius-md: 0.5rem;
}
```

### Tailwind CSS v3

For Tailwind v3, map the CSS custom properties inside your `tailwind.config.js`:

```js title="tailwind.config.js"
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
module.exports = {
  theme: {
    extend: {
      colors: {
        primary: {
          DEFAULT: 'var(--color-primary)',
          hover: 'var(--color-primary-hover)',
          foreground: 'var(--color-primary-foreground)',
        },
      },
    },
  },
};
```

### Without Tailwind CSS

When using plain CSS, override variables on `:root` or a scoped selector:

```css title="styles/theme.css"
:root {
  --color-primary: #059669;
  --color-primary-hover: #047857;
  --color-primary-foreground: #ffffff;
}
```

## Scoped themes

Because tokens are standard CSS custom properties, you can scope different themes to specific DOM branches without affecting the rest of the application:

```css title="app/globals.css"
/* Scoped finance sub-ledger theme */
.theme-finance {
  --color-primary: oklch(50.8% 0.144 164.215);
  --color-primary-hover: oklch(43.5% 0.138 164.5);
  --color-primary-foreground: oklch(100% 0 0);
  --color-card: oklch(98% 0.01 160);
}
```

Apply the class to any enclosing element:

```tsx title="app/finance/page.tsx"
import { Button, Card } from '@innostes/ui';

export function FinanceSection() {
  return (
    <div className="theme-finance p-6">
      <Card>
        <p className="text-sm">Northwind Traders Accounting Module</p>
        <Button variant="primary">Generate Balance Sheet</Button>
      </Card>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## White-label & multi-tenant theming

In multi-tenant ERP deployments, different subsidiaries or client organisations require distinct branding. Implement this by dynamically injecting tenant-specific CSS variables at runtime:

```tsx title="components/tenant-provider.tsx"
import * as React from 'react';

interface TenantTheme {
  primary: string;
  primaryHover: string;
  primaryForeground: string;
}

const TENANT_THEMES: Record<string, TenantTheme> = {
  'northwind-bengaluru': {
    primary: 'oklch(54.6% 0.245 262.881)', // Blue
    primaryHover: 'oklch(48.8% 0.243 264.376)',
    primaryForeground: 'oklch(100% 0 0)',
  },
  'western-logistics': {
    primary: 'oklch(50.8% 0.144 164.215)', // Emerald
    primaryHover: 'oklch(43.5% 0.138 164.5)',
    primaryForeground: 'oklch(100% 0 0)',
  },
};

export function TenantProvider({
  tenantId,
  children,
}: {
  tenantId: string;
  children: React.ReactNode;
}) {
  const theme = TENANT_THEMES[tenantId] || TENANT_THEMES['northwind-bengaluru'];

  const style = {
    '--color-primary': theme.primary,
    '--color-primary-hover': theme.primaryHover,
    '--color-primary-foreground': theme.primaryForeground,
  } as React.CSSProperties;

  return (
    <div data-tenant={tenantId} style={style}>
      {children}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Complete token reference

The table below is generated directly from `theme.css` and `dark.css` at build time, displaying the light theme OKLCH value, dark theme OKLCH value, and an interactive swatch for every semantic token:

<TokenReference />

## Action List (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/action-list)

Actionable task queues pairing descriptions, status icons, and dedicated resolution buttons.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/action-list/basic" align="start" className="p-4 sm:p-4" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  ActionList,
  type ActionListItem,
  type ActionListProps,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `ActionList` when presenting a queue of distinct tasks that need operator decision or approval:

- **Pending managerial authorizations**: Approving purchase orders, expense claims, or credit notes.
- **Compliance review queues**: Reconciling GSTIN discrepancies or reviewing vendor TDS declarations.
- **Operational triage lists**: Discrepancies flagged during warehouse receiving.

**Do not use ActionList for:**
- Non-actionable audit logs without buttons — use [ActivityFeed](/ui/docs/widgets/activity-feed).
- Full enterprise bulk approvals — use [DataTable](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table) with row selection.
- General application shortcut triggers — use [QuickActions](/ui/docs/widgets/quick-actions).

## Examples

### Pending purchase order approvals inside WidgetCard

Pairing `ActionList` with `WidgetCard` and an unread count badge:

```tsx
<WidgetCard
  title="Pending authorizations"
  description="Procurement requests requiring managerial sign-off"
  count={3}
  countTone="primary"
>
  <ActionList
    divided
    items={[
      {
        id: '1',
        title: 'Approve purchase order PO-2026-081',
        description: 'Bengaluru Spices Pvt Ltd · ₹89,400',
        icon: <Clock className="size-4" />,
        tone: 'primary',
        action: {
          label: 'Approve',
          variant: 'primary',
          onClick: () => handleApprove('PO-2026-081'),
        },
      },
      {
        id: '2',
        title: 'Review GSTIN reconciliation mismatch',
        description: 'Invoice INV-2026-074 requires e-way bill re-validation',
        icon: <AlertTriangle className="size-4" />,
        tone: 'warning',
        action: {
          label: 'Review',
          variant: 'secondary',
          onClick: () => openReview('INV-2026-074'),
        },
      },
    ]}
  />
</WidgetCard>
```

### Empty state handling

When all pending tasks are resolved, `ActionList` automatically renders a clean empty state:

```tsx
<ActionList
  items={[]}
  emptyText="All pending approvals have been resolved."
/>
```

## Accessibility

`ActionList` renders semantic list structures with accessible action targets.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus sequentially between the action buttons across each task row.' },
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Activates the focused task action button.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- Rows render inside semantic `<ul>` and `<li>` elements.
- Each action button maintains distinct accessible context linking the button label with the task title.
- Empty states render with accessible text containers announced cleanly to screen readers.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Provide clear, imperative action labels like "Approve", "Review", or "Verify".',
    code: `<ActionListItem action={{ label: 'Approve' }} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not use vague labels like "Click here" or "Go".',
    code: `<ActionListItem action={{ label: 'Click' }} />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Pair ActionList with WidgetCard count to highlight the exact number of pending items.',
    code: `<WidgetCard count={items.length}><ActionList items={items} /></WidgetCard>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not hide task counts when operators rely on them to gauge urgency.',
    code: `<WidgetCard><ActionList items={items} /></WidgetCard>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['ActionList']} />

## Related

- [WidgetCard](/ui/docs/widgets/widget-card) — Standard container card for housing task lists.
- [ActivityFeed](/ui/docs/widgets/activity-feed) — Read-only chronological timeline of events.
- [Button](/ui/docs/components/actions/button) — Action button component used for row actions.

## Activity Feed (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/activity-feed)

Compact list and connected timeline views with relative timestamps, day groupings, and status tones.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/activity-feed/basic" align="start" className="p-4 sm:p-4" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  ActivityFeed,
  type ActivityItem,
  type ActivityFeedProps,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `ActivityFeed` to communicate operational history, audit trails, and collaborative milestones:

- **ERP record history**: Purchase order lifecycles (Draft → Approved → Dispatched → Invoiced).
- **Consignment tracking**: Shipments moving between distribution hubs.
- **System audit trails**: Documenting changes made to GST returns or tax configurations.

**Do not use ActivityFeed for:**
- Interactive task lists requiring immediate completion buttons — use [ActionList](/ui/docs/widgets/action-list).
- Standalone unread alerts — use [Notifications](/ui/docs/widgets/notifications).
- Multi-step sequential progress inputs — use [Stepper](/ui/docs/components/navigation/stepper).

## Examples

### Connected timeline with day grouping

Set `variant="timeline"` and `groupByDay={true}` to join items with a vertical connecting stem grouped under "Today", "Yesterday", and calendar dates:

```tsx
<ActivityFeed
  variant="timeline"
  groupByDay
  items={[
    {
      id: '1',
      title: 'Consignment DISP-2026-992 in transit',
      description: 'Dispatched via Blue Dart to Mumbai central warehouse.',
      time: new Date(Date.now() - 1000 * 60 * 18),
      icon: <Truck className="size-4" />,
      tone: 'primary',
    },
    {
      id: '2',
      title: 'Tax invoice approved',
      description: 'Priya Sharma verified ₹89,400 with GST e-invoicing.',
      time: new Date(Date.now() - 1000 * 60 * 120),
      icon: <CheckCircle2 className="size-4" />,
      tone: 'success',
    },
  ]}
/>
```

### Compact list variant

Use `variant="list"` inside narrow cards or sidebars:

```tsx
<ActivityFeed
  variant="list"
  items={activities}
/>
```

## Accessibility

`ActivityFeed` renders semantic ordered list elements.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus sequentially across interactive links or action buttons within feed items.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- Feed items render inside semantic `<ul>` lists with `role="list"`.
- Relative timestamps use semantic `<time dateTime="...">` tags containing ISO 8601 strings for assistive readers.
- Icons use decorative attributes, ensuring screen readers prioritize event titles and descriptions.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Provide proper ISO dates to the time prop so relative time formatting updates automatically.',
    code: `<ActivityItem time={new Date(event.timestamp)} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not pass unformatted ambiguous numbers or static strings to time.',
    code: `<ActivityItem time="3 hours" />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use the timeline variant for historical record audits and the list variant for compact dashboard widgets.',
    code: `<ActivityFeed variant="timeline" groupByDay />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not enable day grouping when feed items lack valid Date objects.',
    code: `<ActivityFeed groupByDay items={stringDateItems} />`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['ActivityFeed']} />

## Related

- [ChangeLog](/ui/docs/widgets/change-log) — Deep diff view built on top of ActivityFeed.
- [ActionList](/ui/docs/widgets/action-list) — Task-oriented list with actionable buttons.
- [WidgetCard](/ui/docs/widgets/widget-card) — Standard container card for housing activity feeds.

## App Switcher (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/app-switcher)

Popover launcher with grouped application sections, descriptions, status icons, and built-in search.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/app-switcher/basic" align="center" className="p-4 sm:p-4" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  AppSwitcher,
  type AppSwitcherProps,
  type AppSwitcherSection,
  type AppSwitcherApp,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `AppSwitcher` in the top application bar to enable direct transitions between major ERP business systems:

- **Ecosystem module navigation**: Jumping between Procurement, Warehousing, Invoicing, and Human Resources.
- **Multi-tenant portal switching**: Switching between Northwind Traders distribution entities.
- **Developer tools and settings**: Moving from core operational views to analytics consoles.

**Do not use AppSwitcher for:**
- Page-level sub-navigation within a single module — use [Sidebar](/ui/docs/components/layout/sidebar).
- Flat icon navigation rails — use [AppRail](/ui/docs/components/layout/app-rail).
- Standalone command execution — use [CommandPalette](/ui/docs/components/overlays/command-palette).

## Examples

### Grouped modules with search filter

Organising business modules under titled sections with built-in search:

```tsx
const sections: AppSwitcherSection[] = [
  {
    label: 'Supply chain & operations',
    apps: [
      {
        id: 'procurement',
        name: 'Procurement',
        description: 'Purchase orders, vendors, and RFQs',
        icon: <ShoppingCart className="size-5" />,
        tone: 'chart-1',
        href: '/procurement',
      },
      {
        id: 'inventory',
        name: 'Warehousing & inventory',
        description: 'Stock management, bins, and e-way bills',
        icon: <Package className="size-5" />,
        tone: 'chart-2',
        href: '/inventory',
      },
    ],
  },
  {
    label: 'Finance & compliance',
    apps: [
      {
        id: 'billing',
        name: 'Invoices & GST',
        description: 'Tax invoices, credit notes, and GSTR-1',
        icon: <FileText className="size-5" />,
        tone: 'chart-3',
        href: '/finance',
      },
    ],
  },
];

<AppSwitcher sections={sections} />
```

## Accessibility

`AppSwitcher` is built on Base UI Popover primitives (`@base-ui/react/popover`).

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Opens or closes the application switcher popover.' },
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus into the search input and across module application links.' },
    { key: 'Escape', action: 'Dismisses the open switcher popover and returns focus to the trigger button.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The trigger button receives `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded="true | false"`.
- Application tiles use semantic anchor links (`<a>`) with accessible titles and descriptions.
- The built-in search filter uses `role="searchbox"` to filter apps dynamically without losing keyboard focus.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Provide meaningful descriptions for each application so operators know which module to select.',
    code: `<AppSwitcherApp name="Procurement" description="Purchase orders and RFQs" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not overload sections with dozens of obscure sub-links (link to module homepages only).',
    code: `<AppSwitcherSection apps={fortySubpages} />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Place the AppSwitcher in TopBarStart alongside branding for instant wayfinding.',
    code: `<TopBarStart><AppSwitcher sections={sections} /></TopBarStart>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not bury the app switcher deep within in-page body content.',
    code: `<div className="mt-96"><AppSwitcher /></div>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['AppSwitcher']} />

## Related

- [TopBar](/ui/docs/components/layout/top-bar) — Global application top bar hosting AppSwitcher.
- [AppRail](/ui/docs/components/layout/app-rail) — Persistent vertical navigation rail for module switching.
- [CommandPalette](/ui/docs/components/overlays/command-palette) — Search overlay for jumping directly to deep records.

## Change Log (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/change-log)

Audit trail with field-level before and after values, notes, actor identities, and day grouping.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/change-log/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  ChangeLog,
  type ChangeLogEntry,
  type ChangeLogProps,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `ChangeLog` when providing immutable historical inspection of record modifications:

- **ERP record revision history**: Tracking revisions to purchase orders, contracts, and vendor profiles.
- **Statutory tax modifications**: Logging alterations to GSTIN registrations, PAN details, and bank mandates.
- **Security credential adjustments**: Showing permission modifications made to operator roles.

**Do not use ChangeLog for:**
- High-level event timelines without field-level diffs — use [ActivityFeed](/ui/docs/widgets/activity-feed).
- Pending authorization task queues — use [ActionList](/ui/docs/widgets/action-list).
- Ephemeral toast notifications — use [Toast](/ui/docs/components/feedback/toast).

## Examples

### Field-level diffs with day grouping

Mapping audit records to structured entries with `from` and `to` values:

```tsx
<ChangeLog
  groupByDay
  entries={[
    {
      id: '1',
      actor: 'Priya Sharma',
      action: 'updated purchase order terms',
      time: new Date(Date.now() - 1000 * 60 * 30),
      changes: [
        { field: 'Payment terms', from: 'Net 30', to: 'Net 60' },
        { field: 'Delivery depot', from: 'Koramangala Hub', to: 'Whitefield Central Depot' },
      ],
      note: 'Adjusted per vendor renegotiation meeting.',
    },
    {
      id: '2',
      actor: 'Ramesh Kumar',
      action: 'authorized discount rate',
      time: new Date(Date.now() - 1000 * 60 * 180),
      changes: [
        { field: 'Trade discount', from: '0%', to: '5%' },
      ],
    },
  ]}
/>
```

### Badges and custom diff elements

`from` and `to` accept arbitrary React nodes, enabling live status badge diffs:

```tsx
<ChangeLog
  entries={[
    {
      id: '3',
      actor: 'System Automation',
      action: 'reconciled e-way bill status',
      time: new Date(),
      changes: [
        {
          field: 'GST Status',
          from: <Badge variant="warning">Generated</Badge>,
          to: <Badge variant="success">Validated</Badge>,
        },
      ],
    },
  ]}
/>
```

## Accessibility

`ChangeLog` renders semantic description lists with accessible diff tags.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus sequentially between interactive links or user profile buttons in the log.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- Differences use semantic `<del>` (for previous values) and `<ins>` (for updated values).
- Visually hidden labels (`diffLabels`, customizable for localization) announce "from" and "to" explicitly to screen readers.
- Day headers group revisions cleanly under accessible regional landmarks.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Provide clear, contextual notes explaining why critical regulatory fields were updated.',
    code: `<ChangeLogEntry note="GST circular compliance update" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not omit previous values (from) when documenting audited business changes.',
    code: `<ChangeLogEntry changes={[{ field: 'Amount', from: undefined, to: '₹50,000' }]} />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use ActivityFeed when events do not involve discrete field diffs (e.g. "Consignment arrived").',
    code: `<ActivityFeed items={events} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not abuse ChangeLog for generic activity logs without before/after comparisons.',
    code: `<ChangeLog entries={eventsWithoutChanges} />`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['ChangeLog']} />

## Related

- [ActivityFeed](/ui/docs/widgets/activity-feed) — Chronological event stream primitive upon which ChangeLog is built.
- [Badge](/ui/docs/components/data-display/badge) — Status badge frequently rendered inside ChangeLog diffs.
- [WidgetCard](/ui/docs/widgets/widget-card) — Standard container card for housing audit history.
