## Entity List (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/entity-list)

High-density business entity rows with avatars, status metadata, and row actions.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/entity-list/basic" align="start" className="p-4 sm:p-4" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  EntityList,
  type EntityListItem,
  type EntityListProps,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `EntityList` to present curated collections of business records within dashboard cards or drawers:

- **Key vendor rankings**: Top suppliers by spend or pending invoice balance.
- **Customer account summaries**: Recent high-value corporate buyers.
- **Warehouse personnel rosters**: On-duty supervisors at regional depots.

**Do not use EntityList for:**
- Full-page searchable and sortable enterprise records — use [DataTable](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table).
- Pure task checklists with action buttons — use [ActionList](/ui/docs/widgets/action-list).
- Event audit feeds — use [ActivityFeed](/ui/docs/widgets/activity-feed).

## Examples

### Business vendor roster with status badges and actions

Presenting primary ERP suppliers with initials avatars, financial totals, and direct action triggers:

```tsx
<EntityList
  divided
  items={[
    {
      id: '1',
      title: 'Bengaluru Spices Pvt Ltd',
      subtitle: 'GSTIN: 29ABCDE1234F1Z5 · Koramangala Hub',
      initials: 'BS',
      tone: 'primary',
      meta: <span className="font-semibold">₹4,28,900</span>,
      action: (
        <Button size="sm" variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="View ledger">
          <ExternalLink className="size-4" />
        </Button>
      ),
    },
    {
      id: '2',
      title: 'Malabar Cardamom Producers',
      subtitle: 'GSTIN: 32AABCM5678K1Z2 · Kochi Depot',
      initials: 'MC',
      tone: 'success',
      meta: <span className="font-semibold">₹2,85,000</span>,
    },
  ]}
/>
```

### Compact density for sidebars

Set `density="sm"` when placing the list inside narrow navigation drawers or secondary panels:

```tsx
<EntityList
  density="sm"
  items={recentCustomers}
  onItemClick={(item) => navigateToCustomer(item.id)}
/>
```

## Accessibility

`EntityList` implements semantic list patterns with interactive row semantics.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus sequentially between interactive row buttons or links.' },
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Activates the focused entity row or row action button.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- Rows render inside semantic `<ul>` and `<li>` elements.
- When `onItemClick` is supplied, each item renders an accessible button element with full keyboard support.
- Action buttons inside rows maintain distinct accessible labels via `aria-label`.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Provide meaningful subtitles (such as GSTIN or depot location) to help operators distinguish similar vendor entities.',
    code: `<EntityListItem title="Acme India" subtitle="GSTIN: 27AABCA1234F1Z1" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not crowd entity rows with dozens of dense data columns (use DataTable for wide tabular data).',
    code: `<EntityListItem meta={<Table>{allFiftyFields}</Table>} />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use initials avatars with distinct tones (primary, success, neutral) to provide quick visual recognition.',
    code: `<EntityListItem initials="BS" tone="primary" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not leave avatars blank when customer profile photos are unavailable.',
    code: `<EntityListItem avatarSrc="" />`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['EntityList']} />

## Related

- [DataTable](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table) — Tabular enterprise data grid with sorting and pagination.
- [WidgetCard](/ui/docs/widgets/widget-card) — Standard container card for housing entity lists.
- [Avatar](/ui/docs/components/data-display/avatar) — Profile photo and initials indicator used inside EntityList.

## Widgets (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/index)

High-level business blocks combining primitives with built-in loading, empty, and error contracts.

import { CategoryGrid } from '@/components/docs/category-grid';

# Widgets

Widgets are domain-ready, composite business blocks designed for enterprise ERP applications at Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd. While primitive components (such as buttons, inputs, and dialogs) provide isolated UI elements, widgets assemble multiple primitives into complete functional modules with predictable asynchronous data contracts.

## Components

<CategoryGrid category="widgets" />

## Widgets versus components

Understanding when to reach for a primitive component versus a composed widget:

| Dimension | Primitive components | Composed widgets |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Scope** | Atomic building blocks (`Button`, `Input`, `Dialog`, `Badge`). | Domain-specific blocks (`MetricCard`, `KanbanBoard`, `ActivityFeed`). |
| **State management** | Local interactive UI state (open/closed, focus, active). | Async business data states (`loading`, `empty`, `error`, retry). |
| **Layout integration** | Sits inside forms, toolbars, and cards. | Forms entire dashboard cards, kanban boards, or navigation shells. |
| **Composition** | Extended via standard props and Tailwind classes. | Enclosed inside `WidgetCard` with consistent headers and actions. |

## The shared data contract

Every dashboard widget in `@innostes/ui` adheres to a shared three-state lifecycle:

1. **`loading`**: When asynchronous fetches are in flight, the widget displays skeleton placeholders matching the exact geometry of expected content, eliminating layout shifts.
2. **`empty`**: When a query resolves with zero matching records, the widget renders a clean, accessible empty state prompt rather than a broken or blank canvas.
3. **`error`**: When network requests or API authorizations fail, the widget displays a localized error indicator alongside an optional retry action (`onRetry`).

## Composing custom widgets with WidgetCard

`WidgetCard` provides the standardized outer shell for all widgets. Use it to compose custom ERP dashboard widgets that directly inherit the standard header, actions, count badges, and state handling:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
import { WidgetCard, Button } from '@innostes/ui';

export function WarehouseStockWidget({ warehouseId }: { warehouseId: string }) {
  const [data, setData] = useState<StockRecord[] | null>(null);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);

  const fetchStock = async () => {
    setLoading(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      const res = await fetch(`/api/warehouses/${warehouseId}/stock`);
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error('Failed to load stock data');
      const json = await res.json();
      setData(json);
    } catch (err: any) {
      setError(err.message);
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  };

  useEffect(() => {
    fetchStock();
  }, [warehouseId]);

  return (
    <WidgetCard
      title="Warehouse stock balance"
      description="Bengaluru Central Hub · Koramangala"
      count={data?.length}
      countTone="primary"
      loading={loading}
      loadingRows={4}
      error={error}
      onRetry={fetchStock}
      empty={data?.length === 0}
      emptyState="No inventory items allocated to this depot."
      viewAll={{ href: `/inventory/warehouses/${warehouseId}` }}
    >
      <div className="space-y-2">
        {data?.map((item) => (
          <div key={item.id} className="flex justify-between text-sm py-1 border-b">
            <span>{item.name}</span>
            <span className="font-semibold">{item.quantity} units</span>
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
    </WidgetCard>
  );
}
```

---

## Kanban Board (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/kanban-board)

Interactive multi-column board with optimistic drag-and-drop moves, WIP limits, touch support, and full keyboard navigation.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/kanban-board/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  KanbanBoard,
  moveKanbanItem,
  type KanbanColumn,
  type KanbanMove,
  type KanbanBoardProps,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `KanbanBoard` when managing visual work pipelines where records transition across discrete sequential stages:

- **Purchase order approvals**: Draft → Verification → Manager Review → Authorized.
- **Logistics consignment pipeline**: Booked → Packed → Dispatched → In Transit → Delivered.
- **Vendor KYC onboarding**: Applied → Documents Submitted → Bank Verification → Approved.

**Do not use KanbanBoard for:**
- Standard multi-column tabular data with sorting and filtering — use [DataTable](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table).
- Linear step-by-step form wizards — use [Stepper](/ui/docs/components/navigation/stepper).
- Flat chronological event streams — use [ActivityFeed](/ui/docs/widgets/activity-feed).

## Examples

### The move contract and optimistic updates

`onValueChange` fires when a card is dropped or moved via keyboard, providing the next column array and a `KanbanMove` descriptor:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { KanbanBoard, moveKanbanItem, type KanbanColumn, type KanbanMove, toast } from '@innostes/ui';

export function ProcurementPipeline({ initialColumns }: { initialColumns: KanbanColumn<Order>[] }) {
  const [columns, setColumns] = useState(initialColumns);

  const handleMove = async (nextColumns: KanbanColumn<Order>[], move: KanbanMove) => {
    // 1. Optimistically apply change to local state immediately
    const previousColumns = columns;
    setColumns(nextColumns);

    try {
      // 2. Persist to API
      const response = await fetch(`/api/orders/${move.itemId}/stage`, {
        method: 'PATCH',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          toStage: move.toColumnId,
          toIndex: move.toIndex,
        }),
      });

      if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Stage transition rejected by server');
      toast.success('Purchase order moved');
    } catch (err) {
      // 3. Rollback immediately on server failure
      setColumns(previousColumns);
      toast.error('Failed to update stage. Reverting position.');
    }
  };

  return (
    <KanbanBoard
      aria-label="Procurement pipeline"
      value={columns}
      onValueChange={handleMove}
      canMove={(move) => {
        // Enforce stage constraints: cannot jump directly from Draft to Authorized
        if (move.fromColumnId === 'draft' && move.toColumnId === 'authorized') {
          toast.warning('Draft orders must undergo verification before authorization.');
          return false;
        }
        return true;
      }}
      getItemLabel={(order) => `${order.id} · ${order.supplier}`}
      renderCard={(order) => <OrderCard order={order} />}
      onCardOpen={(order) => router.push(`/purchases/${order.id}`)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Column WIP limits

Set `limit={5}` on a column to enforce Work In Progress (WIP) bounds. The column header automatically renders a badge showing `count / limit` and turns warning/destructive when capacity is exceeded:

```tsx
const columns: KanbanColumn<Order>[] = [
  { id: 'review', title: 'Under review', limit: 4, items: reviewOrders },
  { id: 'dispatched', title: 'Dispatched', limit: 8, items: dispatchedOrders },
];
```

### Touch devices and mobile strategy

On mobile touch devices where native HTML drag-and-drop is limited, `KanbanBoard` provides a built-in touch column selector, allowing users to tap a card and pick its destination column directly from a native select control, or trigger `onCardOpen` to update the stage from an inspection drawer.

## Accessibility

`KanbanBoard` provides complete non-pointer keyboard operation and screen reader announcements.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus into the board and between cards and column action controls.' },
    { key: 'ArrowDown / ArrowUp', action: 'Moves keyboard focus to the next or previous card in the current column.' },
    { key: 'ArrowRight / ArrowLeft', action: 'Moves keyboard focus to the adjacent column at the same relative height.' },
    { key: 'Space', action: 'Picks up the focused card to begin a keyboard move.' },
    { key: 'Arrow keys (while holding)', action: 'Repositions the held card within or across columns.' },
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Drops the held card into its new position and announces the move.' },
    { key: 'Escape', action: 'Cancels the active keyboard move and returns the card to its original position.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- Columns render as semantic `<section>` regions with `aria-labelledby` referencing column titles.
- Cards maintain `role="button"` or `role="article"` with clear `aria-roledescription="Draggable card"`.
- Live region announcements notify screen readers when a card is grabbed, moved, dropped, or blocked by `canMove`.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Enforce optimistic rollbacks with try/catch to maintain data integrity when network calls fail.',
    code: `try { setColumns(next); await api.save(); } catch { setColumns(prev); }`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not update server data without reverting UI state if the backend rejects the stage transition.',
    code: `setColumns(next); api.save(); // Ignored error leaves UI out of sync`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use canMove to validate business logic before allowing invalid state jumps.',
    code: `canMove={(m) => !(m.fromColumnId === 'draft' && m.toColumnId === 'paid')}`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not allow arbitrary transitions that violate regulatory ERP stage gates.',
    code: `canMove={() => true}`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['KanbanBoard']} />

- [Stepper](/ui/docs/components/navigation/stepper) — Multi-step sequential progression wizard.

## Metric Card (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/metric-card)

High-density business metric cards with delta indicators, comparison baselines, sparklines, and progress bars.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/metric-card/variants" align="start" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  MetricCard,
  MetricGrid,
  MetricDelta,
  type MetricCardProps,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `MetricCard` to display primary Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) across executive and operational dashboards:

- **Executive overview**: Total revenue, gross margin, accounts receivable, and net profit.
- **Logistics operations**: On-time dispatches, warehouse capacity, and fleet turnaround.
- **Procurement metrics**: Open purchase order spend, vendor fulfilment rate, and average lead time.

**Do not use MetricCard for:**
- Long tabular data rows — use [DataTable](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table).
- Multi-step interactive wizards — use [Stepper](/ui/docs/components/navigation/stepper).
- Detailed multi-dimensional data charts — use [CartesianChart](/ui/docs/charts/cartesian).

## Examples

### Seven design variants

Select from seven specialized variants to match the density and focus of each dashboard row:

| Variant | Best for |
| :--- | :--- |
| `default` | Standard KPI with icon, primary value, delta badge, and comparison period. |
| `compact` | High-density grids, sidebars, or auxiliary operational cards. |
| `accent` | Highlighting the single most vital metric on the page. |
| `sparkline` | Emphasizing trajectory over time rather than a single static number. |
| `progress` | Tracking achievement toward an explicit quota or quarterly target. |
| `comparison` | Side-by-side contrast between current period and historical benchmark. |
| `split` | Decomposing a total into segmented parts (e.g. order status distribution). |

### Deltas, trends, and Indian fiscal formatting

Format numeric deltas as fractional values (e.g. `0.125` formats as `+12.5%`) and format rupee values in `en-IN`:

```tsx
<MetricGrid columns={3}>
  <MetricCard
    label="Monthly procurement"
    value="₹48,25,000"
    delta={0.142}
    comparison="vs last month"
  />
  <MetricCard
    label="Average lead time"
    value="3.2 days"
    delta={-0.18}
    upIsGood={false}
    comparison="vs target"
  />
  <MetricCard
    variant="sparkline"
    label="Daily order volume"
    value="142 orders"
    sparklineData={[110, 118, 125, 130, 138, 142]}
  />
</MetricGrid>
```

### Progress toward quarterly quota

Track goal completion percentages with `variant="progress"`:

```tsx
<MetricCard
  variant="progress"
  label="FY 2026 Q3 dispatch target"
  value="₹1.84 Cr"
  progress={82}
  comparison="Target: ₹2.25 Cr"
/>
```

### Loading and empty states

Metric cards reflect loading and zero-value states consistently:

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/metric-card/states" />

## Accessibility

`MetricCard` formats values and delta directions with accessible announcements.

### Keyboard navigation

Metric cards render as readable informational blocks. When rendered with an `href` or interactive action, cards receive standard keyboard focus with Enter/Space triggers.

### ARIA attributes

- Directional delta arrows announce their trajectory ("Up", "Down") explicitly to screen readers so meaning is not conveyed by colour alone.
- Progress bars inside `variant="progress"` use semantic `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin="0"`, and `aria-valuemax="100"`.
- Cards render within semantic `<section>` or `<article>` landmarks.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Set `upIsGood={false}` for metrics where an increase is undesirable (e.g. return rate, late dispatches).',
    code: `<MetricCard label="Late dispatches" delta={0.15} upIsGood={false} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not leave upIsGood true when an increase signifies a defect or operational failure.',
    code: `<MetricCard label="Late dispatches" delta={0.15} />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Maintain uniform variants across a single horizontal MetricGrid row for balanced visual alignment.',
    code: `<MetricGrid columns={3}><MetricCard variant="default" /><MetricCard variant="default" /><MetricCard variant="default" /></MetricGrid>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not randomly mix different variants with uneven card heights in the same horizontal row.',
    code: `<MetricGrid><MetricCard variant="split" /><MetricCard variant="compact" /></MetricGrid>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['MetricCard', 'MetricGrid', 'MetricDelta']} />

- [Sparkline](/ui/docs/widgets/sparkline) — Lightweight SVG trendline component used inside MetricCard.
- [WidgetCard](/ui/docs/widgets/widget-card) — Standard container card for housing dashboard metrics.
- [Stat](/ui/docs/components/data-display/stat) — Atomic numerical statistic display tile.

## Notifications (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/notifications)

Popover notification trigger with unread badge counter, relative timestamps, and standalone list component.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/notification-bell/basic" align="center" className="p-4 sm:p-4" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  NotificationBell,
  NotificationList,
  type NotificationItem,
  type NotificationBellProps,
  type NotificationListProps,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `NotificationBell` and `NotificationList` to keep operators informed of high-priority system events without disrupting their active workflow:

- **Top navigation bar alerts**: Persistent notification badge with dropdown menu in [TopBar](/ui/docs/components/layout/top-bar).
- **Dedicated notifications center**: Full-page notifications feed using `NotificationList`.
- **Dashboard alert widgets**: Embedding `NotificationList` inside [WidgetCard](/ui/docs/widgets/widget-card).

**Do not use NotificationBell for:**
- Immediate transient feedback to direct user actions — use [Toast](/ui/docs/components/feedback/toast).
- Persistent in-page warning messages — use [Alert](/ui/docs/components/feedback/alert).
- High-stakes modal confirmations — use [AlertDialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/alert-dialog).

## Examples

### Top navigation bell popover

The standard top-bar bell with unread badge counter and action callbacks:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { NotificationBell, type NotificationItem, toast } from '@innostes/ui';
import { FileText, Truck, AlertTriangle } from 'lucide-react';

export function NavigationNotifications() {
  const [items, setItems] = useState<NotificationItem[]>([
    {
      id: '1',
      title: 'Tax invoice approved',
      description: 'Priya Sharma verified INV-2026-081 for ₹89,400',
      time: new Date(Date.now() - 1000 * 60 * 15),
      icon: <FileText className="size-4" />,
      tone: 'success',
      read: false,
    },
    {
      id: '2',
      title: 'Consignment DISP-2026-992 in transit',
      description: 'E-way bill Ka-01-AB-1234 validated',
      time: new Date(Date.now() - 1000 * 60 * 60 * 2),
      icon: <Truck className="size-4" />,
      tone: 'primary',
      read: false,
    },
  ]);

  const markAllRead = () => {
    setItems((prev) => prev.map((item) => ({ ...item, read: true })));
    toast.success('Marked all notifications as read');
  };

  return (
    <NotificationBell
      items={items}
      onMarkAllRead={markAllRead}
      viewAll={{ label: 'View all notifications', href: '/notifications' }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Standalone NotificationList inside WidgetCard

Embed the raw notification list inside a dashboard card or dedicated full-page audit view:

```tsx
<WidgetCard title="System alerts" count={unreadCount} countTone="destructive">
  <NotificationList
    items={notifications}
    onItemClick={(item) => navigateToRecord(item.id)}
  />
</WidgetCard>
```

## Accessibility

`NotificationBell` is built on Base UI Popover primitives (`@base-ui/react/popover`).

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Opens or closes the notification popover from the bell trigger.' },
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus into the notification list and across action links.' },
    { key: 'Escape', action: 'Dismisses the open popover and restores focus to the bell button.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The trigger button has `aria-label="Notifications, N unread"` (or `aria-label="Notifications"` when all caught up).
- When opened, `aria-expanded="true"` announces the open popover surface.
- Unread status dots include hidden `<span className="sr-only">Unread</span>` elements so screen reader operators are immediately informed of unread state.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Provide an onMarkAllRead handler so operators can quickly clear notification queues.',
    code: `<NotificationBell items={items} onMarkAllRead={handleMarkAll} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not omit action links when operators have dozens of queued notifications.',
    code: `<NotificationBell items={fiftyItems} />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use clear, specific tones (primary, success, warning, destructive) to visually distinguish alert categories.',
    code: `<NotificationItem tone="warning" title="TDS mismatch" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not render all notifications with identical icons and colours.',
    code: `<NotificationItem tone="neutral" />`,
  }}
/>

<ApiTable components={['NotificationBell', 'NotificationList']} />

## Permission Matrix (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/permission-matrix)

Interactive permission grid with module grouping, row and column bulk toggles, read-only roles, and sticky headers.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/permission-matrix/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  PermissionMatrix,
  permissionKey,
  type PermissionMatrixAction,
  type PermissionMatrixResource,
  type PermissionMatrixProps,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `PermissionMatrix` for Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) administration in enterprise ERP setups:

- **Role authorization configurations**: Assigning Create, Read, Update, Delete, and Approve rights to operator roles.
- **Auditing system privileges**: Inspecting immutable read-only permissions on default admin profiles.
- **Tenant permissions**: Multi-tenant access controls across finance, logistics, and inventory modules.

**Do not use PermissionMatrix for:**
- Single-permission toggles on user profiles — use [Switch](/ui/docs/components/forms/switch).
- Flat lists of checkboxes — use [CheckboxGroup](/ui/docs/components/forms/checkbox).
- Data records with varying row heights — use [DataTable](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table).

## Examples

### Value format and API persistence

The value format is a flat array of `"resource:action"` strings. Use `permissionKey(resource, action)` to construct or parse keys safely:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { PermissionMatrix, permissionKey, toast } from '@innostes/ui';

export function RolePermissionsManager({ roleId, initialPermissions }: { roleId: string; initialPermissions: string[] }) {
  const [permissions, setPermissions] = useState<string[]>(initialPermissions);
  const [saving, setSaving] = useState(false);

  const handleSave = async (updated: string[]) => {
    setPermissions(updated);
    setSaving(true);
    try {
      const res = await fetch(`/api/roles/${roleId}/permissions`, {
        method: 'PUT',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({ permissions: updated }),
      });
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error('Failed to update permissions');
      toast.success('Role permissions updated successfully');
    } catch (err) {
      toast.error('Failed to persist permissions to backend');
    } finally {
      setSaving(false);
    }
  };

  return (
    <PermissionMatrix
      aria-label="Procurement Officer Permissions"
      actions={[
        { id: 'view', label: 'View' },
        { id: 'create', label: 'Create' },
        { id: 'edit', label: 'Edit' },
        { id: 'approve', label: 'Approve' },
      ]}
      resources={[
        { id: 'purchase_orders', label: 'Purchase orders', group: 'Procurement' },
        { id: 'vendor_profiles', label: 'Vendor profiles', group: 'Procurement' },
        { id: 'tax_invoices', label: 'Tax invoices', group: 'Finance & GST', actions: ['view', 'approve'] },
        { id: 'e_way_bills', label: 'E-Way bills', group: 'Logistics', actions: ['view', 'create'] },
      ]}
      value={permissions}
      onValueChange={handleSave}
    />
  );
}
```

### Read-only system roles

System-defined roles (like `Super Administrator` or `Auditor`) should not be editable. Pass `readOnly={true}` to lock all checkboxes and suppress bulk row/column toggles:

```tsx
<PermissionMatrix
  readOnly
  aria-label="Statutory Auditor (Read-only)"
  actions={actions}
  resources={resources}
  value={auditorPermissions}
/>
```

### Large matrices and sticky scrolling

For large ERP suites with 50+ resources and 8+ actions, wrap `PermissionMatrix` inside a scrollable container with a fixed height. The component headers and resource label columns are styled with CSS sticky positioning, ensuring row and column labels remain pinned in place as operators scroll.

## Accessibility

`PermissionMatrix` renders a semantic HTML `<table>` with complete row and column header associations.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus sequentially between interactive checkboxes across the grid.' },
    { key: 'Space', action: 'Toggles the focused permission checkbox on or off.' },
    { key: 'Arrow keys', action: 'Navigates focus between adjacent grid cells.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The container renders as a `<table>` with `role="table"`.
- Each checkbox is labelled with both its resource and action via `aria-label` (e.g. `aria-label="Approve Tax invoices"`).
- Row and column bulk checkboxes receive `aria-checked="mixed"` when only a partial subset of permissions is selected.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Group related resources logically by module (Procurement, Finance, Warehousing) to simplify scanning.',
    code: `<Resource label="Purchase orders" group="Procurement" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not dump dozens of ungrouped resources into an arbitrary alphabetical list.',
    code: `<Resource label="Purchase orders" group={undefined} />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use readOnly for system roles that must not be altered by tenant administrators.',
    code: `<PermissionMatrix readOnly value={immutableSystemPermissions} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not leave checkboxes active for roles that will reject updates upon saving.',
    code: `<PermissionMatrix value={systemPermissions} onValueChange={noOp} />`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['PermissionMatrix']} />

- [DataTable](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table) — Interactive table component for tabular record listings.
- [Checkbox](/ui/docs/components/forms/checkbox) — Checkbox component used inside matrix cells.
- [WidgetCard](/ui/docs/widgets/widget-card) — Standard container card for housing administrative tools.

## Quick Actions (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/quick-actions)

Shortcut launcher cards for high-frequency tasks such as creating orders, invoices, or dispatch notes.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/quick-actions/basic" align="start" className="p-4 sm:p-4" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  QuickActions,
  type QuickAction,
  type QuickActionsProps,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `QuickActions` on administrative dashboards to provide instant one-click access to repetitive enterprise tasks:

- **ERP procurement launchers**: "Create Purchase Order", "Issue Tax Invoice", "Log Consignment".
- **Inventory shortcuts**: "Stock Transfer", "Physical Count Audit", "Reorder Low Stock".
- **HRMS actions**: "Record Attendance", "Apply Leave", "Initiate Payroll".

**Do not use QuickActions for:**
- Global application search — use [CommandPalette](/ui/docs/components/overlays/command-palette).
- Table row action menus — use [DropdownMenu](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu).
- Linear step-by-step wizard progress — use [Stepper](/ui/docs/components/navigation/stepper).

## Examples

### Row layout for dashboard cards

Displaying shortcuts horizontally with descriptions alongside icons:

```tsx
<QuickActions
  layout="row"
  items={[
    {
      id: 'po',
      label: 'Create purchase order',
      description: 'Procure goods from registered vendors',
      icon: <ShoppingCart className="size-5" />,
      tone: 'primary',
      onClick: () => router.push('/purchases/new'),
    },
    {
      id: 'inv',
      label: 'Issue tax invoice',
      description: 'GST-compliant B2B e-invoice with IRN',
      icon: <FileText className="size-5" />,
      tone: 'success',
      onClick: () => router.push('/invoices/new'),
    },
  ]}
/>
```

### Tile layout for top-level launchers

Use `layout="tile"` (default) for grid arrangements where icons sit directly above titles:

```tsx
<QuickActions
  layout="tile"
  minItemWidth="8rem"
  items={shortcuts}
/>
```

## Accessibility

`QuickActions` renders accessible navigation triggers.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus sequentially between shortcut tiles.' },
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Activates the focused action tile.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- Shortcuts render inside semantic `<ul>` and `<li>` elements.
- When an item provides an `href` or `render` prop, it renders an accessible `<a>` tag; when it provides `onClick`, it renders an accessible `<button>` tag.
- Disabled shortcuts receive `aria-disabled="true"`.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Provide short descriptions when using the row layout to explain what each shortcut accomplishes.',
    code: `<QuickAction layout="row" label="Issue invoice" description="GST B2B e-invoice" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not overload dashboards with more than 6–8 shortcuts in a single card.',
    code: `<QuickActions items={twentyFourActions} />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use the render prop with framework router links for smooth client-side page transitions.',
    code: `<QuickAction render={<Link href="/purchases/new" />} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not trigger hard full-page browser reloads for internal application links.',
    code: `<QuickAction onClick={() => { window.location.href = '/purchases/new'; }} />`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['QuickActions']} />

## Related

- [CommandPalette](/ui/docs/components/overlays/command-palette) — Modal keyboard palette for searching commands globally.
- [WidgetCard](/ui/docs/widgets/widget-card) — Standard container card for housing quick action groups.
- [AppSwitcher](/ui/docs/widgets/app-switcher) — High-level enterprise module launcher.

## Sparkline (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/sparkline)

Zero-dependency SVG trendline rendering clean fills and strokes without external chart libraries.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/sparkline/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Sparkline,
  type SparklineProps,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Sparkline` to display immediate trajectory context in compact environments where full chart axes would overwhelm the layout:

- **Data table cells**: Showing 7-day sales trends alongside inventory rows.
- **KPI cards**: Showing monthly cash flow trajectory in [MetricCard](/ui/docs/widgets/metric-card).
- **Stat summary tiles**: Visualizing delivery performance or return rates.

**Do not use Sparkline for:**
- Interactive data analysis requiring hover tooltips, axis labels, or multiple series — use [CartesianChart](/ui/docs/charts/cartesian).
- Part-to-whole categorical breakdowns — use [DonutChart](/ui/docs/charts/donut).
- Progress completion toward a fixed target — use [Progress](/ui/docs/components/feedback/progress).

## Examples

### Trendline with gradient area fill

Displaying 7-day revenue trend with accessible status tones:

```tsx
<Sparkline
  data={[42000, 48000, 45000, 52000, 61000, 58000, 69000]}
  tone="success"
  label="7-day revenue trajectory, rising"
  height={40}
/>
```

### Table cell line-only variant

Set `area={false}` to draw a minimal stroke-only line without gradient shading:

```tsx
<Sparkline
  data={[12, 18, 15, 22, 28]}
  area={false}
  height={24}
  className="w-24"
/>
```

## Accessibility

`Sparkline` generates accessible SVG elements with screen reader labels.

### Keyboard navigation

Sparklines are non-interactive graphical representations. Keyboard focus naturally moves past them unless wrapped in an interactive element.

### ARIA attributes

- When the `label` prop is provided, the SVG renders `role="img"` with `aria-label={label}`.
- If `label` is omitted, the SVG renders `aria-hidden="true"` so decorative sparklines do not distract screen reader operators when the trend metric is already articulated in text.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Always provide an explicit label (e.g. "Revenue, last 7 days, rising") when the sparkline conveys standalone trend meaning.',
    code: `<Sparkline label="7-day revenue, rising" data={data} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not rely on the sparkline visual alone to communicate critical business decreases without text or accessible labels.',
    code: `<Sparkline data={[100, 20]} />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use `area={false}` in tight table cells to preserve clean visual vertical rhythm.',
    code: `<Sparkline area={false} height={20} className="w-20" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not force large 100px area fills into compact 36px table row cells.',
    code: `<Sparkline height={100} area />`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Sparkline']} />

## Related

- [MetricCard](/ui/docs/widgets/metric-card) — KPI card featuring built-in sparkline support.
- [CartesianChart](/ui/docs/charts/cartesian) — Full-featured chart component with tooltips and axes.
- [Stat](/ui/docs/components/data-display/stat) — Statistical display tile paired with trend indicators.

## User Menu (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/user-menu)

User profile button that opens a dropdown menu with avatar fallbacks, status subtitles, and account actions.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/user-menu/basic" align="center" className="p-4 sm:p-4" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  UserMenu,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuSeparator,
  type UserMenuProps,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `UserMenu` in primary navigation headers or sidebar footers to provide operator account management and session termination:

- **Top navigation bar end slot**: Quick access to personal settings, company switcher, and sign out in [TopBar](/ui/docs/components/layout/top-bar).
- **Sidebar footer**: Grounding the desktop application layout in [Sidebar](/ui/docs/components/layout/sidebar).
- **Branch switching**: Switching active warehouse division or operational role.

**Do not use UserMenu for:**
- Static non-interactive team rosters — use [AvatarGroup](/ui/docs/components/data-display/avatar) or [EntityList](/ui/docs/widgets/entity-list).
- Standalone button menus without user profile metadata — use [DropdownMenu](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu).
- In-form user selection — use [Select](/ui/docs/components/forms/select).

## Examples

### Basic usage with avatar fallback and menu items

If `avatarSrc` is omitted, `UserMenu` automatically derives initials from the `name` prop:

```tsx
<UserMenu
  name="Priya Sharma"
  subtitle="Northwind Traders · Bengaluru Hub"
  email="priya.sharma@northwind.in"
  avatarSrc="/avatars/priya.jpg"
>
  <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => router.push('/settings/profile')}>
    Profile & preferences
  </DropdownMenuItem>
  <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => router.push('/settings/security')}>
    Security & 2FA
  </DropdownMenuItem>
  <DropdownMenuSeparator />
  <DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={handleSignOut}>
    Sign out
  </DropdownMenuItem>
</UserMenu>
```

### In sidebar footer

Placing `UserMenu` at the bottom of the application sidebar:

```tsx
<SidebarFooter>
  <UserMenu
    name="Ramesh Kumar"
    subtitle="Logistics Manager"
    email="ramesh.k@northwind.in"
  >
    <DropdownMenuItem>Switch depot</DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuSeparator />
    <DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive">Sign out</DropdownMenuItem>
  </UserMenu>
</SidebarFooter>
```

## Accessibility

`UserMenu` is built on Base UI Menu primitives (`@base-ui/react/menu`).

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Enter / Space / DownArrow', action: 'Opens the user account menu and focuses the first item.' },
    { key: 'DownArrow / UpArrow', action: 'Cycles focus between account menu items.' },
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Activates the focused menu item and dismisses the menu.' },
    { key: 'Escape', action: 'Dismisses the menu and restores focus to the user menu trigger button.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The trigger button receives `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded="true | false"`, and an accessible name incorporating the user's name.
- The dropdown container has `role="menu"`.
- Action items have `role="menuitem"`.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Always use variant="destructive" on the Sign out action item.',
    code: `<DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={signOut}>Sign out</DropdownMenuItem>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not style the destructive sign-out action as a regular harmless menu option.',
    code: `<DropdownMenuItem onClick={signOut}>Sign out</DropdownMenuItem>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Provide an email or subtitle to help operators verify their active organizational tenant and login identity.',
    code: `<UserMenu name="Priya Sharma" subtitle="Northwind Traders (Karnataka)" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not render completely blank user buttons with no accessible name.',
    code: `<UserMenu name="" />`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['UserMenu']} />

## Related

- [TopBar](/ui/docs/components/layout/top-bar) — Global application top bar hosting UserMenu.
- [Sidebar](/ui/docs/components/layout/sidebar) — Application sidebar hosting UserMenu in SidebarFooter.
- [DropdownMenu](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu) — Underlying dropdown menu primitive.

## Welcome Banner (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/welcome-banner)

Top-of-dashboard greeting card with container-query responsiveness, background variants, and quick action buttons.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/welcome-banner/basic" align="start" className="p-4 sm:p-4" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  WelcomeBanner,
  type WelcomeBannerProps,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `WelcomeBanner` as the welcoming centerpiece at the top of high-level role dashboards:

- **Department hubs**: Greeting procurement managers, warehouse leads, or finance officers.
- **Onboarding dashboards**: Welcoming newly joined staff with links to initial setup tasks.
- **Executive summaries**: Presenting high-level fiscal dates alongside organizational mottos.

**Do not use WelcomeBanner for:**
- Entity record detail pages (like a specific purchase order or invoice) — use [PageHeader](/ui/docs/components/layout/page-header).
- Compact KPI metric displays — use [MetricCard](/ui/docs/widgets/metric-card).
- In-form instructional callouts — use [Alert](/ui/docs/components/feedback/alert).

## Examples

### Gradient variant with action buttons and inspirational quote

The standard administrative dashboard greeting:

```tsx
<WelcomeBanner
  eyebrow="Fiscal Year 2026-27 · Bengaluru Division"
  title="Welcome back, Priya Sharma"
  description="You have 3 purchase orders pending approval and 1 GST filing discrepancy to resolve."
  variant="gradient"
  quote="Integrity in procurement delivers resilience in supply."
  actions={
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
      <Button size="sm">Create PO</Button>
      <Button size="sm" variant="outline">Export tax report</Button>
    </div>
  }
/>
```

### Brand and plain variants

- `variant="gradient"` (default): Uses a gentle wash of the primary theme tint.
- `variant="brand"`: Solid primary background with light text for high-contrast executive portals.
- `variant="plain"`: Clean card surface with standard border.

```tsx
<WelcomeBanner
  variant="brand"
  title="Supply Chain Operations"
  description="Northwind Traders Bengaluru Central Depot"
/>
```

## Accessibility

`WelcomeBanner` renders semantic section landmarks.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus sequentially between interactive action buttons inside the banner.' },
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Triggers the focused action button.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The container renders as a `<section data-slot="welcome-banner">`.
- Heading titles render with semantic hierarchy appropriate for top-of-page introductions.
- Decorative illustrations render with `aria-hidden="true"`.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Keep the description concise (1–2 sentences) highlighting actionable summary numbers.',
    code: `<WelcomeBanner description="3 purchase orders awaiting your approval today." />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not overload the banner with multi-paragraph operational documentation.',
    code: `<WelcomeBanner description="Paragraph 1... Paragraph 2... Paragraph 3..." />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Include 1–3 primary action buttons that directly resolve common daily tasks.',
    code: `<WelcomeBanner actions={<Button>Create PO</Button>} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not embed complex multi-field input forms inside the welcome banner.',
    code: `<WelcomeBanner actions={<Form>{twentyFields}</Form>} />`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['WelcomeBanner']} />

## Related

- [PageHeader](/ui/docs/components/layout/page-header) — Administrative page header for record views.
- [MetricCard](/ui/docs/widgets/metric-card) — KPI metric cards placed directly beneath welcome banners.
- [QuickActions](/ui/docs/widgets/quick-actions) — Grid of task shortcuts.

## Widget Card (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/widget-card)

Standardized dashboard card frame with headers, count badges, actions, view-all links, and built-in loading, empty, and error states.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/widget-card/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  WidgetCard,
  type WidgetCardProps,
  type WidgetCardViewAll,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `WidgetCard` as the outer container for every component or visualization placed on an administrative dashboard:

- **Asynchronous data widgets**: Housing lists, charts, and metrics fetching from backend APIs.
- **Task queues and alerts**: Presenting pending approval lists with real-time count badges.
- **Embedded tabular summaries**: Presenting top vendors or recent invoices.

**Do not use WidgetCard for:**
- Standard static article cards — use [Card](/ui/docs/components/data-display/card).
- In-form field groups — use [FormSection](/ui/docs/components/layout/form-layout).
- Slide-over inspection drawers — use [Sheet](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet).

## Examples

### Complete async lifecycle states

Wrap any content to provide consistent loading, error with retry, and empty state handling:

```tsx
'use client';

import { WidgetCard, ActionList, PeriodSelect } from '@innostes/ui';

export function PendingApprovalsWidget() {
  const { data, isLoading, error, refetch } = usePendingApprovals();

  return (
    <WidgetCard
      title="Pending authorizations"
      description="Purchase orders and credit notes awaiting review"
      count={data?.length}
      countTone="primary"
      viewAll={{ href: '/approvals', label: 'View all authorizations' }}
      actions={<PeriodSelect />}
      loading={isLoading}
      loadingRows={4}
      error={error ? 'Unable to load pending approvals from server.' : undefined}
      onRetry={refetch}
      empty={data?.length === 0}
      emptyState="All procurement authorizations have been cleared."
    >
      <ActionList items={data ?? []} divided />
    </WidgetCard>
  );
}
```

### Full-bleed content with padding="none"

Set `padding="none"` when embedding tables, charts, or maps so their edges align cleanly with the card boundaries:

```tsx
<WidgetCard
  title="Recent consignments"
  padding="none"
  viewAll={{ href: '/logistics/consignments' }}
>
  <Table>{/* Full-bleed table */}</Table>
</WidgetCard>
```

## Accessibility

`WidgetCard` renders semantic HTML5 `<section>` landmarks.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus into the card, cycling through header actions, view-all links, and body controls.' },
  ]}
/>

### ARIA attributes

- The container renders as a `<section>` labelled by its heading via `aria-labelledby`, allowing screen reader operators to jump between dashboard widgets using standard landmark shortcuts.
- Loading states use `aria-busy="true"` and accessible skeleton elements.
- Error states render with `role="alert"` so network failures are announced promptly.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Provide an onRetry callback when passing an error to give operators a direct way to recover.',
    code: `<WidgetCard error={error} onRetry={refetch} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not render raw error traces or leave users stranded on failed data queries without a retry button.',
    code: `<WidgetCard error={String(err.stack)} />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use padding="none" for tables and charts to let data grids reach the card perimeter.',
    code: `<WidgetCard padding="none"><DataTable /></WidgetCard>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not introduce double padding by combining standard card padding with padded tables.',
    code: `<WidgetCard padding="default"><div className="p-6"><DataTable /></div></WidgetCard>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['WidgetCard']} />

## Related

- [Card](/ui/docs/components/data-display/card) — General-purpose card container primitive.
- [Skeleton](/ui/docs/components/feedback/skeleton) — Placeholder primitive used during WidgetCard loading states.
- [EmptyState](/ui/docs/components/data-display/empty-state) — Empty state primitive used inside WidgetCard.
